title: 羅密歐與茱麗葉
author: William Shakespeare 威廉·莎士比亞
description: 《Romeo and Juliet》(約1595)。維洛那兩大世仇家族嘅子女羅密歐同茱麗葉一見鍾情、秘密成婚,卻因家族仇恨同命運嘅捉弄,雙雙殉情,亦終令兩家和解。全劇五幕二十六段(連兩段序詩),每段對白標示說話者,英文原文對照廣東話/普通話翻譯。

chapters.title: Prologue 序詩

passages.original: Enter Chorus.
passages.vernacular: [序詩者上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [序詩者上。]

passages.title: Chorus 序詩者
passages.original: Two households, both alike in dignity, In fair Verona, where we lay our scene, From ancient grudge break to new mutiny, Where civil blood makes civil hands unclean.
passages.vernacular: 兩個家族,同樣尊貴,喺美麗嘅維洛嗰,我哋喺此設定場景,因古老嘅怨恨爆發新嘅暴亂,公民嘅血使公民嘅手不潔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個家族,同樣尊貴,在美麗的維洛那,我們在此設定場景,因古老的怨恨爆發新的暴亂,公民的血使公民的手不潔。

passages.original: From forth the fatal loins of these two foes A pair of star-cross’d lovers take their life;
passages.vernacular: 從呢兩個仇敵命定嘅腰間,一對命運不佳嘅戀人誕生;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從這兩個仇敵命定的腰間,一對命運不佳的戀人誕生;

passages.original: Whose misadventur’d piteous overthrows Doth with their death bury their parents’ strife.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不幸而可憐嘅覆亡,以死亡埋葬咗父母嘅爭執。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不幸而可憐的覆亡,以死亡埋葬了父母的爭執。

passages.original: The fearful passage of their death-mark’d love, And the continuance of their parents’ rage, Which, but their children’s end, nought could remove, Is now the two hours’ traffic of our stage;
passages.vernacular: 佢哋死亡註定嘅愛情嘅可怕歷程,同父母持續嘅憤怒,除咗子女嘅結局,乜嘢都無法消除,而家成為我哋舞台兩小時嘅演出;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們死亡註定的愛情的可怕歷程,和父母持續的憤怒,除了子女的結局,什麼也無法消除,現在成為我們舞台兩小時的演出;

passages.original: The which, if you with patient ears attend, What here shall miss, our toil shall strive to mend.
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋耐心傾聽,呢度有所欠缺嘅,我哋嘅辛勞將努力彌補。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們耐心傾聽,這裡有所欠缺的,我們的辛勞將努力彌補。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene I — A Public Place 第一幕第一場:公共場所

passages.original: Enter Sampson and Gregory armed with swords and bucklers.
passages.vernacular: [參森同格列高里佩劍帶盾上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [參森和格列高里佩劍帶盾上。]

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: Gregory, on my word, we’ll not carry coals.
passages.vernacular: 格列高里,我講真嘅,我哋可不扛煤(受氣)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 格列高里,我說真的,我們可不扛煤(受氣)。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: No, for then we should be colliers.
passages.vernacular: 不,因為嗰樣我哋就成咗煤工。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,因為那樣我們就成了煤工。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: I mean, if we be in choler, we’ll draw.
passages.vernacular: 我係講,如果我哋發怒,我哋就拔劍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是說,如果我們發怒,我們就拔劍。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: Ay, while you live, draw your neck out o’ the collar.
passages.vernacular: 對,只要你活住,就把你嘅脖子從絞索裡抽出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,只要你活著,就把你的脖子從絞索裡抽出來。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: I strike quickly, being moved.
passages.vernacular: 我一被激動就快速出手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一被激動就快速出手。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: But thou art not quickly moved to strike.
passages.vernacular: 不過你唔容易被激動出手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是你不容易被激動出手。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: A dog of the house of Montague moves me.
passages.vernacular: 蒙太古家嘅一條狗就能激動我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒙太古家的一條狗就能激動我。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: To move is to stir; and to be valiant is to stand:
passages.vernacular: 激動就係動;而勇敢就係站住:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 激動就是動;而勇敢就是站住:

passages.original: therefore, if thou art moved, thou runn’st away.
passages.vernacular: 所以,如果你被激動,你就跑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,如果你被激動,你就跑了。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: A dog of that house shall move me to stand.
passages.vernacular: 嗰家嘅一條狗就能激動我站住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那家的一條狗就能激動我站住。

passages.original: I will take the wall of any man or maid of Montague’s.
passages.vernacular: 蒙太古家任何男人或女僕,我都要佔牆邊嘅位置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒙太古家任何男人或女僕,我都要佔牆邊的位置。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: That shows thee a weak slave, for the weakest goes to the wall.
passages.vernacular: 呢顯出你係個軟弱嘅奴才,因為最弱嘅人才被擠到牆邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這顯出你是個軟弱的奴才,因為最弱的人才被擠到牆邊。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: True, and therefore women, being the weaker vessels, are ever thrust to the wall:
passages.vernacular: 冇錯,所以女人,作為較弱嘅器皿,總是被推到牆上:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒錯,所以女人,作為較弱的器皿,總是被推到牆上:

passages.original: therefore I will push Montague’s men from the wall, and thrust his maids to the wall.
passages.vernacular: 所以我要把蒙太古家嘅男人從牆邊推開,把佢家嘅女僕頂到牆上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我要把蒙太古家的男人從牆邊推開,把他家的女僕頂到牆上。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: The quarrel is between our masters and us their men.
passages.vernacular: 爭吵係喺我哋嘅主人同我哋呢啲僕人之間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爭吵是在我們的主人和我們這些僕人之間。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: ’Tis all one, I will show myself a tyrant: when I have fought with the men I will be civil with the maids, I will cut off their heads.
passages.vernacular: 都一樣,我要顯出自己係個暴君:我同男人打完架,對女僕就客氣,我要砍掉佢哋嘅頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 都一樣,我要顯出自己是個暴君:我和男人打完架,對女僕就客氣,我要砍掉她們的頭。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: The heads of the maids?
passages.vernacular: 女僕嘅頭?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女僕的頭?

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: Ay, the heads of the maids, or their maidenheads;
passages.vernacular: 對,女僕嘅頭,或佢哋嘅童貞;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,女僕的頭,或她們的童貞;

passages.original: take it in what sense thou wilt.
passages.vernacular: 你愛點理解就點理解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你愛怎麼理解就怎麼理解。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: They must take it in sense that feel it.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋必須按感覺到嘅意思去理解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們必須按感覺到的意思去理解。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: Me they shall feel while I am able to stand: and ’tis known I am a pretty piece of flesh.
passages.vernacular: 只要我仲站得住,佢哋就會感覺到我:人人都知道我係塊不錯嘅肉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要我還站得住,她們就會感覺到我:人人都知道我是塊不錯的肉。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: ’Tis well thou art not fish; if thou hadst, thou hadst been poor John.
passages.vernacular: 幸好你唔係魚;要係你係魚,你就係乾鱈魚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幸好你不是魚;要是你是魚,你就是乾鱈魚了。

passages.original: Draw thy tool; here comes of the house of Montagues.
passages.vernacular: 拔出你嘅傢伙;蒙太古家嘅人嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拔出你的傢伙;蒙太古家的人來了。

passages.original: Enter Abram and Balthasar.
passages.vernacular: [亞伯拉罕同巴爾薩澤上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [亞伯拉罕和巴爾薩澤上。]

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: My naked weapon is out: quarrel, I will back thee.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅劍已出鞘:吵吧,我支持你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的劍已出鞘:吵吧,我支持你。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: How?
passages.vernacular: 點?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼?

passages.original: Turn thy back and run?
passages.vernacular: 轉身逃跑?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 轉身逃跑?

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: Fear me not.
passages.vernacular: 別怕我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別怕我。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: No, marry; I fear thee!
passages.vernacular: 不,邊嘅話;我怕你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,哪的話;我怕你!

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: Let us take the law of our sides; let them begin.
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋站喺法律呢邊;讓佢哋先動手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們站在法律這邊;讓他們先動手。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: I will frown as I pass by, and let them take it as they list.
passages.vernacular: 我經過時皺眉,隨佢哋點想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我經過時皺眉,隨他們怎麼想。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: Nay, as they dare.
passages.vernacular: 不,隨佢哋敢點想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,隨他們敢怎麼想。

passages.original: I will bite my thumb at them, which is disgrace to them if they bear it.
passages.vernacular: 我要對佢哋咬拇指,佢哋若忍受,就係佢哋嘅恥辱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要對他們咬拇指,他們若忍受,就是他們的恥辱。

passages.title: Abram 亞伯拉罕
passages.original: Do you bite your thumb at us, sir?
passages.vernacular: 先生,你對我哋咬拇指嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,你對我們咬拇指嗎?

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: I do bite my thumb, sir.
passages.vernacular: 我係咬咗拇指,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是咬了拇指,先生。

passages.title: Abram 亞伯拉罕
passages.original: Do you bite your thumb at us, sir?
passages.vernacular: 先生,你對我哋咬拇指嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,你對我們咬拇指嗎?

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: Is the law of our side if I say ay?
passages.vernacular: 我若講係,算站喺法律呢邊嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我若說是,算站在法律這邊嗎?

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: No.
passages.vernacular: 不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: No sir, I do not bite my thumb at you, sir; but I bite my thumb, sir.
passages.vernacular: 不,先生,我唔係對你咬拇指,先生;不過我咬咗拇指,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,先生,我不是對你咬拇指,先生;可是我咬了拇指,先生。

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: Do you quarrel, sir?
passages.vernacular: 你要吵架嗎,先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要吵架嗎,先生?

passages.title: Abram 亞伯拉罕
passages.original: Quarrel, sir? No, sir.
passages.vernacular: 吵架,先生?不,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吵架,先生?不,先生。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: But if you do, sir, I am for you.
passages.vernacular: 但你若要吵,先生,我奉陪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你若要吵,先生,我奉陪。

passages.original: I serve as good a man as you.
passages.vernacular: 我服侍嘅主人同你嘅一樣好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我服侍的主人和你的一樣好。

passages.title: Abram 亞伯拉罕
passages.original: No better.
passages.vernacular: 唔會更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不會更好。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: Well, sir.
passages.vernacular: 好吧,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,先生。

passages.original: Enter Benvolio.
passages.vernacular: [班伏里奧上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [班伏里奧上。]

passages.title: Gregory 格列高里
passages.original: Say better; here comes one of my master’s kinsmen.
passages.vernacular: 講「更好」;我主人嘅一個親戚嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說「更好」;我主人的一個親戚來了。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: Yes, better, sir.
passages.vernacular: 對,更好,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,更好,先生。

passages.title: Abram 亞伯拉罕
passages.original: You lie.
passages.vernacular: 你撒謊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你撒謊。

passages.title: Sampson 參森
passages.original: Draw, if you be men.
passages.vernacular: 拔劍,如果你哋係男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拔劍,如果你們是男人。

passages.original: Gregory, remember thy washing blow.
passages.vernacular: 格列高里,記得你嗰致命嘅一擊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 格列高里,記得你那致命的一擊。

passages.original: [They fight.]
passages.vernacular: [二人交戰。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [二人交戰。]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Part, fools!
passages.vernacular: 分開,蠢貨!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 分開,蠢貨!

passages.original: put up your swords, you know not what you do.
passages.vernacular: 收起你哋嘅劍,你哋唔知道自己喺做乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收起你們的劍,你們不知道自己在做什麼。

passages.original: [Beats down their swords.]
passages.vernacular: [打落佢哋嘅劍。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [打落他們的劍。]

passages.original: Enter Tybalt.
passages.vernacular: [提伯特上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [提伯特上。]

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: What, art thou drawn among these heartless hinds?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,你喺呢啲冇心冇肺嘅鄉巴佬中拔咗劍?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,你在這些沒心沒肺的鄉巴佬中拔了劍?

passages.original: Turn thee Benvolio, look upon thy death.
passages.vernacular: 轉過嚟,班伏里奧,睇你嘅死期。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 轉過來,班伏里奧,看你的死期。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: I do but keep the peace, put up thy sword, Or manage it to part these men with me.
passages.vernacular: 我只係維持和平,收起你嘅劍,或者幫我分開呢啲人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是維持和平,收起你的劍,或者幫我分開這些人。

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: What, drawn, and talk of peace?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,拔咗劍,仲談和平?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,拔了劍,還談和平?

passages.original: I hate the word As I hate hell, all Montagues, and thee: Have at thee, coward.
passages.vernacular: 我恨呢個詞,如同恨地獄、所有蒙太古家嘅人,同你:睇劍,懦夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我恨這個詞,如同恨地獄、所有蒙太古家的人,和你:看劍,懦夫。

passages.original: [They fight.]
passages.vernacular: [二人交戰。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [二人交戰。]

passages.original: Enter three or four Citizens with clubs.
passages.vernacular: [三四名市民持棍棒上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [三四名市民持棍棒上。]

passages.title: First Citizen 第一市民
passages.original: Clubs, bills and partisans! Strike!
passages.vernacular: 棍棒、長戟、戰斧!打!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 棍棒、長戟、戰斧!打!

passages.original: Beat them down!
passages.vernacular: 打倒佢哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 打倒他們!

passages.original: Down with the Capulets!
passages.vernacular: 打倒凱普雷特家!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 打倒凱普雷特家!

passages.original: Down with the Montagues!
passages.vernacular: 打倒蒙太古家!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 打倒蒙太古家!

passages.original: Enter Capulet in his gown, and Lady Capulet.
passages.vernacular: [凱普雷特穿瞓袍,偕凱普雷特夫人上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱普雷特穿睡袍,偕凱普雷特夫人上。]

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: What noise is this?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係乜嘢吵鬧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是什麼吵鬧?

passages.original: Give me my long sword, ho!
passages.vernacular: 畀我長劍,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我長劍,喂!

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: A crutch, a crutch!
passages.vernacular: 拐杖,拐杖!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拐杖,拐杖!

passages.original: Why call you for a sword?
passages.vernacular: 你叫劍幹乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你叫劍幹什麼?

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: My sword, I say!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅劍,我講!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的劍,我說!

passages.original: Old Montague is come, And flourishes his blade in spite of me.
passages.vernacular: 老蒙太古來喇,不顧我,揮舞住佢嘅刀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老蒙太古來了,不顧我,揮舞著他的刀。

passages.original: Enter Montague and his Lady Montague.
passages.vernacular: [蒙太古同蒙太古夫人上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [蒙太古與蒙太古夫人上。]

passages.title: Montague 蒙太古
passages.original: Thou villain Capulet!
passages.vernacular: 你呢惡棍凱普雷特!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這惡棍凱普雷特!

passages.original: Hold me not, let me go.
passages.vernacular: 別拉住我,讓我去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別拉住我,讓我去。

passages.title: Lady Montague 蒙太古夫人
passages.original: Thou shalt not stir one foot to seek a foe.
passages.vernacular: 你不准邁一步去找仇人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不准邁一步去找仇人。

passages.original: Enter Prince Escalus, with Attendants.
passages.vernacular: [親王艾斯卡勒斯偕侍從上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [親王艾斯卡勒斯偕侍從上。]

passages.title: Prince 親王
passages.original: Rebellious subjects, enemies to peace, Profaners of this neighbour-stained steel,— Will they not hear? What, ho!
passages.vernacular: 叛逆嘅臣民,和平嘅敵人,玷污呢被鄰人血污染嘅鋼刃嘅人,——佢哋不聽嗎?乜嘢,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叛逆的臣民,和平的敵人,玷污這被鄰人血污染的鋼刃的人,——他們不聽嗎?什麼,喂!

passages.original: You men, you beasts, That quench the fire of your pernicious rage With purple fountains issuing from your veins, On pain of torture, from those bloody hands Throw your mistemper’d weapons to the ground And hear the sentence of your moved prince.
passages.vernacular: 你哋呢啲人,你哋呢啲野獸,用你哋血管裡湧出嘅紫色噴泉去熄滅你哋有害憤怒嘅火焰,喺酷刑嘅懲罰下,從嗰啲血腥嘅手中,把你哋使壞嘅武器扔到地上,聽你哋被激怒嘅親王嘅判決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們這些人,你們這些野獸,用你們血管裡湧出的紫色噴泉去熄滅你們有害憤怒的火焰,在酷刑的懲罰下,從那些血腥的手中,把你們使壞的武器扔到地上,聽你們被激怒的親王的判決。

passages.original: Three civil brawls, bred of an airy word, By thee, old Capulet, and Montague, Have thrice disturb’d the quiet of our streets, And made Verona’s ancient citizens Cast by their grave beseeming ornaments, To wield old partisans, in hands as old, Canker’d with peace, to part your canker’d hate.
passages.vernacular: 三場平民鬥毆,由一句空話引起,由你,老凱普雷特,同蒙太古,三次擾亂咗我哋街道嘅安寧,使維洛嗰嘅老市民扔掉佢哋莊重得體嘅服飾,用老手舞動生咗鏽嘅長戟,以調解你哋生咗鏽嘅仇恨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三場平民鬥毆,由一句空話引起,由你,老凱普雷特,和蒙太古,三次擾亂了我們街道的安寧,使維洛那的老市民扔掉他們莊重得體的服飾,用老手舞動生了鏽的長戟,以調解你們生了鏽的仇恨。

passages.original: If ever you disturb our streets again, Your lives shall pay the forfeit of the peace.
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋再擾亂我哋嘅街道,你哋嘅性命將為和平付出代價。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們再擾亂我們的街道,你們的性命將為和平付出代價。

passages.original: For this time all the rest depart away: You, Capulet, shall go along with me, And Montague, come you this afternoon, To know our farther pleasure in this case, To old Free-town, our common judgement-place.
passages.vernacular: 呢一次其餘嘅人都散去:你,凱普雷特,跟我嚟,而蒙太古,你今日下午嚟,聽取我哋對呢案件嘅進一步旨意,到自由城,我哋共同嘅審判地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一次其餘的人都散去:你,凱普雷特,跟我來,而蒙太古,你今天下午來,聽取我們對這案件的進一步旨意,到自由城,我們共同的審判地。

passages.original: Once more, on pain of death, all men depart.
passages.vernacular: 再一次,違者處死,所有人散去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再一次,違者處死,所有人散去。

passages.original: [Exeunt Prince and Attendants; Capulet, Lady Capulet, Tybalt, Citizens and Servants.]
passages.vernacular: [親王及侍從下;凱普雷特、凱普雷特夫人、提伯特、市民同僕人哋下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [親王及侍從下;凱普雷特、凱普雷特夫人、提伯特、市民和僕人們下。]

passages.title: Montague 蒙太古
passages.original: Who set this ancient quarrel new abroach?
passages.vernacular: 邊個又挑起呢古老嘅爭吵?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰又挑起這古老的爭吵?

passages.original: Speak, nephew, were you by when it began?
passages.vernacular: 講,侄兒,爭吵開始時你在場嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說,侄兒,爭吵開始時你在場嗎?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Here were the servants of your adversary And yours, close fighting ere I did approach.
passages.vernacular: 你對頭嘅僕人同你嘅僕人,喺我到達之前就喺近身搏鬥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你對頭的僕人和你的僕人,在我到達之前就在近身搏鬥。

passages.original: I drew to part them, in the instant came The fiery Tybalt, with his sword prepar’d, Which, as he breath’d defiance to my ears, He swung about his head, and cut the winds, Who nothing hurt withal, hiss’d him in scorn.
passages.vernacular: 我拔劍去分開佢哋,就喺嗰一刻火爆嘅提伯特拔劍而嚟,佢一邊對我耳朵吐出挑戰,一邊把劍喺頭上揮舞,劈開風,風毫無傷害,嘶嘶地嘲笑佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我拔劍去分開他們,就在那一刻火爆的提伯特拔劍而來,他一邊對我耳朵吐出挑戰,一邊把劍在頭上揮舞,劈開風,風毫無傷害,嘶嘶地嘲笑他。

passages.original: While we were interchanging thrusts and blows Came more and more, and fought on part and part, Till the Prince came, who parted either part.
passages.vernacular: 我哋互相刺擊嘅時候,越嚟越多嘅人嚟喇,雙方互相打,直到親王嚟喇,把兩邊都分開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們互相刺擊的時候,越來越多的人來了,雙方互相打,直到親王來了,把兩邊都分開。

passages.title: Lady Montague 蒙太古夫人
passages.original: O where is Romeo, saw you him today?
passages.vernacular: 啊,羅密歐喺邊度?你今日見到佢咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,羅密歐在哪裡?你今天見到他了嗎?

passages.original: Right glad I am he was not at this fray.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興佢冇喺呢場混戰中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興他沒在這場混戰中。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Madam, an hour before the worshipp’d sun Peer’d forth the golden window of the east, A troubled mind drave me to walk abroad, Where underneath the grove of sycamore That westward rooteth from this city side, So early walking did I see your son.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,喺受人崇拜嘅太陽從東方金色嘅窗口探頭之前一小時,一種煩亂嘅心情驅使我出去散步,喺從呢城邊向西生長嘅嗰片無花果樹林下,我睇見令郎咁早就喺走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,在受人崇拜的太陽從東方金色的窗口探頭之前一小時,一種煩亂的心情驅使我出去散步,在從這城邊向西生長的那片無花果樹林下,我看見令郎那麼早就在走。

passages.original: Towards him I made, but he was ware of me, And stole into the covert of the wood.
passages.vernacular: 我向佢走去,佢卻察覺我,溜進咗樹林深處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向他走去,他卻察覺我,溜進了樹林深處。

passages.original: I, measuring his affections by my own, Which then most sought where most might not be found, Being one too many by my weary self, Pursu’d my humour, not pursuing his, And gladly shunn’d who gladly fled from me.
passages.vernacular: 我以自己嘅心情衡量佢嘅感情,喺嗰時最想找冇人嘅地方,因為被我呢疲倦嘅自己當成多餘嘅一個,我順從我嘅心境,冇去追佢嘅,高興地避開嗰高興地躲我嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以自己的心情衡量他的感情,在那時最想找沒人的地方,因為被我這疲倦的自己當成多餘的一個,我順從我的心境,沒去追他的,高興地避開那高興地躲我的人。

passages.title: Montague 蒙太古
passages.original: Many a morning hath he there been seen, With tears augmenting the fresh morning’s dew, Adding to clouds more clouds with his deep sighs;
passages.vernacular: 許多個早晨,人哋喺嗰度見到佢,用淚水增添清晨嘅露水,用深深嘅嘆息畀雲彩添上更多嘅雲;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 許多個早晨,人們在那裡見到他,用淚水增添清晨的露水,用深深的嘆息給雲彩添上更多的雲;

passages.original: But all so soon as the all-cheering sun Should in the farthest east begin to draw The shady curtains from Aurora’s bed, Away from light steals home my heavy son, And private in his chamber pens himself, Shuts up his windows, locks fair daylight out And makes himself an artificial night.
passages.vernacular: 但一等到普照萬物嘅太陽開始喺極遠嘅東方從奧羅拉嘅床上拉開陰暗嘅帷幕,我嗰沉重嘅兒子就從光明中溜回家,把自己關喺臥室裡,關上窗,把美好嘅日光鎖喺外面,為自己造出人工嘅黑夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但一等到普照萬物的太陽開始在極遠的東方從奧羅拉的床上拉開陰暗的帷幕,我那沉重的兒子就從光明中溜回家,把自己關在臥室裡,關上窗,把美好的日光鎖在外面,為自己造出人工的黑夜。

passages.original: Black and portentous must this humour prove, Unless good counsel may the cause remove.
passages.vernacular: 呢種心境必定證明係黑暗而不祥嘅,除非好嘅勸告能除去原因。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種心境必定證明是黑暗而不祥的,除非好的勸告能除去原因。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: My noble uncle, do you know the cause?
passages.vernacular: 我高貴嘅叔父,你知道原因嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我高貴的叔父,你知道原因嗎?

passages.title: Montague 蒙太古
passages.original: I neither know it nor can learn of him.
passages.vernacular: 我既唔知道,都唔能夠從佢嗰度得知。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我既不知道,也不能從他那裡得知。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Have you importun’d him by any means?
passages.vernacular: 你用乜嘢辦法催問過佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你用什麼辦法催問過他嗎?

passages.title: Montague 蒙太古
passages.original: Both by myself and many other friends; But he, his own affections’ counsellor, Is to himself—I will not say how true— But to himself so secret and so close, So far from sounding and discovery, As is the bud bit with an envious worm Ere he can spread his sweet leaves to the air, Or dedicate his beauty to the sun.
passages.vernacular: 我自己同許多其他朋友都試過;但佢,佢自己感情嘅謀士,對自己——我不講有多真誠——卻對自己如此隱秘、如此封閉,如此難以探測同發現,像花蕾被嫉妒嘅蟲咬喇,仲嚟不及向空氣展開甜美嘅葉子,或把美麗獻畀太陽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己和許多其他朋友都試過;但他,他自己感情的謀士,對自己——我不說有多真誠——卻對自己如此隱秘、如此封閉,如此難以探測和發現,像花蕾被嫉妒的蟲咬了,還來不及向空氣展開甜美的葉子,或把美麗獻給太陽。

passages.original: Could we but learn from whence his sorrows grow, We would as willingly give cure as know.
passages.vernacular: 要係我哋能知道佢嘅悲傷從邊度生出,我哋會像想知道一樣樂意畀佢醫治。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是我們能知道他的悲傷從哪裡生出,我們會像想知道一樣樂意給他醫治。

passages.original: Enter Romeo.
passages.vernacular: [羅密歐上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅密歐上。]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: See, where he comes.
passages.vernacular: 睇,佢嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,他來了。

passages.original: So please you step aside; I’ll know his grievance or be much denied.
passages.vernacular: 請你哋站到一旁;我要麼知道佢嘅憂愁,要麼被佢嚴拒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你們站到一旁;我要麼知道他的憂愁,要麼被他嚴拒。

passages.title: Montague 蒙太古
passages.original: I would thou wert so happy by thy stay To hear true shrift.
passages.vernacular: 但願你留下嚟能得到你真正嘅告解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但願你留下來能得到你真正的告解。

passages.original: Come, madam, let’s away,
passages.vernacular: 嚟,夫人,我哋走吧,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,夫人,我們走吧,

passages.original: [Exeunt Montague and Lady Montague.]
passages.vernacular: [蒙太古同蒙太古夫人下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [蒙太古與蒙太古夫人下。]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Good morrow, cousin.
passages.vernacular: 早安,堂兄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早安,堂兄。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Is the day so young?
passages.vernacular: 天仲咁早嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天還這麼早嗎?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: But new struck nine.
passages.vernacular: 剛敲過九點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 剛敲過九點。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Ay me, sad hours seem long.
passages.vernacular: 唉,憂愁嘅時辰好像特別長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,憂愁的時辰好像特別長。

passages.original: Was that my father that went hence so fast?
passages.vernacular: 頭先匆匆走開嘅係我父親嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 剛才匆匆走開的是我父親嗎?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: It was.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的。

passages.original: What sadness lengthens Romeo’s hours?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢憂愁延長咗羅密歐嘅時辰?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼憂愁延長了羅密歐的時辰?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Not having that which, having, makes them short.
passages.vernacular: 因為冇嗰擁有咗就會讓時辰變短嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為沒有那擁有了就會讓時辰變短的東西。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: In love?
passages.vernacular: 戀愛喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戀愛了?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Out.
passages.vernacular: 失戀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 失戀。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Of love?
passages.vernacular: 失去愛?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 失去愛?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Out of her favour where I am in love.
passages.vernacular: 失去我所愛嘅佢嘅青睞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 失去我所愛的她的青睞。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Alas that love so gentle in his view, Should be so tyrannous and rough in proof.
passages.vernacular: 唉,愛情睇來咁樣溫柔,實際卻咁樣暴虐粗暴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,愛情看來這樣溫柔,實際卻這樣暴虐粗暴。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Alas that love, whose view is muffled still, Should, without eyes, see pathways to his will!
passages.vernacular: 唉,愛情,眼睛總是被蒙住,卻能唔使眼睛睇到通往佢意願嘅路!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,愛情,眼睛總是被蒙著,卻能不用眼睛看到通往他意願的路!

passages.original: Where shall we dine? O me!
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺邊度食飯?哎呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在哪裡吃飯?哎呀!

passages.original: What fray was here?
passages.vernacular: 呢度有過乜嘢鬥毆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡有過什麼鬥毆?

passages.original: Yet tell me not, for I have heard it all.
passages.vernacular: 不過別告訴我,我都聽講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過別告訴我,我都聽說了。

passages.original: Here’s much to do with hate, but more with love:
passages.vernacular: 呢度有許多同恨有關嘅事,但更多同愛有關:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡有許多與恨有關的事,但更多與愛有關:

passages.original: Why, then, O brawling love!
passages.vernacular: 咁,啊,吵鬧嘅愛!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,啊,吵鬧的愛!

passages.original: O loving hate!
passages.vernacular: 啊,有愛嘅恨!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,有愛的恨!

passages.original: O anything, of nothing first create!
passages.vernacular: 啊,從無中先創造出嘅一切!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,從無中先創造出的一切!

passages.original: O heavy lightness!
passages.vernacular: 啊,沉重嘅輕浮!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,沉重的輕浮!

passages.original: serious vanity!
passages.vernacular: 嚴肅嘅虛妄!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嚴肅的虛妄!

passages.original: Misshapen chaos of well-seeming forms!
passages.vernacular: 睇似美好形體嘅醜陋混沌!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看似美好形體的醜陋混沌!

passages.original: Feather of lead, bright smoke, cold fire, sick health!
passages.vernacular: 鉛嘅羽毛,明亮嘅煙,冰冷嘅火,生病嘅健康!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鉛的羽毛,明亮的煙,冰冷的火,生病的健康!

passages.original: Still-waking sleep, that is not what it is!
passages.vernacular: 一直醒住嘅瞓眠,唔係佢自己所係嘅嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一直醒著的睡眠,不是它自己所是的東西!

passages.original: This love feel I, that feel no love in this.
passages.vernacular: 我感覺到呢種愛,卻喺呢度感覺唔到愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感覺到這種愛,卻在這裡感覺不到愛。

passages.original: Dost thou not laugh?
passages.vernacular: 你不笑嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不笑嗎?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: No coz, I rather weep.
passages.vernacular: 不,堂兄,我寧願哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,堂兄,我寧願哭。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Good heart, at what?
passages.vernacular: 好心人,點解?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好心人,為什麼?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: At thy good heart’s oppression.
passages.vernacular: 為你好心被壓迫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為你好心被壓迫。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Why such is love’s transgression.
passages.vernacular: 哎,呢個就係愛嘅過錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,這就是愛的過錯。

passages.original: Griefs of mine own lie heavy in my breast, Which thou wilt propagate to have it prest With more of thine.
passages.vernacular: 我自己嘅憂愁沉重地壓喺我胸口,你想擴大佢,要讓佢被更多你嘅憂愁壓上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己的憂愁沉重地壓在我胸口,你想擴大它,要讓它被更多你的憂愁壓上。

passages.original: This love that thou hast shown Doth add more grief to too much of mine own.
passages.vernacular: 你所顯示嘅呢份愛,只係喺我過多嘅憂愁上添加更多憂愁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你所顯示的這份愛,只是在我過多的憂愁上添加更多憂愁。

passages.original: Love is a smoke made with the fume of sighs; Being purg’d, a fire sparkling in lovers’ eyes;
passages.vernacular: 愛情係嘆息嘅煙氣生成嘅煙;被淨化時,係戀人眼中閃爍嘅火;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛情是嘆息的煙氣生成的煙;被淨化時,是戀人眼中閃爍的火;

passages.original: Being vex’d, a sea nourish’d with lovers’ tears: What is it else?
passages.vernacular: 被攪擾時,係戀人眼淚滋養嘅海:佢定係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被攪擾時,是戀人眼淚滋養的海:它還是什麼?

passages.original: A madness most discreet, A choking gall, and a preserving sweet.
passages.vernacular: 一種最審慎嘅瘋狂,一種哽喉嘅膽汁,同一種保存人嘅甜蜜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一種最審慎的瘋狂,一種哽喉的膽汁,和一種保存人的甜蜜。

passages.original: Farewell, my coz.
passages.vernacular: 再會,我嘅堂兄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會,我的堂兄。

passages.original: [Going.]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Soft!
passages.vernacular: 且慢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 且慢!

passages.original: I will go along: And if you leave me so, you do me wrong.
passages.vernacular: 我陪你走:你咁樣丟下我,係對我不公。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我陪你走:你這樣丟下我,是對我不公。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Tut!
passages.vernacular: 呸!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呸!

passages.original: I have lost myself; I am not here.
passages.vernacular: 我丟咗我自己;我不喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我丟了我自己;我不在這裡。

passages.original: This is not Romeo, he’s some other where.
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係羅密歐,佢喺別嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是羅密歐,他在別的地方。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Tell me in sadness who is that you love?
passages.vernacular: 認真地告訴我,你愛嘅係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 認真地告訴我,你愛的是誰?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: What, shall I groan and tell thee?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,要我呻吟住告訴你?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,要我呻吟著告訴你?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Groan!
passages.vernacular: 呻吟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呻吟!

passages.original: Why, no; but sadly tell me who.
passages.vernacular: 不,唔使;認真地告訴我係邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,不用;認真地告訴我是誰。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Bid a sick man in sadness make his will, A word ill urg’d to one that is so ill.
passages.vernacular: 叫一個病人認真地立遺囑,呢話對病得咁重嘅人講得太不好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫一個病人認真地立遺囑,這話對病得這麼重的人說得太不好。

passages.original: In sadness, cousin, I do love a woman.
passages.vernacular: 認真講,堂兄,我愛一個女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 認真說,堂兄,我愛一個女人。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: I aim’d so near when I suppos’d you lov’d.
passages.vernacular: 我猜你戀愛咗嘅時候,猜得差不多就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我猜你戀愛了的時候,猜得差不多就是這樣。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: A right good markman, and she’s fair I love.
passages.vernacular: 好一個神射手,而且我愛嘅女子好美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好一個神射手,而且我愛的女子很美。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: A right fair mark, fair coz, is soonest hit.
passages.vernacular: 最美嘅靶子,好堂兄,最容易被射中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最美的靶子,好堂兄,最容易被射中。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Well, in that hit you miss: she’ll not be hit With Cupid’s arrow, she hath Dian’s wit;
passages.vernacular: 好,你射偏喇:佢唔會被丘比特嘅箭射中,佢有狄安娜嘅智慧;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,你射偏了:她不會被丘比特的箭射中,她有狄安娜的智慧;

passages.original: And in strong proof of chastity well arm’d, From love’s weak childish bow she lives uncharm’d.
passages.vernacular: 並且有堅固嘅貞潔作為鎧甲,從愛情嗰軟弱幼稚嘅弓下毫髮無損地活住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並且有堅固的貞潔作為鎧甲,從愛情那軟弱幼稚的弓下毫髮無損地活著。

passages.original: She will not stay the siege of loving terms Nor bide th’encounter of assailing eyes, Nor ope her lap to saint-seducing gold:
passages.vernacular: 佢唔肯受愛情言語嘅圍攻,唔肯忍受攻擊嘅眼睛嘅交鋒,都唔肯向能誘惑聖人嘅黃金敞開懷抱:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不肯受愛情言語的圍攻,不肯忍受攻擊的眼睛的交鋒,也不肯向能誘惑聖人的黃金敞開懷抱:

passages.original: O she’s rich in beauty, only poor That when she dies, with beauty dies her store.
passages.vernacular: 啊,佢嘅美貌富有,只係貧窮在於,當佢死時,佢嘅美貌所有嘅財富都隨之而死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,她的美貌富有,只是貧窮在於,當她死時,她的美貌所有的財富也隨之而死。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Then she hath sworn that she will still live chaste?
passages.vernacular: 嗰佢已發誓要永遠保持貞潔?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那她已發誓要永遠保持貞潔?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: She hath, and in that sparing makes huge waste;
passages.vernacular: 佢已發誓,而喺呢吝嗇中浪費極大;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她已發誓,而在這吝嗇中浪費極大;

passages.original: For beauty starv’d with her severity, Cuts beauty off from all posterity.
passages.vernacular: 因為美被佢嘅嚴苛餓死,斷絕咗美嘅所有後代。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為美被她的嚴苛餓死,斷絕了美的所有後代。

passages.original: She is too fair, too wise; wisely too fair, To merit bliss by making me despair.
passages.vernacular: 佢太美,太聰明;聰明得太美,以致讓我絕望嚟換取佢嘅福分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她太美,太聰明;聰明得太美,以致讓我絕望來換取她的福分。

passages.original: She hath forsworn to love, and in that vow Do I live dead, that live to tell it now.
passages.vernacular: 佢已發誓放棄愛情,而喺呢誓言裡,我雖活住講呢話,卻等於活住嘅死人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她已發誓放棄愛情,而在這誓言裡,我雖活著說這話,卻等於活著的死人。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Be rul’d by me, forget to think of her.
passages.vernacular: 聽我嘅,唔好再想佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽我的,別再想她。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: O teach me how I should forget to think.
passages.vernacular: 啊,教我點樣忘記去想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,教我怎樣忘記去想。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: By giving liberty unto thine eyes; Examine other beauties.
passages.vernacular: 讓你嘅眼睛自由;去睇別嘅美人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓你的眼睛自由;去看別的美人。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: ’Tis the way To call hers, exquisite, in question more.
passages.vernacular: 呢正是使佢嘅美,嗰絕妙嘅美,更受質疑嘅辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這正是使她的美,那絕妙的美,更受質疑的辦法。

passages.original: These happy masks that kiss fair ladies’ brows, Being black, puts us in mind they hide the fair;
passages.vernacular: 呢啲親吻美麗女士額頭嘅快樂面具,因為係黑嘅,提醒我哋佢哋遮住咗美人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些親吻美麗女士額頭的快樂面具,因為是黑的,提醒我們它們遮住了美人;

passages.original: He that is strucken blind cannot forget The precious treasure of his eyesight lost.
passages.vernacular: 被打瞎嘅人唔能夠忘記佢失去嘅視力嗰寶貴嘅寶藏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被打瞎的人不能忘記他失去的視力那寶貴的寶藏。

passages.original: Show me a mistress that is passing fair, What doth her beauty serve but as a note Where I may read who pass’d that passing fair?
passages.vernacular: 畀我睇一位美得出眾嘅情人,佢嘅美貌除咗作為記號,仲有乜嘢用,讓我讀出邊個比嗰出眾嘅美人更出眾?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我看一位美得出眾的情人,她的美貌除了作為記號,還有什麼用,讓我讀出誰比那出眾的美人更出眾?

passages.original: Farewell, thou canst not teach me to forget.
passages.vernacular: 再會,你唔能夠教我忘記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會,你不能教我忘記。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: I’ll pay that doctrine, or else die in debt.
passages.vernacular: 我要仲清呢個教訓,否則就欠住債死去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要還清這個教訓,否則就欠著債死去。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene II — A Street 第一幕第二場:街道

passages.original: Enter Capulet, Paris and Servant.
passages.vernacular: [凱普雷特、帕里斯同一名僕人上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱普雷特、帕里斯與一名僕人上。]

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: But Montague is bound as well as I, In penalty alike;
passages.vernacular: 但蒙太古同我一樣受約束,受同樣嘅懲罰;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但蒙太古和我一樣受約束,受同樣的懲罰;

passages.original: and ’tis not hard, I think, For men so old as we to keep the peace.
passages.vernacular: 我想,對我哋咁老嘅人來講,保持和平不難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想,對我們這麼老的人來說,保持和平不難。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: Of honourable reckoning are you both, And pity ’tis you liv’d at odds so long.
passages.vernacular: 你哋兩位都係備受尊敬嘅人,可惜你哋咁久互相敵對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們兩位都是備受尊敬的人,可惜你們這麼久互相敵對。

passages.original: But now my lord, what say you to my suit?
passages.vernacular: 不過而家,大人,您對我嘅求婚點講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過現在,大人,您對我的求婚怎麼說?

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: But saying o’er what I have said before.
passages.vernacular: 我只能重複我以前講過嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只能重複我以前說過的話。

passages.original: My child is yet a stranger in the world, She hath not seen the change of fourteen years;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅細路在世上定係個陌生人,佢仲冇見過十四個年頭嘅變遷;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的孩子在世上還是個陌生人,她還沒見過十四個年頭的變遷;

passages.original: Let two more summers wither in their pride Ere we may think her ripe to be a bride.
passages.vernacular: 再讓兩個夏天喺盛放中凋謝,我哋才可以認為佢成熟得可以做新娘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再讓兩個夏天在盛放中凋謝,我們才可以認為她成熟得可以做新娘。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: Younger than she are happy mothers made.
passages.vernacular: 比佢更年輕嘅,都成咗快樂嘅母親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比她更年輕的,都成了快樂的母親。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: And too soon marr’d are those so early made.
passages.vernacular: 太早造就嘅,都太早毀壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太早造就的,也太早毀壞。

passages.original: The earth hath swallowed all my hopes but she, She is the hopeful lady of my earth:
passages.vernacular: 大地吞噬咗我除佢以外嘅所有希望,佢係我塵世上嘅希望之女:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大地吞噬了我除她以外的所有希望,她是我塵世上的希望之女:

passages.original: But woo her, gentle Paris, get her heart, My will to her consent is but a part;
passages.vernacular: 但你去追求佢吧,溫和嘅帕里斯,贏得佢嘅心,我嘅意願只係佢同意嘅一部分;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你去追求她吧,溫和的帕里斯,贏得她的心,我的意願只是她同意的一部分;

passages.original: And she agree, within her scope of choice Lies my consent and fair according voice.
passages.vernacular: 只要佢答應,喺佢選擇嘅範圍內,就有我嘅同意同欣然嘅贊成。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要她答應,在她選擇的範圍內,就有我的同意和欣然的贊成。

passages.original: This night I hold an old accustom’d feast, Whereto I have invited many a guest, Such as I love, and you among the store, One more, most welcome, makes my number more.
passages.vernacular: 今晚我舉行一個老習慣嘅宴會,邀請咗許多客人,都係我喜愛嘅,你都喺其中;多一位最受歡迎嘅客人,就使我嘅人數更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晚我舉行一個老習慣的宴會,邀請了許多客人,都是我喜愛的,你也在其中;多一位最受歡迎的客人,就使我的人數更多。

passages.original: At my poor house look to behold this night Earth-treading stars that make dark heaven light:
passages.vernacular: 今晚喺我寒舍,你會睇到踏住大地嘅星星,使黑暗嘅天空變亮:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晚在我寒舍,你會看到踏著大地的星星,使黑暗的天空變亮:

passages.original: Such comfort as do lusty young men feel When well apparell’d April on the heel Of limping winter treads, even such delight Among fresh female buds shall you this night Inherit at my house.
passages.vernacular: 像精神抖擻嘅年輕人感受到嘅嗰種慰藉,當穿戴整齊嘅四月緊跟住跛行嘅冬天嘅腳跟而嚟,今晚喺我家,你將喺鮮嫩嘅女花蕾中享受到同樣嘅歡樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像精神抖擻的年輕人感受到的那種慰藉,當穿戴整齊的四月緊跟著跛行的冬天的腳跟而來,今晚在我家,你將在鮮嫩的女花蕾中享受到同樣的歡樂。

passages.original: Hear all, all see, And like her most whose merit most shall be:
passages.vernacular: 聽盡所有,睇盡所有,最鍾意嗰優點最大嘅人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽盡所有,看盡所有,最喜歡那優點最大的人:

passages.original: Which, on more view of many, mine, being one, May stand in number, though in reckoning none.
passages.vernacular: 喺多睇多人之後,我女兒作為其中之一,或者能算一個數目,卻不算乜嘢價值。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在多看多人之後,我女兒作為其中之一,也許能算一個數目,卻不算什麼價值。

passages.original: Come, go with me.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,跟我走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,跟我走。

passages.original: Go, sirrah, trudge about Through fair Verona;
passages.vernacular: 去,小子,喺美麗嘅維洛嗰四處跑跑;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,小子,在美麗的維洛那四處跑跑;

passages.original: find those persons out Whose names are written there, [gives a paper] and to them say, My house and welcome on their pleasure stay.
passages.vernacular: 找出名字寫喺呢上面嘅人,[遞一張紙]對佢哋講,我嘅家同歡迎隨佢哋樂意恭候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 找出名字寫在這上面的人,[遞一張紙]對他們說,我的家和歡迎隨他們樂意恭候。

passages.original: [Exeunt Capulet and Paris.]
passages.vernacular: [凱普雷特同帕里斯下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱普雷特與帕里斯下。]

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: Find them out whose names are written here!
passages.vernacular: 找出名字寫喺呢度嘅人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 找出名字寫在這裡的人!

passages.original: It is written that the shoemaker should meddle with his yard and the tailor with his last, the fisher with his pencil, and the painter with his nets;
passages.vernacular: 有話講,鞋匠該管佢嘅尺,裁縫該管佢嘅鞋楦,漁夫該管佢嘅畫筆,畫家該管佢嘅網;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有話說,鞋匠該管他的尺,裁縫該管他的鞋楦,漁夫該管他的畫筆,畫家該管他的網;

passages.original: but I am sent to find those persons whose names are here writ, and can never find what names the writing person hath here writ.
passages.vernacular: 不過我被派去找名字寫喺呢度嘅人,卻永遠找唔到寫呢字嘅人喺呢度寫嘅係乜嘢名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我被派去找名字寫在這裡的人,卻永遠找不到寫這字的人在這裡寫的是什麼名字。

passages.original: I must to the learned.
passages.vernacular: 我得去找有學問嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得去找有學問的人。

passages.original: In good time!
passages.vernacular: 嚟得正好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來得正好!

passages.original: Enter Benvolio and Romeo.
passages.vernacular: [班伏里奧同羅密歐上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [班伏里奧與羅密歐上。]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Tut, man, one fire burns out another’s burning, One pain is lessen’d by another’s anguish;
passages.vernacular: 呸,老兄,一團火燒滅另一團火嘅燃燒,一種痛苦因另一種痛苦嘅劇烈而減輕;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呸,老兄,一團火燒滅另一團火的燃燒,一種痛苦因另一種痛苦的劇烈而減輕;

passages.original: Turn giddy, and be holp by backward turning; One desperate grief cures with another’s languish:
passages.vernacular: 頭暈就倒轉身子嚟治,一種絕望嘅悲傷由另一種嘅衰弱嚟治:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 頭暈就倒轉身子來治,一種絕望的悲傷由另一種的衰弱來治:

passages.original: Take thou some new infection to thy eye, And the rank poison of the old will die.
passages.vernacular: 讓你嘅眼睛染上一種新嘅傳染,舊嘅惡毒就會死去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓你的眼睛染上一種新的傳染,舊的惡毒就會死去。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Your plantain leaf is excellent for that.
passages.vernacular: 你嗰車前草葉對嗰個好有效。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你那車前草葉對那個很有效。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: For what, I pray thee?
passages.vernacular: 對乜嘢,請問?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對什麼,請問?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: For your broken shin.
passages.vernacular: 對你摔破嘅脛骨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對你摔破的脛骨。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Why, Romeo, art thou mad?
passages.vernacular: 點,羅密歐,你瘋咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,羅密歐,你瘋了嗎?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Not mad, but bound more than a madman is: Shut up in prison, kept without my food, Whipp’d and tormented and—God-den, good fellow.
passages.vernacular: 唔係瘋喇,但比瘋子仲被綑得緊:被關喺牢裡,不畀飯食,被鞭打、折磨,而且——晚安,好朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是瘋了,但比瘋子還被綑得緊:被關在牢裡,不給飯吃,被鞭打、折磨,而且——晚安,好朋友。

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: God gi’ go-den.
passages.vernacular: 願上帝賜你晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上帝賜你晚安。

passages.original: I pray, sir, can you read?
passages.vernacular: 請問,先生,你識字嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請問,先生,你識字嗎?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Ay, mine own fortune in my misery.
passages.vernacular: 識,喺我嘅不幸中讀自己嘅命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 識,在我的不幸中讀自己的命運。

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: Perhaps you have learned it without book.
passages.vernacular: 或者你係不睇書就學會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許你是不看書就學會的。

passages.original: But I pray, can you read anything you see?
passages.vernacular: 但請問,你睇到乜嘢都能讀嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但請問,你看到什麼都能讀嗎?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Ay, If I know the letters and the language.
passages.vernacular: 能,只要我認得字母同語言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 能,只要我認得字母和語言。

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: Ye say honestly, rest you merry!
passages.vernacular: 你講得老實,祝你愉快!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說得老實,祝你愉快!

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Stay, fellow; I can read.
passages.vernacular: 站住,朋友;我能讀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 站住,朋友;我能讀。

passages.original: [He reads the letter.]
passages.vernacular: [佢讀信。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [他讀信。]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Signior Martino and his wife and daughters; County Anselmo and his beauteous sisters;
passages.vernacular: 馬丁諾先生同佢嘅妻子同女兒哋;安塞莫伯爵同佢美麗嘅姊妹哋;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬丁諾先生和他的妻子與女兒們;安塞莫伯爵和他美麗的姊妹們;

passages.original: The lady widow of Utruvio; Signior Placentio and his lovely nieces;
passages.vernacular: 烏特魯維奧嘅寡婦夫人;普拉森提奧先生同佢可愛嘅侄女哋;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 烏特魯維奧的寡婦夫人;普拉森提奧先生和他可愛的侄女們;

passages.original: Mercutio and his brother Valentine; Mine uncle Capulet, his wife, and daughters;
passages.vernacular: 茂丘西奧同佢嘅兄弟瓦倫丁;我嘅叔父凱普雷特、佢嘅妻子同女兒哋;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 茂丘西奧和他的兄弟瓦倫丁;我的叔父凱普雷特、他的妻子和女兒們;

passages.original: My fair niece Rosaline and Livia; Signior Valentio and his cousin Tybalt;
passages.vernacular: 我美麗嘅侄女羅瑟琳同莉維婭;瓦倫提奧先生同佢嘅堂弟提伯特;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我美麗的侄女羅瑟琳和莉維婭;瓦倫提奧先生和他的堂弟提伯特;

passages.original: Lucio and the lively Helena.
passages.vernacular: 魯西奧同活潑嘅海倫娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 魯西奧和活潑的海倫娜。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: A fair assembly.
passages.vernacular: 好一個盛會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好一個盛會。

passages.original: [Gives back the paper] Whither should they come?
passages.vernacular: [把紙還畀佢]佢哋到邊度去?
passages.vernacularMandarin: [把紙還給他]他們到哪裡去?

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: Up.
passages.vernacular: 上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上去。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Whither to supper?
passages.vernacular: 到邊度食飯?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到哪裡吃飯?

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: To our house.
passages.vernacular: 到我哋家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到我們家。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Whose house?
passages.vernacular: 邊個家?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰家?

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: My master’s.
passages.vernacular: 我主人家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我主人家。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Indeed I should have ask’d you that before.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,我早該先問你呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,我早該先問你這個。

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: Now I’ll tell you without asking.
passages.vernacular: 而家我唔使問就告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我不用問就告訴你。

passages.original: My master is the great rich Capulet, and if you be not of the house of Montagues, I pray come and crush a cup of wine.
passages.vernacular: 我主人係富有嘅大人物凱普雷特,如果你唔係蒙太古家嘅人,請嚟飲一杯酒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我主人是富有的大人物凱普雷特,如果你不是蒙太古家的人,請來喝一杯酒。

passages.original: Rest you merry.
passages.vernacular: 祝你愉快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 祝你愉快。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: At this same ancient feast of Capulet’s Sups the fair Rosaline whom thou so lov’st;
passages.vernacular: 喺凱普雷特呢場老宴會上,你所愛嘅美麗羅瑟琳都要去赴宴;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在凱普雷特這場老宴會上,你所愛的美麗羅瑟琳也要去赴宴;

passages.original: With all the admired beauties of Verona.
passages.vernacular: 同維洛嗰所有令人讚嘆嘅美人一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 和維洛那所有令人讚嘆的美人一起。

passages.original: Go thither and with unattainted eye, Compare her face with some that I shall show, And I will make thee think thy swan a crow.
passages.vernacular: 到嗰度去,用不帶偏見嘅眼睛,把佢嘅臉同我將指畀你睇嘅幾個比較,我會讓你把你嘅天鵝睇成烏鴉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到那裡去,用不帶偏見的眼睛,把她的臉和我將指給你看的幾個比較,我會讓你把你的天鵝看成烏鴉。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: When the devout religion of mine eye Maintains such falsehood, then turn tears to fire;
passages.vernacular: 當我眼睛虔誠嘅宗教堅持咁樣嘅虛假時,嗰就讓淚水變成火;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我眼睛虔誠的宗教堅持這樣的虛假時,那就讓淚水變成火;

passages.original: And these who, often drown’d, could never die, Transparent heretics, be burnt for liars.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲常常淹沒卻從唔能夠死嘅透明異端,就因講謊被燒死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些常常淹沒卻從不能死的透明異端,就因說謊被燒死。

passages.original: One fairer than my love?
passages.vernacular: 有比我嘅愛人更美嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有比我的愛人更美的?

passages.original: The all-seeing sun Ne’er saw her match since first the world begun.
passages.vernacular: 無所唔見嘅太陽,自從世界開始,就從冇見過佢嘅對手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無所不見的太陽,自從世界開始,就從沒見過她的對手。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Tut, you saw her fair, none else being by, Herself pois’d with herself in either eye:
passages.vernacular: 呸,你睇佢美,因為旁邊冇別人,佢只係喺你兩眼中同自己對秤:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呸,你看她美,因為旁邊沒有別人,她只是在你兩眼中與自己對秤:

passages.original: But in that crystal scales let there be weigh’d Your lady’s love against some other maid That I will show you shining at this feast, And she shall scant show well that now shows best.
passages.vernacular: 不過喺嗰水晶秤盤上,讓你情人嘅愛,同我將喺呢場宴會上指畀你睇嘅另一個少女秤一秤,而家顯得最美嘅佢,會幾乎不顯得好睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過在那水晶秤盤上,讓你情人的愛,與我將在這場宴會上指給你看的另一個少女秤一秤,現在顯得最美的她,會幾乎不顯得好看。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I’ll go along, no such sight to be shown, But to rejoice in splendour of my own.
passages.vernacular: 我跟你去,唔係為睇咁樣嘅景象,而係為欣賞自己愛人嘅光彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我跟你去,不是為看這樣的景象,而是為欣賞自己愛人的光彩。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene III — A Room in Capulet’s House 第一幕第三場:凱普雷特家一室

passages.original: Enter Lady Capulet and Nurse.
passages.vernacular: [凱普雷特夫人同奶媽上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱普雷特夫人與奶媽上。]

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Nurse, where’s my daughter?
passages.vernacular: 奶媽,我女兒喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奶媽,我女兒在哪裡?

passages.original: Call her forth to me.
passages.vernacular: 叫佢出嚟見我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫她出來見我。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Now, by my maidenhead, at twelve year old, I bade her come. What, lamb!
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,憑我十二歲時嘅貞潔,我已叫佢嚟喇。乜嘢,小羊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,憑我十二歲時的貞潔,我已叫她來了。什麼,小羊!

passages.original: What ladybird! God forbid!
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,瓢蟲!上帝保佑!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,瓢蟲!上帝保佑!

passages.original: Where’s this girl?
passages.vernacular: 呢丫頭喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這丫頭在哪裡?

passages.original: What, Juliet!
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,茱麗葉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,茱麗葉!

passages.original: Enter Juliet.
passages.vernacular: [茱麗葉上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茱麗葉上。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: How now, who calls?
passages.vernacular: 點喇,邊個喺叫?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,誰在叫?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Your mother.
passages.vernacular: 你母親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你母親。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Madam, I am here.
passages.vernacular: 母親,我喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 母親,我在這裡。

passages.original: What is your will?
passages.vernacular: 您有乜嘢吩咐?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您有什麼吩咐?

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: This is the matter.
passages.vernacular: 事情係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事情是這樣。

passages.original: Nurse, give leave awhile, We must talk in secret.
passages.vernacular: 奶媽,先離開一會兒,我哋要私下談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奶媽,先離開一會兒,我們要私下談話。

passages.original: Nurse, come back again, I have remember’d me, thou’s hear our counsel.
passages.vernacular: 奶媽,回嚟吧,我想起嚟喇,你都聽聽我哋嘅商議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奶媽,回來吧,我想起來了,你也聽聽我們的商議。

passages.original: Thou knowest my daughter’s of a pretty age.
passages.vernacular: 你知道我女兒到咗不小嘅年紀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道我女兒到了不小的年紀。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Faith, I can tell her age unto an hour.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,我能把佢嘅年紀講到幾點鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,我能把她的年紀說到幾點鐘。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: She’s not fourteen.
passages.vernacular: 佢仲唔到十四歲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她還不到十四歲。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: I’ll lay fourteen of my teeth, And yet, to my teen be it spoken, I have but four, She is not fourteen.
passages.vernacular: 我賭上我嘅十四顆牙,不過講來我痛心,我只剩四顆,佢仲唔到十四歲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我賭上我的十四顆牙,可是說來我痛心,我只剩四顆,她還不到十四歲。

passages.original: How long is it now To Lammas-tide?
passages.vernacular: 而家離收穫節仲有多久?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在離收穫節還有多久?

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: A fortnight and odd days.
passages.vernacular: 一兩個星期零幾天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一兩個星期零幾天。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Even or odd, of all days in the year, Come Lammas Eve at night shall she be fourteen.
passages.vernacular: 單雙不論,一年中所有日子裡,到收穫節前夜,佢就滿十四歲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 單雙不論,一年中所有日子裡,到收穫節前夜,她就滿十四歲了。

passages.original: Susan and she,—God rest all Christian souls!— Were of an age.
passages.vernacular: 蘇珊同佢——願上帝安息所有基督徒嘅靈魂!——同歲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蘇珊和她——願上帝安息所有基督徒的靈魂!——同歲。

passages.original: Well, Susan is with God; She was too good for me.
passages.vernacular: 好吧,蘇珊喺上帝嗰度;佢對我來講太好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,蘇珊在上帝那裡;她對我來說太好了。

passages.original: But as I said, On Lammas Eve at night shall she be fourteen;
passages.vernacular: 但正如我講嘅,收穫節前夜佢就滿十四歲;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但正如我說的,收穫節前夜她就滿十四歲;

passages.original: That shall she, marry; I remember it well.
passages.vernacular: 佢會嘅,講真嘅;我記得清清楚楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會的,說真的;我記得清清楚楚。

passages.original: ’Tis since the earthquake now eleven years; And she was wean’d,—I never shall forget it—, Of all the days of the year, upon that day:
passages.vernacular: 自從嗰次地震已十一年;佢斷奶——我永遠忘不喇——就喺一年中嗰一天:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從那次地震已十一年;她斷奶——我永遠忘不了——就在一年中那一天:

passages.original: For I had then laid wormwood to my dug, Sitting in the sun under the dovehouse wall;
passages.vernacular: 因為嗰時我喺乳頭上抹咗苦艾,坐喺鴿舍牆下嘅太陽裡;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為那時我在乳頭上抹了苦艾,坐在鴿舍牆下的太陽裡;

passages.original: My lord and you were then at Mantua: Nay, I do bear a brain.
passages.vernacular: 您同老爺嗰時喺曼圖亞:不,我記性好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您和老爺那時在曼圖亞:不,我記性好。

passages.original: But as I said, When it did taste the wormwood on the nipple Of my dug and felt it bitter, pretty fool, To see it tetchy, and fall out with the dug!
passages.vernacular: 但正如我講嘅,當佢嘗到我乳頭上嘅苦艾,覺得苦,可愛嘅小傻瓜,睇佢嗰脾氣,跟乳頭鬧翻喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但正如我說的,當她嘗到我乳頭上的苦艾,覺得苦,可愛的小傻瓜,看她那脾氣,跟乳頭鬧翻了!

passages.original: Shake, quoth the dovehouse: ’twas no need, I trow, To bid me trudge.
passages.vernacular: 鴿舍講「搖」:我想,唔使叫我走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鴿舍說「搖」:我想,不用叫我走開。

passages.original: And since that time it is eleven years; For then she could stand alone;
passages.vernacular: 從嗰時起已十一年;因為嗰時佢能自己站立;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從那時起已十一年;因為那時她能自己站立;

passages.original: nay, by th’rood She could have run and waddled all about;
passages.vernacular: 不,憑聖十字架,佢能到處跑住搖搖擺擺;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,憑聖十字架,她能到處跑著搖搖擺擺;

passages.original: For even the day before she broke her brow, And then my husband,—God be with his soul!
passages.vernacular: 因為就喺前一天,佢摔破咗額頭,然後我丈夫——願上帝同佢嘅靈魂同喺!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為就在前一天,她摔破了額頭,然後我丈夫——願上帝與他的靈魂同在!

passages.original: A was a merry man,—took up the child: ‘Yea,’ quoth he, ‘dost thou fall upon thy face?
passages.vernacular: 佢係個快樂嘅人——抱起細路:「係啊,」佢講,「你臉朝下摔嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個快樂的人——抱起孩子:「是啊,」他說,「你臉朝下摔嗎?

passages.original: Thou wilt fall backward when thou hast more wit; Wilt thou not, Jule?’
passages.vernacular: 等你更有智慧喇,你會往後倒;係唔係,茱兒?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等你更有智慧了,你會往後倒;是不是,茱兒?」

passages.original: and, by my holidame, The pretty wretch left crying, and said ‘Ay’.
passages.vernacular: 憑我嘅聖母,嗰可愛嘅小嘢不哭喇,講「係」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑我的聖母,那可愛的小東西不哭了,說「是」。

passages.original: To see now how a jest shall come about.
passages.vernacular: 睇,一個玩笑點就成真喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,一個玩笑怎麼就成真了。

passages.original: I warrant, and I should live a thousand years, I never should forget it.
passages.vernacular: 我保證,就算我活一千年,我都永遠忘不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我保證,就算我活一千年,我也永遠忘不了。

passages.original: ‘Wilt thou not, Jule?’
passages.vernacular: 「係唔係,茱兒?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是不是,茱兒?」

passages.original: quoth he; And, pretty fool, it stinted, and said ‘Ay.’
passages.vernacular: 佢講;可愛嘅小傻瓜,佢止住喇,講「係」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說;可愛的小傻瓜,它止住了,說「是」。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Enough of this; I pray thee hold thy peace.
passages.vernacular: 夠喇;請你唔好講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夠了;請你別說了。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Yes, madam, yet I cannot choose but laugh, To think it should leave crying, and say ‘Ay’;
passages.vernacular: 係,夫人,不過我定係忍不住笑,想到佢竟停止哭泣,講「係」;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,夫人,可是我還是忍不住笑,想到它竟停止哭泣,說「是」;

passages.original: And yet I warrant it had upon it brow A bump as big as a young cockerel’s stone;
passages.vernacular: 而且我保證佢額頭上有個腫包,像小公雞嘅睪丸咁大;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我保證它額頭上有個腫包,像小公雞的睪丸那麼大;

passages.original: A perilous knock, and it cried bitterly.
passages.vernacular: 一個險惡嘅撞擊,佢哭得好傷心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個險惡的撞擊,它哭得很傷心。

passages.original: ‘Yea,’ quoth my husband, ‘fall’st upon thy face?
passages.vernacular: 「係啊,」我丈夫講,「你臉朝下摔嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是啊,」我丈夫說,「你臉朝下摔嗎?

passages.original: Thou wilt fall backward when thou comest to age; Wilt thou not, Jule?’
passages.vernacular: 等你成年咗你會往後倒;係唔係,茱兒?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等你成年了你會往後倒;是不是,茱兒?」

passages.original: it stinted, and said ‘Ay’.
passages.vernacular: 佢止住喇,講「係」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它止住了,說「是」。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: And stint thou too, I pray thee, Nurse, say I.
passages.vernacular: 你都止住吧,奶媽,求你,就講「係」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你也止住吧,奶媽,求你,就說「是」。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Peace, I have done.
passages.vernacular: 安靜,我講完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安靜,我說完了。

passages.original: God mark thee to his grace Thou wast the prettiest babe that e’er I nurs’d:
passages.vernacular: 願上帝標記你得佢嘅恩典!你係我哺育過嘅最漂亮嘅嬰兒:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上帝標記你得他的恩典!你是我哺育過的最漂亮的嬰兒:

passages.original: And I might live to see thee married once, I have my wish.
passages.vernacular: 只要我能活住睇到你結婚一次,我就如願喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要我能活著看到你結婚一次,我就如願了。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Marry, that marry is the very theme I came to talk of.
passages.vernacular: 講到結婚,嗰正是我嚟要談嘅話題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說到結婚,那正是我來要談的話題。

passages.original: Tell me, daughter Juliet, How stands your disposition to be married?
passages.vernacular: 告訴我,女兒茱麗葉,你對結婚嘅心意如何?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴我,女兒茱麗葉,你對結婚的心意如何?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: It is an honour that I dream not of.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係我做夢都冇想過嘅榮譽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是我做夢也沒想過的榮譽。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: An honour!
passages.vernacular: 榮譽!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 榮譽!

passages.original: Were not I thine only nurse, I would say thou hadst suck’d wisdom from thy teat.
passages.vernacular: 要唔係我係你唯一嘅奶媽,我會講你係從奶頭上吸嚟咗智慧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要不是我是你唯一的奶媽,我會說你是從奶頭上吸來了智慧。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Well, think of marriage now: younger than you, Here in Verona, ladies of esteem, Are made already mothers.
passages.vernacular: 好,而家想想結婚:比你年輕嘅,喺呢維洛嗰有地位嘅小姐,已經做咗母親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,現在想想結婚:比你年輕的,在這維洛那有地位的小姐,已經做了母親。

passages.original: By my count I was your mother much upon these years That you are now a maid.
passages.vernacular: 照我嘅算法,我喺你而家定係少女嘅呢個年紀,已經做咗你嘅母親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 照我的算法,我在你現在還是少女的這個年紀,已經做了你的母親。

passages.original: Thus, then, in brief; The valiant Paris seeks you for his love.
passages.vernacular: 咁簡單講:英勇嘅帕里斯要追求你做佢嘅愛人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼簡單說:英勇的帕里斯要追求你做他的愛人。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: A man, young lady!
passages.vernacular: 一個男人,小姐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個男人,小姐!

passages.original: Lady, such a man As all the world—why he’s a man of wax.
passages.vernacular: 小姐,咁樣一個男人,全世界——哎,佢係個蠟做嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姐,這樣一個男人,全世界——哎,他是個蠟做的人。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Verona’s summer hath not such a flower.
passages.vernacular: 維洛嗰嘅夏天冇咁樣嘅花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 維洛那的夏天沒有這樣的花。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Nay, he’s a flower, in faith a very flower.
passages.vernacular: 不,佢係花,講真嘅,係朵真正嘅花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,他是花,說真的,是朵真正的花。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: What say you, can you love the gentleman?
passages.vernacular: 你點講,你能愛呢位紳士嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼說,你能愛這位紳士嗎?

passages.original: This night you shall behold him at our feast;
passages.vernacular: 今晚你會喺我哋嘅宴會上見到佢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晚你會在我們的宴會上見到他;

passages.original: Read o’er the volume of young Paris’ face, And find delight writ there with beauty’s pen.
passages.vernacular: 讀一讀年輕帕里斯面容呢本書,你會發現用美嘅筆寫喺上面嘅歡愉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讀一讀年輕帕里斯面容這本書,你會發現用美的筆寫在上面的歡愉。

passages.original: Examine every married lineament, And see how one another lends content;
passages.vernacular: 審視每一道相配嘅線條,睇佢哋點樣互相畀予滿足;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 審視每一道相配的線條,看它們怎樣互相給予滿足;

passages.original: And what obscur’d in this fair volume lies, Find written in the margent of his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 呢本美麗嘅書中隱藏住嘅嘢,你會喺佢眼睛嘅頁邊找到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這本美麗的書中隱藏著的東西,你會在他眼睛的頁邊找到。

passages.original: This precious book of love, this unbound lover, To beautify him, only lacks a cover:
passages.vernacular: 呢本珍貴嘅愛情之書,呢位冇裝訂嘅情人,要使佢更美,只欠一個封面:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這本珍貴的愛情之書,這位沒裝訂的情人,要使他更美,只欠一個封面:

passages.original: The fish lives in the sea; and ’tis much pride For fair without the fair within to hide.
passages.vernacular: 魚活喺海裡;美麗嘅外表若把內喺嘅美藏起嚟,太驕傲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 魚活在海裡;美麗的外表若把內在的美藏起來,太驕傲了。

passages.original: That book in many’s eyes doth share the glory, That in gold clasps locks in the golden story;
passages.vernacular: 嗰本書喺許多人眼中分享榮耀,因為佢用金扣鎖住金色嘅故事;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那本書在許多人眼中分享榮耀,因為它用金扣鎖住金色的故事;

passages.original: So shall you share all that he doth possess, By having him, making yourself no less.
passages.vernacular: 你都會分享佢擁有嘅一切,得到佢,而你自己並不減少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你也會分享他擁有的一切,得到他,而你自己並不減少。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: No less, nay bigger.
passages.vernacular: 不減少,不,仲會變大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不減少,不,還會變大。

passages.original: Women grow by men.
passages.vernacular: 女人靠男人而變大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女人靠男人而變大。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Speak briefly, can you like of Paris’ love?
passages.vernacular: 簡單講,你能鍾意帕里斯嘅愛嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡單說,你能喜歡帕里斯的愛嗎?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: I’ll look to like, if looking liking move: But no more deep will I endart mine eye Than your consent gives strength to make it fly.
passages.vernacular: 我會去睇睇喜不鍾意,如果睇能引起鍾意:但我嘅眼睛射出嘅箭唔會比您嘅同意畀佢飛嘅力量更深。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會去看看喜不喜歡,如果看能引起喜歡:但我的眼睛射出的箭不會比您的同意給它飛的力量更深。

passages.original: Enter a Servant.
passages.vernacular: [一名僕人上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一名僕人上。]

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: Madam, the guests are come, supper served up, you called, my young lady asked for, the Nurse cursed in the pantry, and everything in extremity.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,客人到喇,晚飯擺好喇,您被叫喇,小姐被問喇,奶媽喺儲藏室被咒罵,一切都亂成一團。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,客人到了,晚飯擺好了,您被叫了,小姐被問了,奶媽在儲藏室被咒罵,一切都亂成一團。

passages.original: I must hence to wait, I beseech you follow straight.
passages.vernacular: 我必須去伺候,請你哋即刻跟嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須去伺候,請你們馬上跟來。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: We follow thee.
passages.vernacular: 我哋跟你嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們跟你來。

passages.original: [Exit Servant.]
passages.vernacular: [僕人下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [僕人下。]

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Juliet, the County stays.
passages.vernacular: 茱麗葉,伯爵喺等住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 茱麗葉,伯爵在等著。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Go, girl, seek happy nights to happy days.
passages.vernacular: 去吧,細路,為快樂嘅日子尋找快樂嘅夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去吧,孩子,為快樂的日子尋找快樂的夜晚。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene IV — A Street 第一幕第四場:街道

passages.original: Enter Romeo, Mercutio, Benvolio, with five or six Maskers; Torch-bearers and others.
passages.vernacular: [羅密歐、茂丘西奧、班伏里奧偕五六個蒙面者、火把手及其他人上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅密歐、茂丘西奧、班伏里奧偕五六個蒙面者、火把手及其他人上。]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: What, shall this speech be spoke for our excuse?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,我哋要念呢段開場白嚟作為藉口嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,我們要念這段開場白來作為藉口嗎?

passages.original: Or shall we on without apology?
passages.vernacular: 定係不加道歉就闖進去?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還是不加道歉就闖進去?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: The date is out of such prolixity: We’ll have no Cupid hoodwink’d with a scarf, Bearing a Tartar’s painted bow of lath, Scaring the ladies like a crow-keeper;
passages.vernacular: 呢種冗長已經過時:我哋唔好蒙住頭巾嘅丘比特,攞住韃靼人嘅塗漆木弓,像稻草人一樣嚇唬女士哋;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種冗長已經過時:我們不要蒙著頭巾的丘比特,拿著韃靼人的塗漆木弓,像稻草人一樣嚇唬女士們;

passages.original: Nor no without-book prologue, faintly spoke After the prompter, for our entrance:
passages.vernacular: 都唔好事先背好、跟喺提詞人後面有氣無力地念嘅開場白,作為我哋嘅入場:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也不要事先背好、跟在提詞人後面有氣無力地念的開場白,作為我們的入場:

passages.original: But let them measure us by what they will, We’ll measure them a measure, and be gone.
passages.vernacular: 讓佢哋隨便點衡量我哋,我哋畀佢哋跳一支舞就走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓他們隨便怎麼衡量我們,我們給他們跳一支舞就走。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Give me a torch, I am not for this ambling; Being but heavy I will bear the light.
passages.vernacular: 畀我一支火把,我不適合呢種蹓躂;我心情沉重,就替你哋擎燈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我一支火把,我不適合這種蹓躂;我心情沉重,就替你們擎燈。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Nay, gentle Romeo, we must have you dance.
passages.vernacular: 不,溫和嘅羅密歐,我哋必須讓你跳舞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,溫和的羅密歐,我們必須讓你跳舞。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Not I, believe me, you have dancing shoes, With nimble soles, I have a soul of lead So stakes me to the ground I cannot move.
passages.vernacular: 我不去,相信我,你哋有跳舞嘅鞋,輕快嘅鞋底,我卻有一個鉛做嘅靈魂,把我釘喺地上,動彈唔得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不去,相信我,你們有跳舞的鞋,輕快的鞋底,我卻有一個鉛做的靈魂,把我釘在地上,動彈不得。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: You are a lover, borrow Cupid’s wings, And soar with them above a common bound.
passages.vernacular: 你係情人,借丘比特嘅翅膀,飛到普通嘅界限之上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是情人,借丘比特的翅膀,飛到普通的界限之上。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I am too sore enpierced with his shaft To soar with his light feathers, and so bound, I cannot bound a pitch above dull woe.
passages.vernacular: 我被佢嘅箭傷得太重,無法用佢輕盈嘅羽毛飛翔,又被束縛,唔能夠高於沉悶嘅悲傷一個音調。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被他的箭傷得太重,無法用他輕盈的羽毛飛翔,又被束縛,不能高於沉悶的悲傷一個音調。

passages.original: Under love’s heavy burden do I sink.
passages.vernacular: 我喺愛情嘅沉重負擔下下沉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在愛情的沉重負擔下下沉。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: And, to sink in it, should you burden love; Too great oppression for a tender thing.
passages.vernacular: 你若下沉其中,就係畀愛情加咗負擔;對一個溫柔嘅嘢壓得太重喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你若下沉其中,就是給愛情加了負擔;對一個溫柔的東西壓得太重了。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Is love a tender thing?
passages.vernacular: 愛情係溫柔嘅嘢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛情是溫柔的東西嗎?

passages.original: It is too rough, Too rude, too boisterous; and it pricks like thorn.
passages.vernacular: 佢太粗暴、太粗魯、太喧鬧,而且像荊棘一樣刺人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它太粗暴、太粗魯、太喧鬧,而且像荊棘一樣刺人。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: If love be rough with you, be rough with love;
passages.vernacular: 如果愛情對你粗暴,你就對愛情粗暴;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果愛情對你粗暴,你就對愛情粗暴;

passages.original: Prick love for pricking, and you beat love down.
passages.vernacular: 因為被刺而刺愛情,你就把愛情打倒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為被刺而刺愛情,你就把愛情打倒了。

passages.original: Give me a case to put my visage in: [Putting on a mask.]
passages.vernacular: 畀我一個面具嚟裝我嘅臉:[戴上面具。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我一個面具來裝我的臉:[戴上面具。]

passages.original: A visor for a visor.
passages.vernacular: 一個面具蓋一個面具。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個面具蓋一個面具。

passages.original: What care I What curious eye doth quote deformities?
passages.vernacular: 我在乎乜嘢好奇嘅眼睛會注意到我嘅醜陋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在乎什麼好奇的眼睛會注意到我的醜陋?

passages.original: Here are the beetle-brows shall blush for me.
passages.vernacular: 呢度有濃眉嘅面具替我臉紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡有濃眉的面具替我臉紅。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Come, knock and enter; and no sooner in But every man betake him to his legs.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,敲門進去;一進去,每個人就都用腿跳起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,敲門進去;一進去,每個人就都用腿跳起來。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: A torch for me: let wantons, light of heart, Tickle the senseless rushes with their heels;
passages.vernacular: 畀我一支火把:讓輕浮嘅、心輕嘅人用腳跟去搔無知覺嘅蘆席;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我一支火把:讓輕浮的、心輕的人用腳跟去搔無知覺的蘆席;

passages.original: For I am proverb’d with a grandsire phrase, I’ll be a candle-holder and look on, The game was ne’er so fair, and I am done.
passages.vernacular: 因為我被一句祖父嘅諺語所束縛,我要做執燈嘅旁觀者:遊戲從冇咁好過,我要收手喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我被一句祖父的諺語所束縛,我要做執燈的旁觀者:遊戲從沒這麼好過,我要收手了。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Tut, dun’s the mouse, the constable’s own word:
passages.vernacular: 呸,「老鼠係灰褐色嘅」,呢個係巡警自己嘅話:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呸,「老鼠是灰褐色的」,這是巡警自己的話:

passages.original: If thou art dun, we’ll draw thee from the mire Or save your reverence love, wherein thou stickest Up to the ears.
passages.vernacular: 如果你係灰褐色(死氣沉沉),我哋就把你從泥沼中拉出嚟,或者,恕我直言,從愛情中拉出嚟,你正陷喺裡面直到耳朵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你是灰褐色(死氣沉沉),我們就把你從泥沼中拉出來,或者,恕我直言,從愛情中拉出來,你正陷在裡面直到耳朵。

passages.original: Come, we burn daylight, ho.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,我哋喺白白燒日光,喂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我們在白白燒日光,喂。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Nay, that’s not so.
passages.vernacular: 不,唔係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,不是這樣。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: I mean sir, in delay We waste our lights in vain, light lights by day.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅意思係,先生,拖延會讓我哋白白浪費燈火,像喺白天點燈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的意思是,先生,拖延會讓我們白白浪費燈火,像在白天點燈。

passages.original: Take our good meaning, for our judgment sits Five times in that ere once in our five wits.
passages.vernacular: 領會我哋嘅好意,因為我哋嘅判斷喺呢上面坐咗五次,才喺五種智慧中坐一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 領會我們的好意,因為我們的判斷在這上面坐了五次,才在五種智慧中坐一次。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: And we mean well in going to this mask; But ’tis no wit to go.
passages.vernacular: 我哋去呢個化裝舞會係好意;但去並不明智。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們去這個化裝舞會是好意;但去並不明智。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Why, may one ask?
passages.vernacular: 點解,可以問嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼,可以問嗎?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I dreamt a dream tonight.
passages.vernacular: 我今晚做咗個夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我今晚做了個夢。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: And so did I.
passages.vernacular: 我都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也是。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Well what was yours?
passages.vernacular: 好,你嘅係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,你的是什麼?

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: That dreamers often lie.
passages.vernacular: 做夢嘅人常常講謊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 做夢的人常常說謊。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: In bed asleep, while they do dream things true.
passages.vernacular: 喺床上瞓住時,佢哋夢見嘅事卻係真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在床上睡著時,他們夢見的事卻是真的。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: O, then, I see Queen Mab hath been with you.
passages.vernacular: 啊,咁,我睇麥布女王曾經光顧你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,那麼,我看麥布女王曾經光顧你。

passages.original: She is the fairies’ midwife, and she comes In shape no bigger than an agate-stone On the fore-finger of an alderman, Drawn with a team of little atomies Over men’s noses as they lie asleep:
passages.vernacular: 佢係仙子嘅接生婆,佢嚟時身形不比市議員食指上嘅瑪瑙石大,由一隊小小嘅微粒拉住,喺人哋瞓覺時越過佢哋嘅鼻子:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是仙子的接生婆,她來時身形不比市議員食指上的瑪瑙石大,由一隊小小的微粒拉著,在人們睡覺時越過他們的鼻子:

passages.original: Her waggon-spokes made of long spinners’ legs;
passages.vernacular: 佢車輪嘅輻條係長腿蜘蛛嘅腿做嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她車輪的輻條是長腿蜘蛛的腿做的;

passages.original: The cover, of the wings of grasshoppers; Her traces, of the smallest spider’s web;
passages.vernacular: 車篷係蚱蜢嘅翅膀;佢嘅韁繩係最小嘅蜘蛛網;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 車篷是蚱蜢的翅膀;她的韁繩是最小的蜘蛛網;

passages.original: The collars, of the moonshine’s watery beams;
passages.vernacular: 項圈係月光嘅水汪汪嘅光線;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 項圈是月光的水汪汪的光線;

passages.original: Her whip of cricket’s bone; the lash, of film;
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅鞭子係蟋蟀嘅骨頭;鞭梢係薄膜;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的鞭子是蟋蟀的骨頭;鞭梢是薄膜;

passages.original: Her waggoner, a small grey-coated gnat, Not half so big as a round little worm Prick’d from the lazy finger of a maid:
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅車夫係一隻灰衣小蚊子,仲唔到從懶惰少女手指上挑出嘅圓小蟲嘅一半大:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的車夫是一隻灰衣小蚊子,還不到從懶惰少女手指上挑出的圓小蟲的一半大:

passages.original: Her chariot is an empty hazelnut, Made by the joiner squirrel or old grub, Time out o’ mind the fairies’ coachmakers.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅馬車係個空榛子殼,由細木匠松鼠或老蛆製造,自古以來就係仙子嘅造車匠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的馬車是個空榛子殼,由細木匠松鼠或老蛆製造,自古以來就是仙子的造車匠。

passages.original: And in this state she gallops night by night Through lovers’ brains, and then they dream of love;
passages.vernacular: 佢就咁樣威風地夜復一夜馳過戀人嘅腦子,佢哋於是夢見愛情;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她就這樣威風地夜復一夜馳過戀人的腦子,他們於是夢見愛情;

passages.original: O’er courtiers’ knees, that dream on curtsies straight;
passages.vernacular: 馳過朝臣嘅膝蓋,佢哋即刻夢見行禮;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馳過朝臣的膝蓋,他們立刻夢見行禮;

passages.original: O’er lawyers’ fingers, who straight dream on fees;
passages.vernacular: 馳過律師嘅手指,佢哋即刻夢見酬金;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馳過律師的手指,他們立刻夢見酬金;

passages.original: O’er ladies’ lips, who straight on kisses dream, Which oft the angry Mab with blisters plagues, Because their breaths with sweetmeats tainted are:
passages.vernacular: 馳過女士嘅嘴唇,佢哋即刻夢見親吻,而憤怒嘅麥布常用水泡折磨佢哋,因為佢哋嘅呼吸被糖果污染喇:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馳過女士的嘴唇,她們立刻夢見親吻,而憤怒的麥布常用水泡折磨它們,因為她們的呼吸被糖果污染了:

passages.original: Sometime she gallops o’er a courtier’s nose, And then dreams he of smelling out a suit;
passages.vernacular: 有時佢馳過朝臣嘅鼻子,佢就夢見嗅出一個差事;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時她馳過朝臣的鼻子,他就夢見嗅出一個差事;

passages.original: And sometime comes she with a tithe-pig’s tail, Tickling a parson’s nose as a lies asleep, Then dreams he of another benefice:
passages.vernacular: 有時佢帶住什一稅豬嘅尾巴嚟,搔住瞓住嘅牧師嘅鼻子,佢就夢見另一個牧師職位:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時她帶著什一稅豬的尾巴來,搔著睡著的牧師的鼻子,他就夢見另一個牧師職位:

passages.original: Sometime she driveth o’er a soldier’s neck, And then dreams he of cutting foreign throats, Of breaches, ambuscados, Spanish blades, Of healths five fathom deep;
passages.vernacular: 有時佢駛過士兵嘅脖子,佢就夢見割外國人嘅喉嚨,夢見突破口、伏擊、西班牙劍、五噚深嘅乾杯;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時她駛過士兵的脖子,他就夢見割外國人的喉嚨,夢見突破口、伏擊、西班牙劍、五噚深的乾杯;

passages.original: and then anon Drums in his ear, at which he starts and wakes;
passages.vernacular: 然後即刻喺佢耳中擂鼓,佢被驚醒跳起;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後立刻在他耳中擂鼓,他被驚醒跳起;

passages.original: And, being thus frighted, swears a prayer or two, And sleeps again.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣受驚之後,佢念一兩句禱告,又瞓住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣受驚之後,他念一兩句禱告,又睡著。

passages.original: This is that very Mab That plats the manes of horses in the night;
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係嗰個麥布,喺夜裡把馬鬃編成辮子;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是那個麥布,在夜裡把馬鬃編成辮子;

passages.original: And bakes the elf-locks in foul sluttish hairs, Which, once untangled, much misfortune bodes:
passages.vernacular: 把污穢邋遢頭髮烤成精靈結,一旦解開,就預示許多不幸:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把污穢邋遢頭髮烤成精靈結,一旦解開,就預示許多不幸:

passages.original: This is the hag, when maids lie on their backs, That presses them, and learns them first to bear, Making them women of good carriage: This is she,—
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係嗰個老妖婆,當少女仰臥時,壓住佢哋,教佢哋第一次承受,使佢哋成為舉止得體嘅女人:呢個就係佢,——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是那個老妖婆,當少女仰臥時,壓著她們,教她們第一次承受,使她們成為舉止得體的女人:這就是她,——

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Peace, peace, Mercutio, peace, Thou talk’st of nothing.
passages.vernacular: 住口,住口,茂丘西奧,住口,你講嘅係無稽之談。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 住口,住口,茂丘西奧,住口,你說的是無稽之談。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: True, I talk of dreams, Which are the children of an idle brain, Begot of nothing but vain fantasy, Which is as thin of substance as the air, And more inconstant than the wind, who woos Even now the frozen bosom of the north, And, being anger’d, puffs away from thence, Turning his side to the dew-dropping south.
passages.vernacular: 對,我講嘅係夢,夢係閒散頭腦嘅細路,只由虛妄嘅幻想所生,佢嘅實質像空氣一樣稀薄,比風仲不定,風正在追求北方冰凍嘅胸膛,一發怒就從嗰度吹走,轉過身對住滴露嘅南方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,我說的是夢,夢是閒散頭腦的孩子,只由虛妄的幻想所生,它的實質像空氣一樣稀薄,比風還不定,風正在追求北方冰凍的胸膛,一發怒就從那裡吹走,轉過身對著滴露的南方。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: This wind you talk of blows us from ourselves:
passages.vernacular: 你講嘅呢風把我哋從自己身邊吹走:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說的這風把我們從自己身邊吹走:

passages.original: Supper is done, and we shall come too late.
passages.vernacular: 晚飯已食完,我哋要遲到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚飯已吃完,我們要遲到了。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I fear too early: for my mind misgives Some consequence yet hanging in the stars, Shall bitterly begin his fearful date With this night’s revels;
passages.vernacular: 我怕係太早:因為我心裡有預感,有某種後果仍懸喺星辰裡,將喺今夜嘅狂歡中痛苦地開始佢可怕嘅紀年;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕是太早:因為我心裡有預感,有某種後果仍懸在星辰裡,將在今夜的狂歡中痛苦地開始它可怕的紀年;

passages.original: and expire the term Of a despised life, clos’d in my breast By some vile forfeit of untimely death.
passages.vernacular: 並喺我胸中禁閉嘅可鄙生命嘅期限,因某種可恥嘅過早死亡嘅喪失而終結。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並在我胸中禁閉的可鄙生命的期限,因某種可恥的過早死亡的喪失而終結。

passages.original: But he that hath the steerage of my course Direct my suit.
passages.vernacular: 但願掌管我航程嘅嗰一位指引我嘅行動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但願掌管我航程的那一位指引我的行動。

passages.original: On, lusty gentlemen!
passages.vernacular: 前進,勇敢嘅先生哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 前進,勇敢的先生們!

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Strike, drum.
passages.vernacular: 擊鼓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 擊鼓。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene V — A Hall in Capulet’s House 第一幕第五場:凱普雷特家大廳

passages.original: Musicians waiting. Enter Servants.
passages.vernacular: [樂師哋等候。僕人哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [樂師們等候。僕人們上。]

passages.title: First Servant 第一僕人
passages.original: Where’s Potpan, that he helps not to take away?
passages.vernacular: 帕特潘喺邊度,佢點不嚟幫忙收拾?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帕特潘在哪裡,他怎麼不來幫忙收拾?

passages.original: He shift a trencher!
passages.vernacular: 佢嚟挪盤子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他來挪盤子!

passages.original: He scrape a trencher!
passages.vernacular: 佢嚟刮盤子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他來刮盤子!

passages.title: Second Servant 第二僕人
passages.original: When good manners shall lie all in one or two men’s hands, and they unwash’d too, ’tis a foul thing.
passages.vernacular: 當禮貌全落喺一兩個人手上,而且手仲冇洗,嗰就太討厭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當禮貌全落在一兩個人手上,而且手還沒洗,那就太討厭了。

passages.title: First Servant 第一僕人
passages.original: Away with the join-stools, remove the court-cupboard, look to the plate.
passages.vernacular: 把長凳撤走,把櫥櫃搬開,睇好銀器。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把長凳撤走,把櫥櫃搬開,看好銀器。

passages.original: Good thou, save me a piece of marchpane; and as thou loves me, let the porter let in Susan Grindstone and Nell.
passages.vernacular: 好心人,替我留一塊杏仁糖;睇喺你愛我嘅份上,叫門房放蘇珊·磨石同內爾進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好心人,替我留一塊杏仁糖;看在你愛我的份上,叫門房放蘇珊·磨石和內爾進來。

passages.original: Antony and Potpan!
passages.vernacular: 安東尼同帕特潘!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安東尼和帕特潘!

passages.title: Second Servant 第二僕人
passages.original: Ay, boy, ready.
passages.vernacular: 喺,小子,嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在,小子,來了。

passages.title: First Servant 第一僕人
passages.original: You are looked for and called for, asked for and sought for, in the great chamber.
passages.vernacular: 大廳裡有人找你哋、叫你哋、問你哋、尋你哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大廳裡有人找你們、叫你們、問你們、尋你們。

passages.title: Second Servant 第二僕人
passages.original: We cannot be here and there too.
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔能夠同時喺呢兒同嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不能同時在這兒和那兒。

passages.original: Cheerly, boys.
passages.vernacular: 打起精神嚟,小子哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 打起精神來,小子們。

passages.original: Be brisk awhile, and the longer liver take all.
passages.vernacular: 活躍一陣子,活得長嘅人攞走一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 活躍一陣子,活得長的人拿走一切。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

passages.original: Enter Capulet, &c. with the Guests and Gentlewomen to the Maskers.
passages.vernacular: [凱普雷特等偕客人同女士哋迎接蒙面者上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱普雷特等偕客人和女士們迎接蒙面者上。]

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Welcome, gentlemen, ladies that have their toes Unplagu’d with corns will have a bout with you.
passages.vernacular: 歡迎,先生哋,腳趾冇被雞眼折磨嘅女士哋會跟你哋跳一輪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎,先生們,腳趾沒被雞眼折磨的女士們會跟你們跳一輪。

passages.original: Ah my mistresses, which of you all Will now deny to dance?
passages.vernacular: 啊,我嘅小姐哋,你哋邊一位而家會拒絕跳舞?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我的小姐們,你們哪一位現在會拒絕跳舞?

passages.original: She that makes dainty, She I’ll swear hath corns.
passages.vernacular: 裝模作樣嘅嗰位,我敢發誓佢有雞眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 裝模作樣的那位,我敢發誓她有雞眼。

passages.original: Am I come near ye now?
passages.vernacular: 我而家講到點子上咗吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在說到點子上了吧?

passages.original: Welcome, gentlemen!
passages.vernacular: 歡迎,先生哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎,先生們!

passages.original: I have seen the day That I have worn a visor, and could tell A whispering tale in a fair lady’s ear, Such as would please;
passages.vernacular: 我見過嗰樣嘅日子,我都戴過面具,能喺美麗女士耳邊講悄悄話,講得動聽:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我見過那樣的日子,我也戴過面具,能在美麗女士耳邊說悄悄話,說得動聽:

passages.original: ’tis gone, ’tis gone, ’tis gone, You are welcome, gentlemen!
