passages.vernacular: 都過去喇,過去喇,過去喇,歡迎,先生哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 都過去了,過去了,過去了,歡迎,先生們!

passages.original: Come, musicians, play.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,樂師,奏樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,樂師,奏樂。

passages.original: A hall, a hall, give room!
passages.vernacular: 讓出大廳,讓出大廳,讓點地方!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓出大廳,讓出大廳,讓點地方!

passages.original: And foot it, girls.
passages.vernacular: 跳吧,姑娘哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跳吧,姑娘們。

passages.original: [Music plays, and they dance.]
passages.vernacular: [奏樂,眾人跳舞。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奏樂,眾人跳舞。]

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: More light, you knaves; and turn the tables up, And quench the fire, the room is grown too hot.
passages.vernacular: 多點燈光,你哋呢啲傢伙;把桌子翻起嚟,熄掉火,房間太熱喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多點燈光,你們這些傢伙;把桌子翻起來,熄掉火,房間太熱了。

passages.original: Ah sirrah, this unlook’d-for sport comes well.
passages.vernacular: 啊,老兄,呢意外嘅娛樂嚟得正好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,老兄,這意外的娛樂來得正好。

passages.original: Nay sit, nay sit, good cousin Capulet, For you and I are past our dancing days;
passages.vernacular: 不,坐,坐,好堂兄凱普雷特,因為你同我都過咗跳舞嘅年紀;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,坐,坐,好堂兄凱普雷特,因為你和我都過了跳舞的年紀;

passages.original: How long is’t now since last yourself and I Were in a mask?
passages.vernacular: 從你我上次戴面具到而家有多久喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從你我上次戴面具到現在有多久了?

passages.title: Capulet’s Cousin 凱普雷特的堂兄
passages.original: By’r Lady, thirty years.
passages.vernacular: 憑聖母,三十年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑聖母,三十年。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: What, man, ’tis not so much, ’tis not so much:
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,老兄,冇咁久,冇咁久:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,老兄,沒有那麼久,沒有那麼久:

passages.original: ’Tis since the nuptial of Lucentio, Come Pentecost as quickly as it will, Some five and twenty years; and then we mask’d.
passages.vernacular: 從盧森提奧嘅婚禮算起,不論聖靈降臨節嚟得多快,大約二十五年;嗰時我哋戴過面具。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從盧森提奧的婚禮算起,不論聖靈降臨節來得多快,大約二十五年;那時我們戴過面具。

passages.title: Capulet’s Cousin 凱普雷特的堂兄
passages.original: ’Tis more, ’tis more, his son is elder, sir; His son is thirty.
passages.vernacular: 比嗰更久,更久,佢嘅兒子更年長,先生;佢兒子三十歲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比那更久,更久,他的兒子更年長,先生;他兒子三十歲了。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Will you tell me that?
passages.vernacular: 你咁樣告訴我?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這樣告訴我?

passages.original: His son was but a ward two years ago.
passages.vernacular: 佢兒子兩年前定係個被監護人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他兒子兩年前還是個被監護人。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: What lady is that, which doth enrich the hand Of yonder knight?
passages.vernacular: 嗰位女士係邊個,佢使嗰邊騎士嘅手增光?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位女士是誰,她使那邊騎士的手增光?

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: I know not, sir.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道,先生。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: O, she doth teach the torches to burn bright!
passages.vernacular: 啊,佢教火把燃燒得更明亮!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,她教火把燃燒得更明亮!

passages.original: It seems she hangs upon the cheek of night As a rich jewel in an Ethiop’s ear;
passages.vernacular: 佢似乎掛喺夜嘅臉頰上,像衣索比亞人耳上嘅珍貴寶石;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她似乎掛在夜的臉頰上,像衣索比亞人耳上的珍貴寶石;

passages.original: Beauty too rich for use, for earth too dear!
passages.vernacular: 美太珍貴,不宜使用,對塵世太貴重!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美太珍貴,不宜使用,對塵世太貴重!

passages.original: So shows a snowy dove trooping with crows As yonder lady o’er her fellows shows.
passages.vernacular: 就像雪白嘅鴿子雜喺烏鴉中,嗰邊嗰位女士喺佢嘅同伴中就係咁樣顯眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就像雪白的鴿子雜在烏鴉中,那邊那位女士在她的同伴中就是這樣顯眼。

passages.original: The measure done, I’ll watch her place of stand, And touching hers, make blessed my rude hand.
passages.vernacular: 舞曲結束,我要觀察佢站嘅地方,觸碰佢嘅手,使我粗魯嘅手受到祝福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 舞曲結束,我要觀察她站的地方,觸碰她的手,使我粗魯的手受到祝福。

passages.original: Did my heart love till now?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅心直到而家才算愛過嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的心直到現在才算愛過嗎?

passages.original: Forswear it, sight!
passages.vernacular: 發誓否認吧,眼睛!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 發誓否認吧,眼睛!

passages.original: For I ne’er saw true beauty till this night.
passages.vernacular: 因為我直到今夜才見過真正嘅美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我直到今夜才見過真正的美。

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: This by his voice, should be a Montague.
passages.vernacular: 從聲音聽嚟,呢應係個蒙太古。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從聲音聽來,這應是個蒙太古。

passages.original: Fetch me my rapier, boy.
passages.vernacular: 畀我攞我嘅長劍嚟,細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我拿我的長劍來,孩子。

passages.original: What, dares the slave Come hither, cover’d with an antic face, To fleer and scorn at our solemnity?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,呢奴才竟敢蒙住古怪嘅臉嚟到呢度,嘲笑我哋嘅盛典?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,這奴才竟敢蒙著古怪的臉來到這裡,嘲笑我們的盛典?

passages.original: Now by the stock and honour of my kin, To strike him dead I hold it not a sin.
passages.vernacular: 憑我家族嘅根源同榮譽,我認為把佢打死不算罪過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑我家族的根源和榮譽,我認為把他打死不算罪過。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Why how now, kinsman!
passages.vernacular: 點喇,親戚!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,親戚!

passages.original: Wherefore storm you so?
passages.vernacular: 你點解咁樣大發雷霆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼這樣大發雷霆?

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: Uncle, this is a Montague, our foe; A villain that is hither come in spite, To scorn at our solemnity this night.
passages.vernacular: 叔叔,呢個係個蒙太古,我哋嘅仇人;一個故意嚟呢度嘅惡棍,今夜嚟嘲笑我哋嘅盛典。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叔叔,這是個蒙太古,我們的仇人;一個故意來這裡的惡棍,今夜來嘲笑我們的盛典。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Young Romeo, is it?
passages.vernacular: 係年輕嘅羅密歐嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是年輕的羅密歐嗎?

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: ’Tis he, that villain Romeo.
passages.vernacular: 就係佢,嗰惡棍羅密歐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是他,那惡棍羅密歐。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Content thee, gentle coz, let him alone, A bears him like a portly gentleman;
passages.vernacular: 冷靜,好堂弟,別管佢;佢舉止像個高貴嘅紳士;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冷靜,好堂弟,別管他;他舉止像個高貴的紳士;

passages.original: And, to say truth, Verona brags of him To be a virtuous and well-govern’d youth.
passages.vernacular: 講實話,維洛嗰都誇佢係個有德行、教養好嘅青年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說實話,維洛那都誇他是個有德行、教養好的青年。

passages.original: I would not for the wealth of all the town Here in my house do him disparagement.
passages.vernacular: 就算畀我全城嘅財富,我都唔願喺我家裡羞辱佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就算給我全城的財富,我也不願在我家裡羞辱他。

passages.original: Therefore be patient, take no note of him, It is my will;
passages.vernacular: 所以要忍耐,唔好理會佢,呢個係我嘅意願;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以要忍耐,不要理會他,這是我的意願;

passages.original: the which if thou respect, Show a fair presence and put off these frowns, An ill-beseeming semblance for a feast.
passages.vernacular: 你若尊重佢,就顯出和藹嘅樣子,收起呢啲皺眉,呢喺宴會上係不合適嘅神色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你若尊重它,就顯出和藹的樣子,收起這些皺眉,這在宴會上是不合適的神色。

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: It fits when such a villain is a guest: I’ll not endure him.
passages.vernacular: 當咁樣嘅惡棍做客人時,佢就合適:我唔能夠容忍佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當這樣的惡棍做客人時,它就合適:我不能容忍他。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: He shall be endur’d.
passages.vernacular: 佢必須被容忍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他必須被容忍。

passages.original: What, goodman boy!
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,好漢小子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,好漢小子!

passages.original: I say he shall, go to; Am I the master here, or you? Go to.
passages.vernacular: 我講佢必須,去;呢度我係主人,定係你?去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說他必須,去;這裡我是主人,還是你?去。

passages.original: You’ll not endure him!
passages.vernacular: 你唔容忍佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不容忍他!

passages.original: God shall mend my soul, You’ll make a mutiny among my guests!
passages.vernacular: 上帝嚟改正我嘅靈魂,你要喺我嘅客人中間掀起暴動!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上帝來改正我的靈魂,你要在我的客人中間掀起暴動!

passages.original: You will set cock-a-hoop, you’ll be the man!
passages.vernacular: 你要逞強,你要當大人物!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要逞強,你要當大人物!

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: Why, uncle, ’tis a shame.
passages.vernacular: 唉,叔叔,呢個係恥辱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,叔叔,這是恥辱。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Go to, go to!
passages.vernacular: 去,去!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,去!

passages.original: You are a saucy boy.
passages.vernacular: 你係個無禮嘅小子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是個無禮的小子。

passages.original: Is’t so, indeed?
passages.vernacular: 真嘅係咁樣嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真的是這樣嗎?

passages.original: This trick may chance to scathe you, I know what.
passages.vernacular: 呢種把戲或者會傷到你,我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種把戲也許會傷到你,我知道。

passages.original: You must contrary me!
passages.vernacular: 你一定要頂撞我!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一定要頂撞我!

passages.original: Marry, ’tis time.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,係時候喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,是時候了。

passages.original: Well said, my hearts!—You are a princox; go: Be quiet, or—More light, more light!—For shame!
passages.vernacular: 講得好,我嘅好小子哋!——你係個自大嘅毛頭小子;去:安靜些,否則——多點燈,多點燈!——真丟臉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說得好,我的好小子們!——你是個自大的毛頭小子;去:安靜些,否則——多點燈,多點燈!——真丟臉!

passages.original: I’ll make you quiet.
passages.vernacular: 我要讓你安靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要讓你安靜。

passages.original: What, cheerly, my hearts.
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,打起精神,我嘅好小子哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,打起精神,我的好小子們。

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: Patience perforce with wilful choler meeting Makes my flesh tremble in their different greeting.
passages.vernacular: 強迫嘅忍耐同任性嘅憤怒相遇,使我嘅肉身喺佢哋不同嘅碰面中顫抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 強迫的忍耐與任性的憤怒相遇,使我的肉身在它們不同的碰面中顫抖。

passages.original: I will withdraw: but this intrusion shall, Now seeming sweet, convert to bitter gall.
passages.vernacular: 我要退下:但呢次闖入,而家睇似甜蜜,將轉為苦澀嘅膽汁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要退下:但這次闖入,現在看似甜蜜,將轉為苦澀的膽汁。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: [To Juliet.]
passages.vernacular: [對茱麗葉。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對茱麗葉。]

passages.original: If I profane with my unworthiest hand This holy shrine, the gentle sin is this, My lips, two blushing pilgrims, ready stand To smooth that rough touch with a tender kiss.
passages.vernacular: 如果我用我最不配嘅手褻瀆咗呢座神聖嘅聖殿,呢溫柔嘅罪係咁樣嘅:我嘅嘴唇,兩個臉紅嘅朝聖者,準備好用溫柔嘅一吻嚟撫平嗰粗魯嘅觸碰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我用我最不配的手褻瀆了這座神聖的聖殿,這溫柔的罪是這樣的:我的嘴唇,兩個臉紅的朝聖者,準備好用溫柔的一吻來撫平那粗魯的觸碰。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Good pilgrim, you do wrong your hand too much, Which mannerly devotion shows in this;
passages.vernacular: 好朝聖者,你太委屈你嘅手喇,佢喺呢件事上表現出有禮嘅虔誠;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好朝聖者,你太委屈你的手了,它在這件事上表現出有禮的虔誠;

passages.original: For saints have hands that pilgrims’ hands do touch, And palm to palm is holy palmers’ kiss.
passages.vernacular: 因為聖徒有手,讓朝聖者嘅手碰觸,掌心貼掌心就係虔誠朝聖者嘅親吻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為聖徒有手,讓朝聖者的手碰觸,掌心貼掌心就是虔誠朝聖者的親吻。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Have not saints lips, and holy palmers too?
passages.vernacular: 聖徒冇嘴唇嗎,虔誠嘅朝聖者都冇嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖徒沒有嘴唇嗎,虔誠的朝聖者也沒有嗎?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Ay, pilgrim, lips that they must use in prayer.
passages.vernacular: 有,朝聖者,係佢哋必須用嚟祈禱嘅嘴唇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有,朝聖者,是他們必須用來祈禱的嘴唇。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: O, then, dear saint, let lips do what hands do:
passages.vernacular: 啊,咁,親愛嘅聖徒,讓嘴唇做手所做嘅吧:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,那麼,親愛的聖徒,讓嘴唇做手所做的吧:

passages.original: They pray, grant thou, lest faith turn to despair.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺祈禱,請你應允,以免信仰變成絕望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們在祈禱,請你應允,以免信仰變成絕望。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Saints do not move, though grant for prayers’ sake.
passages.vernacular: 聖徒不動,雖然為祈禱嘅緣故會應允。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖徒不動,雖然為祈禱的緣故會應允。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Then move not while my prayer’s effect I take.
passages.vernacular: 咁別動,我嚟領取我祈禱嘅成果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼別動,我來領取我祈禱的成果。

passages.original: Thus from my lips, by thine my sin is purg’d.
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣,從我嘅嘴唇,通過你嘅,我嘅罪被洗淨喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣,從我的嘴唇,通過你的,我的罪被洗淨了。

passages.original: [Kissing her.]
passages.vernacular: [吻佢。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [吻她。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Then have my lips the sin that they have took.
passages.vernacular: 咁我嘅嘴唇沾上咗佢哋取走嘅罪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼我的嘴唇沾上了它們取走的罪。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Sin from my lips?
passages.vernacular: 從我嘅嘴唇嚟嘅罪?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從我的嘴唇來的罪?

passages.original: O trespass sweetly urg’d!
passages.vernacular: 啊,被甜蜜地催促嘅過錯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,被甜蜜地催促的過錯!

passages.original: Give me my sin again.
passages.vernacular: 把我嘅罪還畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把我的罪還給我。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: You kiss by the book.
passages.vernacular: 你吻得像照書本。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你吻得像照書本。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Madam, your mother craves a word with you.
passages.vernacular: 小姐,你母親要跟你講句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姐,你母親要跟你說句話。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: What is her mother?
passages.vernacular: 佢母親係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她母親是誰?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Marry, bachelor, Her mother is the lady of the house, And a good lady, and a wise and virtuous.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,單身漢,佢母親係呢家嘅女主人,係位好夫人,聰明又有德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,單身漢,她母親是這家的女主人,是位好夫人,聰明又有德。

passages.original: I nurs’d her daughter that you talk’d withal.
passages.vernacular: 你頭先跟佢講話嘅嗰個女兒,係我奶大嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你剛才跟她說話的那個女兒,是我奶大的。

passages.original: I tell you, he that can lay hold of her Shall have the chinks.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴你,邊個能抓住佢,就能得到錢財。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴你,誰能抓住她,就能得到錢財。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Is she a Capulet?
passages.vernacular: 佢係凱普雷特家嘅人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是凱普雷特家的人嗎?

passages.original: O dear account!
passages.vernacular: 啊,可貴嘅代價!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,可貴的代價!

passages.original: My life is my foe’s debt.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅命係我仇人嘅債。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的命是我仇人的債。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Away, be gone; the sport is at the best.
passages.vernacular: 走吧,離開;樂子正好嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走吧,離開;樂子正好的時候。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Ay, so I fear; the more is my unrest.
passages.vernacular: 對,我怕係咁樣;我越發不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,我怕是這樣;我越發不安。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Nay, gentlemen, prepare not to be gone, We have a trifling foolish banquet towards.
passages.vernacular: 不,先生哋,別準備走,我哋仲有一頓小小嘅、不值錢嘅點心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,先生們,別準備走,我們還有一頓小小的、不值錢的點心。

passages.original: Is it e’en so?
passages.vernacular: 真嘅係咁樣嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真的是這樣嗎?

passages.original: Why then, I thank you all; I thank you, honest gentlemen; good night.
passages.vernacular: 咁,我感謝你哋所有人;我感謝你哋,誠實嘅先生哋;晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,我感謝你們所有人;我感謝你們,誠實的先生們;晚安。

passages.original: More torches here!
passages.vernacular: 呢度多攞些火把嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡多拿些火把來!

passages.original: Come on then, let’s to bed.
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧,我哋去瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧,我們去睡覺。

passages.original: Ah, sirrah, by my fay, it waxes late, I’ll to my rest.
passages.vernacular: 啊,老兄,憑我嘅信義,夜深喇,我去休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,老兄,憑我的信義,夜深了,我去休息。

passages.original: [Exeunt all but Juliet and Nurse.]
passages.vernacular: [除茱麗葉同奶媽外,眾人下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [除茱麗葉與奶媽外,眾人下。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Come hither, Nurse.
passages.vernacular: 過嚟,奶媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過來,奶媽。

passages.original: What is yond gentleman?
passages.vernacular: 嗰位先生係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位先生是誰?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: The son and heir of old Tiberio.
passages.vernacular: 老提伯里奧嘅兒子同繼承人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老提伯里奧的兒子和繼承人。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: What’s he that now is going out of door?
passages.vernacular: 嗰個而家要出門嘅係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個現在要出門的是誰?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Marry, that I think be young Petruchio.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,我想係年輕嘅彼特魯喬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,我想是年輕的彼特魯喬。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: What’s he that follows here, that would not dance?
passages.vernacular: 嗰個跟喺後面、唔肯跳舞嘅係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個跟在後面、不肯跳舞的是誰?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: I know not.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Go ask his name.
passages.vernacular: 去問佢嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去問他的名字。

passages.original: If he be married, My grave is like to be my wedding bed.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢已婚,我嘅墳墓恐怕就係我嘅婚床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他已婚,我的墳墓恐怕就是我的婚床。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: His name is Romeo, and a Montague, The only son of your great enemy.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅名字係羅密歐,係蒙太古家嘅人,你嘅大仇人嘅獨生子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的名字是羅密歐,是蒙太古家的人,你的大仇人的獨生子。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: My only love sprung from my only hate!
passages.vernacular: 我唯一嘅愛情從我唯一嘅恨中生出!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我唯一的愛情從我唯一的恨中生出!

passages.original: Too early seen unknown, and known too late!
passages.vernacular: 太早見到咗仲不認識,認識咗卻太遲!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太早見到了還不認識,認識了卻太遲!

passages.original: Prodigious birth of love it is to me, That I must love a loathed enemy.
passages.vernacular: 對我來講呢個係愛情嘅怪異誕生,我必須愛一個可恨嘅仇人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我來說這是愛情的怪異誕生,我必須愛一個可恨的仇人。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: What’s this?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是什麼?

passages.original: What’s this?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是什麼?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: A rhyme I learn’d even now Of one I danc’d withal.
passages.vernacular: 一首我剛學嚟嘅韻詩,係從一個同我跳過舞嘅人嗰度學嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一首我剛學來的韻詩,是從一個和我跳過舞的人那裡學來的。

passages.original: [One calls within, ‘Juliet’.]
passages.vernacular: [內有人喊「茱麗葉」。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內有人喊「茱麗葉」。]

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Anon, anon!
passages.vernacular: 嚟喇,嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來了,來了!

passages.original: Come let’s away, the strangers all are gone.
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧,我哋走,陌生人都走光喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧,我們走,陌生人都走光了。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Prologue to Act II 第二幕序詩

passages.original: Enter Chorus.
passages.vernacular: [序詩者上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [序詩者上。]

passages.title: Chorus 序詩者
passages.original: Now old desire doth in his deathbed lie, And young affection gapes to be his heir;
passages.vernacular: 而家舊日嘅慾望躺喺臨終嘅床上,年輕嘅愛慕張大嘴要繼承佢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在舊日的慾望躺在臨終的床上,年輕的愛慕張大嘴要繼承他;

passages.original: That fair for which love groan’d for and would die, With tender Juliet match’d, is now not fair.
passages.vernacular: 嗰位曾令愛情呻吟、願為之死嘅美人,同溫柔嘅茱麗葉相比,如今已不美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位曾令愛情呻吟、願為之死的美人,與溫柔的茱麗葉相比,如今已不美。

passages.original: Now Romeo is belov’d, and loves again, Alike bewitched by the charm of looks;
passages.vernacular: 而家羅密歐被愛,都喺愛,同樣被眼神嘅魅力迷惑;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在羅密歐被愛,也在愛,同樣被眼神的魅力迷惑;

passages.original: But to his foe suppos’d he must complain, And she steal love’s sweet bait from fearful hooks:
passages.vernacular: 但佢必須向佢所謂嘅仇人傾訴,而佢要從可怕嘅魚鉤上偷取愛情嘅甜蜜誘餌:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他必須向他所謂的仇人傾訴,而她要從可怕的魚鉤上偷取愛情的甜蜜誘餌:

passages.original: Being held a foe, he may not have access To breathe such vows as lovers use to swear;
passages.vernacular: 被視為仇人,佢無法接近佢,去講戀人慣常發嘅誓言;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被視為仇人,他無法接近她,去說戀人慣常發的誓言;

passages.original: And she as much in love, her means much less To meet her new beloved anywhere.
passages.vernacular: 佢同樣深愛,卻更無辦法喺任何地方同佢嘅新愛人會面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她同樣深愛,卻更無辦法在任何地方與她的新愛人會面。

passages.original: But passion lends them power, time means, to meet, Tempering extremities with extreme sweet.
passages.vernacular: 但激情畀佢哋力量,時間畀佢哋會面嘅方法,以極度嘅甜蜜調和極端嘅艱難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但激情給他們力量,時間給他們會面的方法,以極度的甜蜜調和極端的艱難。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene I — An Open Place adjoining Capulet’s Garden 第二幕第一場:凱普雷特花園旁的空地

passages.original: Enter Romeo.
passages.vernacular: [羅密歐上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅密歐上。]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Can I go forward when my heart is here?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅心喺呢度,我仲能往前走嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的心在這裡,我還能往前走嗎?

passages.original: Turn back, dull earth, and find thy centre out.
passages.vernacular: 回去吧,遲鈍嘅泥土,找到你嘅中心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回去吧,遲鈍的泥土,找到你的中心。

passages.original: [He climbs the wall and leaps down within it.]
passages.vernacular: [佢爬上牆,跳進裡面。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [他爬上牆,跳進裡面。]

passages.original: Enter Benvolio and Mercutio.
passages.vernacular: [班伏里奧同茂丘西奧上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [班伏里奧與茂丘西奧上。]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Romeo!
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐!

passages.original: My cousin Romeo! Romeo!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅堂兄羅密歐!羅密歐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的堂兄羅密歐!羅密歐!

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: He is wise, And on my life hath stol’n him home to bed.
passages.vernacular: 佢聰明,我用性命擔保,佢已偷偷回家瞓喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他聰明,我用性命擔保,他已偷偷回家睡了。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: He ran this way, and leap’d this orchard wall: Call, good Mercutio.
passages.vernacular: 佢往呢邊跑,跳過咗呢果園嘅牆:叫佢,好茂丘西奧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他往這邊跑,跳過了這果園的牆:叫他,好茂丘西奧。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Nay, I’ll conjure too. Romeo! Humours! Madman! Passion! Lover!
passages.vernacular: 不,我都要施咒。羅密歐!情緒!瘋子!激情!情人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我也要施咒。羅密歐!情緒!瘋子!激情!情人!

passages.original: Appear thou in the likeness of a sigh, Speak but one rhyme, and I am satisfied; Cry but ‘Ah me!’
passages.vernacular: 以嘆息嘅形象現身吧,只講一句韻,我就滿意喇;只喊一聲「哎呀!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以嘆息的形象現身吧,只說一句韻,我就滿意了;只喊一聲「哎呀!」

passages.original: Pronounce but Love and dove; Speak to my gossip Venus one fair word, One nickname for her purblind son and heir, Young Abraham Cupid, he that shot so trim When King Cophetua lov’d the beggar-maid.
passages.vernacular: 只念「愛」同「鴿」;對我嘅老友維納斯講一句好話,為佢嗰近視嘅兒子兼繼承人起一個外號,就係年輕嘅亞伯拉罕·丘比特,佢喺國王科菲圖亞愛上乞丐女時射得咁準。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只念「愛」與「鴿」;對我的老友維納斯說一句好話,為她那近視的兒子兼繼承人起一個外號,就是年輕的亞伯拉罕·丘比特,他在國王科菲圖亞愛上乞丐女時射得那麼準。

passages.original: He heareth not, he stirreth not, he moveth not;
passages.vernacular: 佢聽唔見,佢不動,佢不動彈;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他聽不見,他不動,他不動彈;

passages.original: The ape is dead, and I must conjure him.
passages.vernacular: 猴子死喇,我必須召喚佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 猴子死了,我必須召喚他。

passages.original: I conjure thee by Rosaline’s bright eyes, By her high forehead and her scarlet lip, By her fine foot, straight leg, and quivering thigh, And the demesnes that there adjacent lie, That in thy likeness thou appear to us.
passages.vernacular: 我憑羅瑟琳明亮嘅眼睛,憑佢高高嘅額頭同朱紅嘅嘴唇,憑佢精緻嘅腳、筆直嘅腿、顫動嘅大腿,以及緊鄰嗰度嘅領地,召喚你,以你嘅模樣向我哋現身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我憑羅瑟琳明亮的眼睛,憑她高高的額頭和朱紅的嘴唇,憑她精緻的腳、筆直的腿、顫動的大腿,以及緊鄰那裡的領地,召喚你,以你的模樣向我們現身。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: An if he hear thee, thou wilt anger him.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢聽見你,你會激怒佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他聽見你,你會激怒他。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: This cannot anger him.
passages.vernacular: 呢唔會激怒佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不會激怒他。

passages.original: ’Twould anger him To raise a spirit in his mistress’ circle, Of some strange nature, letting it there stand Till she had laid it, and conjur’d it down; That were some spite.
passages.vernacular: 嗰才會激怒佢:喺佢情人嘅圈子裡召喚某個古怪性質嘅精靈,讓佢站喺嗰度直到佢把佢安撫、召喚下去;嗰才算惡意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那才會激怒他:在他情人的圈子裡召喚某個古怪性質的精靈,讓它站在那裡直到她把它安撫、召喚下去;那才算惡意。

passages.original: My invocation Is fair and honest, and, in his mistress’ name, I conjure only but to raise up him.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅召喚係光明正大嘅,以佢情人嘅名義,我只係召喚佢出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的召喚是光明正大的,以他情人的名義,我只是召喚他出來。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Come, he hath hid himself among these trees To be consorted with the humorous night.
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧,佢把自己藏喺呢啲樹中間,同多愁善感嘅夜晚為伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧,他把自己藏在這些樹中間,與多愁善感的夜晚為伴。

passages.original: Blind is his love, and best befits the dark.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅愛係盲嘅,最適合黑暗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的愛是盲的,最適合黑暗。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: If love be blind, love cannot hit the mark.
passages.vernacular: 如果愛係盲嘅,愛就射不中靶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果愛是盲的,愛就射不中靶。

passages.original: Now will he sit under a medlar tree, And wish his mistress were that kind of fruit As maids call medlars when they laugh alone.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢會坐喺一棵歐楂樹下,希望佢嘅情人係少女哋獨自笑時叫做歐楂嘅嗰種果子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他會坐在一棵歐楂樹下,希望他的情人是少女們獨自笑時叫做歐楂的那種果子。

passages.original: O Romeo, that she were, O that she were An open-arse and thou a poperin pear!
passages.vernacular: 啊羅密歐,但願佢係,啊但願佢係一個張開嘅屁股,而你係一個波珀林梨!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊羅密歐,但願她是,啊但願她是一個張開的屁股,而你是一個波珀林梨!

passages.original: Romeo, good night.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐,晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐,晚安。

passages.original: I’ll to my truckle-bed.
passages.vernacular: 我去我嘅矮輪床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去我的矮輪床。

passages.original: This field-bed is too cold for me to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 呢野外嘅床對我來講太冷,瞓不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這野外的床對我來說太冷,睡不著。

passages.original: Come, shall we go?
passages.vernacular: 嚟,我哋走嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我們走嗎?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Go then; for ’tis in vain To seek him here that means not to be found.
passages.vernacular: 走吧;因為喺呢度找一個唔想被找到嘅人係徒勞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走吧;因為在這裡找一個不想被找到的人是徒勞。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene II — Capulet’s Garden 第二幕第二場:凱普雷特花園

passages.original: Enter Romeo.
passages.vernacular: [羅密歐上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅密歐上。]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: He jests at scars that never felt a wound.
passages.vernacular: 冇受過傷嘅人才嘲笑傷疤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒受過傷的人才嘲笑傷疤。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Juliet appears above at a window.
passages.vernacular: [茱麗葉出而家上面嘅窗口。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茱麗葉出現在上面的窗口。]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: But soft, what light through yonder window breaks?
passages.vernacular: 但係輕聲,嗰邊窗口透出嘅係乜嘢光?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是輕聲,那邊窗口透出的是什麼光?

passages.original: It is the east, and Juliet is the sun!
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係東方,茱麗葉就係太陽!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是東方,茱麗葉就是太陽!

passages.original: Arise fair sun and kill the envious moon, Who is already sick and pale with grief, That thou her maid art far more fair than she.
passages.vernacular: 升起吧,美麗嘅太陽,殺死嗰嫉妒嘅月亮,佢已因悲傷而病弱蒼白,因為你,佢嘅侍女,比佢美得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 升起吧,美麗的太陽,殺死那嫉妒的月亮,她已因悲傷而病弱蒼白,因為你,她的侍女,比她美得多。

passages.original: Be not her maid since she is envious; Her vestal livery is but sick and green, And none but fools do wear it; cast it off.
passages.vernacular: 別做佢嘅侍女,因為佢嫉妒;佢貞女嘅制服只係病態嘅綠色,只有傻瓜才穿;把佢脫掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別做她的侍女,因為她嫉妒;她貞女的制服只是病態的綠色,只有傻瓜才穿;把它脫掉。

passages.original: It is my lady, O it is my love!
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係我嘅女士,啊,嗰個係我嘅愛人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是我的女士,啊,那是我的愛人!

passages.original: O, that she knew she were!
passages.vernacular: 啊,但願佢知道佢係!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,但願她知道她是!

passages.original: She speaks, yet she says nothing.
passages.vernacular: 佢講話,卻乜嘢都冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說話,卻什麼也沒說。

passages.original: What of that?
passages.vernacular: 嗰有乜嘢關係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那有什麼關係?

passages.original: Her eye discourses, I will answer it.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛喺講話,我嚟回答佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛在說話,我來回答它。

passages.original: I am too bold, ’tis not to me she speaks.
passages.vernacular: 我太大膽喇,佢唔係對我講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太大膽了,她不是對我說話。

passages.original: Two of the fairest stars in all the heaven, Having some business, do entreat her eyes To twinkle in their spheres till they return.
passages.vernacular: 天上最美嘅兩顆星,有點事要辦,懇求佢嘅眼睛喺佢哋嘅軌道上閃爍,直到佢哋回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天上最美的兩顆星,有點事要辦,懇求她的眼睛在它們的軌道上閃爍,直到它們回來。

passages.original: What if her eyes were there, they in her head?
passages.vernacular: 如果佢嘅眼睛喺嗰度,而佢哋喺佢頭上呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她的眼睛在那裡,而它們在她頭上呢?

passages.original: The brightness of her cheek would shame those stars, As daylight doth a lamp;
passages.vernacular: 佢臉頰嘅光輝會使嗰啲星星羞愧,如同日光使油燈黯然;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她臉頰的光輝會使那些星星羞愧,如同日光使油燈黯然;

passages.original: her eyes in heaven Would through the airy region stream so bright That birds would sing and think it were not night.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛喺天上,會穿過空中嘅區域如此明亮地流瀉,以致鳥兒會歌唱,以為唔係夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛在天上,會穿過空中的區域如此明亮地流瀉,以致鳥兒會歌唱,以為不是夜晚。

passages.original: See how she leans her cheek upon her hand.
passages.vernacular: 睇佢點樣把臉頰靠喺手上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看她怎樣把臉頰靠在手上。

passages.original: O that I were a glove upon that hand, That I might touch that cheek.
passages.vernacular: 啊,但願我係嗰隻手上嘅手套,好讓我觸摸嗰臉頰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,但願我是那隻手上的手套,好讓我觸摸那臉頰。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Ay me.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: She speaks.
passages.vernacular: 佢講話喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說話了。

passages.original: O speak again bright angel, for thou art As glorious to this night, being o’er my head, As is a winged messenger of heaven Unto the white-upturned wondering eyes Of mortals that fall back to gaze on him When he bestrides the lazy-puffing clouds And sails upon the bosom of the air.
passages.vernacular: 啊,再講一遍,明亮嘅天使,因為你喺我頭頂,對呢夜晚係如此榮耀,如同一位有翼嘅天使信使,對嗰啲向後仰倒、翻白驚奇地凝視佢嘅凡人嘅眼睛,當佢騎喺懶懶吹氣嘅雲上,航行喺空氣嘅胸懷中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,再說一遍,明亮的天使,因為你在我頭頂,對這夜晚是如此榮耀,如同一位有翼的天使信使,對那些向後仰倒、翻白驚奇地凝視他的凡人的眼睛,當他騎在懶懶吹氣的雲上,航行在空氣的胸懷中。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O Romeo, Romeo, wherefore art thou Romeo?
passages.vernacular: 啊羅密歐,羅密歐,你點解係羅密歐?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊羅密歐,羅密歐,你為什麼是羅密歐?

passages.original: Deny thy father and refuse thy name.
passages.vernacular: 否認你嘅父親,拒絕你嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 否認你的父親,拒絕你的名字。

passages.original: Or if thou wilt not, be but sworn my love, And I’ll no longer be a Capulet.
passages.vernacular: 或者,如果你唔肯,只要發誓做我嘅愛人,我就唔再做凱普雷特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,如果你不肯,只要發誓做我的愛人,我就不再做凱普雷特。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: Shall I hear more, or shall I speak at this?
passages.vernacular: 我該再聽下去,定係而家就講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我該再聽下去,還是現在就說?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: ’Tis but thy name that is my enemy; Thou art thyself, though not a Montague.
passages.vernacular: 只有你嘅名字係我嘅敵人;你就係你自己,即使唔係蒙太古。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有你的名字是我的敵人;你就是你自己,即使不是蒙太古。

passages.original: What’s Montague?
passages.vernacular: 蒙太古係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒙太古是什麼?

passages.original: It is nor hand nor foot, Nor arm, nor face, nor any other part Belonging to a man.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係手,唔係腳,唔係臂,唔係臉,都唔係屬於一個人嘅任何其他部分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它不是手,不是腳,不是臂,不是臉,也不是屬於一個人的任何其他部分。

passages.original: O be some other name.
passages.vernacular: 啊,換個別嘅名字吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,換個別的名字吧。

passages.original: What’s in a name?
passages.vernacular: 名字裡有乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 名字裡有什麼?

passages.original: That which we call a rose By any other name would smell as sweet;
passages.vernacular: 我哋稱作玫瑰嘅花,換任何別嘅名字,聞起嚟都一樣芬芳;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們稱作玫瑰的花,換任何別的名字,聞起來也一樣芬芳;

passages.original: So Romeo would, were he not Romeo call’d, Retain that dear perfection which he owes Without that title.
passages.vernacular: 所以羅密歐,即使不叫羅密歐,都會保有佢本來擁有嘅嗰親愛嘅完美,無需嗰個稱號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以羅密歐,即使不叫羅密歐,也會保有他本來擁有的那親愛的完美,無需那個稱號。

passages.original: Romeo, doff thy name, And for thy name, which is no part of thee, Take all myself.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐,脫掉你嘅名字,為了你呢不屬於你嘅名字,把我整個人攞去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐,脫掉你的名字,為了你這不屬於你的名字,把我整個人拿去。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I take thee at thy word.
passages.vernacular: 我就照你嘅話收你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就照你的話收你。

passages.original: Call me but love, and I’ll be new baptis’d; Henceforth I never will be Romeo.
passages.vernacular: 只管叫我愛,我就重新受洗;從今以後我再都唔係羅密歐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只管叫我愛,我就重新受洗;從今以後我再也不是羅密歐。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: What man art thou that, thus bescreen’d in night So stumblest on my counsel?
passages.vernacular: 你係乜嘢人,咁樣躲喺夜色裡,偷聽到我嘅心事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是什麼人,這樣躲在夜色裡,偷聽到我的心事?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: By a name I know not how to tell thee who I am:
passages.vernacular: 用一個名字,我唔知道點樣告訴你我係邊個:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用一個名字,我不知道怎樣告訴你我是誰:

passages.original: My name, dear saint, is hateful to myself, Because it is an enemy to thee.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅名字,親愛嘅聖徒,我自己都憎恨,因為佢係你嘅敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的名字,親愛的聖徒,我自己都憎恨,因為它是你的敵人。

passages.original: Had I it written, I would tear the word.
passages.vernacular: 如果我把佢寫下嚟,我會撕掉嗰個字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我把它寫下來,我會撕掉那個字。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: My ears have yet not drunk a hundred words Of thy tongue’s utterance, yet I know the sound.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅耳朵仲冇聽到你舌頭講出嘅一百個字,卻已認得嗰聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的耳朵還沒聽到你舌頭說出的一百個字,卻已認得那聲音。

passages.original: Art thou not Romeo, and a Montague?
passages.vernacular: 你唔係羅密歐,蒙太古家嘅人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不是羅密歐,蒙太古家的人嗎?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Neither, fair maid, if either thee dislike.
passages.vernacular: 都唔係,美麗嘅小姐,如果兩者你都不鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 都不是,美麗的小姐,如果兩者你都不喜歡。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: How cam’st thou hither, tell me, and wherefore?
passages.vernacular: 告訴我,你點到呢度嚟嘅,點解?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴我,你怎麼到這裡來的,為什麼?

passages.original: The orchard walls are high and hard to climb, And the place death, considering who thou art, If any of my kinsmen find thee here.
passages.vernacular: 果園嘅牆又高又難爬,而呢個地方對你來講係死地,考慮到你係邊個,如果我嘅親戚發現你喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 果園的牆又高又難爬,而這個地方對你來說是死地,考慮到你是誰,如果我的親戚發現你在這裡。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: With love’s light wings did I o’erperch these walls, For stony limits cannot hold love out, And what love can do, that dares love attempt:
passages.vernacular: 我憑愛情輕盈嘅翅膀飛越呢啲牆,因為石頭嘅界限擋不住愛,愛能做嘅,愛就敢嘗試:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我憑愛情輕盈的翅膀飛越這些牆,因為石頭的界限擋不住愛,愛能做的,愛就敢嘗試:

passages.original: Therefore thy kinsmen are no stop to me.
passages.vernacular: 所以你嘅親戚阻止不咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你的親戚阻止不了我。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: If they do see thee, they will murder thee.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢哋睇見你,佢哋會殺死你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他們看見你,他們會殺死你。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Alack, there lies more peril in thine eye Than twenty of their swords.
passages.vernacular: 唉,你眼中嘅危險比佢哋二十把劍仲多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,你眼中的危險比他們二十把劍還多。

passages.original: Look thou but sweet, And I am proof against their enmity.
passages.vernacular: 只要你對我溫柔地睇,我就能抵禦佢哋嘅敵意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要你對我溫柔地看,我就能抵禦他們的敵意。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: I would not for the world they saw thee here.
passages.vernacular: 無論如何我都唔願佢哋喺呢度睇見你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論如何我都不願他們在這裡看見你。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I have night’s cloak to hide me from their eyes, And but thou love me, let them find me here.
passages.vernacular: 我有夜嘅斗篷把我藏起嚟躲過佢哋嘅眼睛,而只要你不愛我,就讓佢哋喺呢度找到我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有夜的斗篷把我藏起來躲過他們的眼睛,而只要你不愛我,就讓他們在這裡找到我。

passages.original: My life were better ended by their hate Than death prorogued, wanting of thy love.
passages.vernacular: 我寧願生命被佢哋嘅恨結束,都唔好缺少你嘅愛而延遲嘅死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願生命被他們的恨結束,也不要缺少你的愛而延遲的死。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: By whose direction found’st thou out this place?
passages.vernacular: 你係邊個指引你找到呢個地方嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是誰指引你找到這個地方的?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: By love, that first did prompt me to enquire;
passages.vernacular: 係愛,佢最先促使我去打聽;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是愛,它最先促使我去打聽;

passages.original: He lent me counsel, and I lent him eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢借畀我主意,我借畀佢眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它借給我主意,我借給它眼睛。

passages.original: I am no pilot; yet wert thou as far As that vast shore wash’d with the farthest sea, I should adventure for such merchandise.
passages.vernacular: 我唔係舵手;不過即使你遠喺被最遠海洋沖刷嘅嗰片廣闊海岸,我都會為咁樣嘅貨物冒險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是舵手;可是即使你遠在被最遠海洋沖刷的那片廣闊海岸,我也會為這樣的貨物冒險。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Thou knowest the mask of night is on my face, Else would a maiden blush bepaint my cheek For that which thou hast heard me speak tonight.
passages.vernacular: 你知道夜嘅面具喺我臉上,否則少女嘅羞紅會染我嘅臉頰,因為你今夜聽見我所講嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道夜的面具在我臉上,否則少女的羞紅會染我的臉頰,因為你今夜聽見我所說的話。

passages.original: Fain would I dwell on form, fain, fain deny What I have spoke; but farewell compliment.
passages.vernacular: 我好想拘守禮節,好想否認我講過嘅話;但再會喇,客套。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很想拘守禮節,很想否認我說過的話;但再會了,客套。

passages.original: Dost thou love me?
passages.vernacular: 你愛我嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你愛我嗎?

passages.original: I know thou wilt say Ay, And I will take thy word.
passages.vernacular: 我知道你會講「愛」,我會相信你嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道你會說「愛」,我會相信你的話。

passages.original: Yet, if thou swear’st, Thou mayst prove false.
passages.vernacular: 不過,如果你發誓,你可能會食言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是,如果你發誓,你可能會食言。

passages.original: At lovers’ perjuries, They say Jove laughs.
passages.vernacular: 對戀人嘅偽誓,據講朱庇特都會笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對戀人的偽誓,據說朱庇特也會笑。

passages.original: O gentle Romeo, If thou dost love, pronounce it faithfully.
passages.vernacular: 啊,溫柔嘅羅密歐,如果你愛,就誠懇地講出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,溫柔的羅密歐,如果你愛,就誠懇地說出來。

passages.original: Or if thou thinkest I am too quickly won, I’ll frown and be perverse, and say thee nay, So thou wilt woo.
passages.vernacular: 或者,如果你以為我太容易被贏得,我就皺眉、故意刁難,對你講「不」,只要你肯追求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,如果你以為我太容易被贏得,我就皺眉、故意刁難,對你說「不」,只要你肯追求。

passages.original: But else, not for the world.
passages.vernacular: 否則,無論如何不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 否則,無論如何不。

passages.original: In truth, fair Montague, I am too fond; And therefore thou mayst think my ’haviour light:
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,美麗嘅蒙太古,我太癡情喇;因此你可能認為我嘅舉止輕浮:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,美麗的蒙太古,我太癡情了;因此你可能認為我的舉止輕浮:

passages.original: But trust me, gentleman, I’ll prove more true Than those that have more cunning to be strange.
passages.vernacular: 但相信我,先生,我會比嗰啲更懂得裝出疏遠嘅人更真誠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但相信我,先生,我會比那些更懂得裝出疏遠的人更真誠。

passages.original: I should have been more strange, I must confess, But that thou overheard’st, ere I was ’ware, My true-love passion;
passages.vernacular: 我本應更疏遠些,我必須承認,只係你喺我察覺之前,偷聽到咗我真摯嘅愛情激情;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我本應更疏遠些,我必須承認,只是你在我察覺之前,偷聽到了我真摯的愛情激情;

passages.original: therefore pardon me, And not impute this yielding to light love, Which the dark night hath so discovered.
passages.vernacular: 所以請原諒我,唔好把呢份屈從歸為輕率嘅愛,係黑夜如此揭露咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以請原諒我,不要把這份屈從歸為輕率的愛,是黑夜如此揭露了它。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Lady, by yonder blessed moon I vow, That tips with silver all these fruit-tree tops,—
passages.vernacular: 小姐,我憑嗰邊神聖嘅月亮發誓,佢用銀色鑲飾所有果樹嘅樹梢,——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姐,我憑那邊神聖的月亮發誓,她用銀色鑲飾所有果樹的樹梢,——

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O swear not by the moon, th’inconstant moon, That monthly changes in her circled orb, Lest that thy love prove likewise variable.
passages.vernacular: 啊,別憑月亮發誓,嗰多變嘅月亮,每月喺佢嘅圓軌上變化,免得你嘅愛都同樣變化無常。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,別憑月亮發誓,那多變的月亮,每月在她的圓軌上變化,免得你的愛也同樣變化無常。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: What shall I swear by?
passages.vernacular: 嗰我憑乜嘢發誓?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我憑什麼發誓?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Do not swear at all.
passages.vernacular: 根本唔好發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 根本不要發誓。

passages.original: Or if thou wilt, swear by thy gracious self, Which is the god of my idolatry, And I’ll believe thee.
passages.vernacular: 或者,如果你願意,就憑你優雅嘅自己發誓,嗰個係我崇拜嘅神,我就相信你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,如果你願意,就憑你優雅的自己發誓,那是我崇拜的神,我就相信你。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: If my heart’s dear love,—
passages.vernacular: 如果我心中親愛嘅愛,——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我心中親愛的愛,——

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Well, do not swear.
passages.vernacular: 好,唔好發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,不要發誓。

passages.original: Although I joy in thee, I have no joy of this contract tonight;
passages.vernacular: 雖然我以你為喜悅,但我對今晚呢個盟約並不歡喜;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然我以你為喜悅,但我對今晚這個盟約並不歡喜;

passages.original: It is too rash, too unadvis’d, too sudden, Too like the lightning, which doth cease to be Ere one can say “It lightens.”
passages.vernacular: 佢太倉促、太輕率、太突然,太像閃電,喺人講出「閃電喇」之前就消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它太倉促、太輕率、太突然,太像閃電,在人說出「閃電了」之前就消失了。

passages.original: Sweet, good night.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅,晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的,晚安。

passages.original: This bud of love, by summer’s ripening breath, May prove a beauteous flower when next we meet.
passages.vernacular: 呢愛情嘅花蕾,經夏天成熟嘅呼吸,下次我哋見面時或者會成為美麗嘅花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這愛情的花蕾,經夏天成熟的呼吸,下次我們見面時也許會成為美麗的花。

passages.original: Good night, good night.
passages.vernacular: 晚安,晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚安,晚安。

passages.original: As sweet repose and rest Come to thy heart as that within my breast.
passages.vernacular: 願如我胸中嘅嗰般甜美嘅安息同平靜嚟到你心裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願如我胸中的那般甜美的安息與平靜來到你心裡。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: O wilt thou leave me so unsatisfied?
passages.vernacular: 啊,你就咁樣離開我,讓我不滿足嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,你就這樣離開我,讓我不滿足嗎?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: What satisfaction canst thou have tonight?
passages.vernacular: 你今晚仲能得到乜嘢滿足?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你今晚還能得到什麼滿足?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Th’exchange of thy love’s faithful vow for mine.
passages.vernacular: 用你嘅愛嘅忠實誓言,換我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用你的愛的忠實誓言,換我的。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: I gave thee mine before thou didst request it;
passages.vernacular: 我喺你要求之前就已畀咗你我嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在你要求之前就已給了你我的;

passages.original: And yet I would it were to give again.
passages.vernacular: 不過我願嗰個係可以再畀一次嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我願那是可以再給一次的。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Would’st thou withdraw it?
passages.vernacular: 你要收回佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要收回它嗎?

passages.original: For what purpose, love?
passages.vernacular: 為了乜嘢目的,愛人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了什麼目的,愛人?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: But to be frank and give it thee again.
passages.vernacular: 只係為了坦率,再畀你一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是為了坦率,再給你一次。

passages.original: And yet I wish but for the thing I have; My bounty is as boundless as the sea, My love as deep;
passages.vernacular: 然而我所希望嘅,只係我已有嘅嘢;我嘅慷慨像海一樣無邊,我嘅愛一樣深;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而我所希望的,只是我已有的東西;我的慷慨像海一樣無邊,我的愛一樣深;

passages.original: the more I give to thee, The more I have, for both are infinite.
passages.vernacular: 我畀你越多,我擁有越多,因為兩者都係無窮嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給你越多,我擁有越多,因為兩者都是無窮的。

passages.original: I hear some noise within.
passages.vernacular: 我聽到裡面有聲響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽到裡面有聲響。

passages.original: Dear love, adieu.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅,再會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的,再會。

passages.original: [Nurse calls within.]
passages.vernacular: [奶媽在內呼喚。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奶媽在內呼喚。]

passages.original: Anon, good Nurse!—Sweet Montague be true.
passages.vernacular: 嚟喇,好奶媽!——親愛嘅蒙太古,要真心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來了,好奶媽!——親愛的蒙太古,要真心。

passages.original: Stay but a little, I will come again.
passages.vernacular: 稍等一會兒,我再回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稍等一會兒,我再回來。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: O blessed, blessed night.
passages.vernacular: 啊,蒙福嘅,蒙福嘅夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,蒙福的,蒙福的夜晚。

passages.original: I am afeard, Being in night, all this is but a dream, Too flattering sweet to be substantial.
passages.vernacular: 我怕,既然係夜晚,呢一切只係夢,甜蜜得討好,不像係真實嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕,既然是夜晚,這一切只是夢,甜蜜得討好,不像是真實的。

passages.original: Enter Juliet above.
passages.vernacular: [茱麗葉喺上面再上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茱麗葉在上面再上。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Three words, dear Romeo, and good night indeed.
passages.vernacular: 三個字,親愛嘅羅密歐,然後真正晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三個字,親愛的羅密歐,然後真正晚安。

passages.original: If that thy bent of love be honourable, Thy purpose marriage, send me word tomorrow, By one that I’ll procure to come to thee, Where and what time thou wilt perform the rite, And all my fortunes at thy foot I’ll lay And follow thee my lord throughout the world.
passages.vernacular: 如果你愛嘅心意係光明正大嘅,你嘅目的係婚姻,聽日派人告訴我,我會設法讓一個人去見你,告訴我你喺何處何時舉行儀式,我就把我全部嘅命運放喺你腳下,跟隨你,我嘅夫君,走遍世界。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你愛的心意是光明正大的,你的目的是婚姻,明天派人告訴我,我會設法讓一個人去見你,告訴我你在何處何時舉行儀式,我就把我全部的命運放在你腳下,跟隨你,我的夫君,走遍世界。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: [Within.] Madam.
passages.vernacular: [在內。]夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [在內。]夫人。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: I come, anon.— But if thou meanest not well, I do beseech thee,—
passages.vernacular: 我就嚟。——但如果你嘅意圖不善,我求你,——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就來。——但如果你的意圖不善,我求你,——

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: [Within.] Madam.
passages.vernacular: [在內。]夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [在內。]夫人。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: By and by I come— To cease thy strife and leave me to my grief.
passages.vernacular: 即刻就嚟——停止你嘅糾纏,讓我獨自悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬上就來——停止你的糾纏,讓我獨自悲傷。

passages.original: Tomorrow will I send.
passages.vernacular: 我聽日就派人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我明天就派人。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: So thrive my soul,—
passages.vernacular: 願我嘅靈魂興旺,——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願我的靈魂興旺,——

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: A thousand times good night.
passages.vernacular: 千次晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 千次晚安。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: A thousand times the worse, to want thy light.
passages.vernacular: 缺少你嘅光,就係千倍嘅更糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 缺少你的光,就是千倍的更糟。

passages.original: Love goes toward love as schoolboys from their books, But love from love, towards school with heavy looks.
passages.vernacular: 愛向愛而去,如同學童離開佢哋嘅書本;但愛離開愛,卻如去上學,臉帶沉重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛向愛而去,如同學童離開他們的書本;但愛離開愛,卻如去上學,臉帶沉重。

passages.original: [Retiring slowly.]
passages.vernacular: [緩緩退下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [緩緩退下。]

passages.original: Re-enter Juliet, above.
passages.vernacular: [茱麗葉喺上面重上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茱麗葉在上面重上。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Hist!
passages.vernacular: 噓!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 噓!

passages.original: Romeo, hist!
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐,噓!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐,噓!

passages.original: O for a falconer’s voice To lure this tassel-gentle back again.
passages.vernacular: 啊,但願有馴鷹人嘅嗓音,把呢隻雄鷹召回。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,但願有馴鷹人的嗓音,把這隻雄鷹召回。

passages.original: Bondage is hoarse and may not speak aloud, Else would I tear the cave where Echo lies, And make her airy tongue more hoarse than mine With repetition of my Romeo’s name.
passages.vernacular: 被束縛嘅人聲音嘶啞,唔能夠高聲講話,否則我會撕裂回聲女神躺嘅洞穴,用重複我羅密歐嘅名字,讓佢嗰空氣般嘅舌頭比我嘅更嘶啞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被束縛的人聲音嘶啞,不能高聲說話,否則我會撕裂回聲女神躺的洞穴,用重複我羅密歐的名字,讓她那空氣般的舌頭比我的更嘶啞。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: It is my soul that calls upon my name.
passages.vernacular: 係我嘅靈魂喺呼喚我嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是我的靈魂在呼喚我的名字。

passages.original: How silver-sweet sound lovers’ tongues by night, Like softest music to attending ears.
passages.vernacular: 戀人喺夜裡嘅舌頭聽嚟幾咁銀樣甜美,像最柔和嘅音樂傳進傾聽嘅耳朵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戀人在夜裡的舌頭聽來多麼銀樣甜美,像最柔和的音樂傳進傾聽的耳朵。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Romeo.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: My dear?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅親愛嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的親愛的?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: What o’clock tomorrow Shall I send to thee?
passages.vernacular: 聽日幾點鐘,我該派人去你嗰度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明天幾點鐘,我該派人去你那裡?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: By the hour of nine.
passages.vernacular: 九點鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 九點鐘。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: I will not fail.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會失約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會失約。

passages.original: ’Tis twenty years till then.
passages.vernacular: 到嗰時仲有二十年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到那時還有二十年。

passages.original: I have forgot why I did call thee back.
passages.vernacular: 我忘咗點解叫你回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我忘了為什麼叫你回來。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Let me stand here till thou remember it.
passages.vernacular: 讓我站喺呢度,直到你想起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我站在這裡,直到你想起來。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: I shall forget, to have thee still stand there, Remembering how I love thy company.
passages.vernacular: 我會忘記,好讓你一直站喺嗰度,想起我幾咁愛你嘅陪伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會忘記,好讓你一直站在那裡,想起我多麼愛你的陪伴。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: And I’ll still stay, to have thee still forget, Forgetting any other home but this.
passages.vernacular: 我會一直留下,好讓你一直忘記,忘記除咗呢度之外嘅任何家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會一直留下,好讓你一直忘記,忘記除了這裡之外的任何家。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: ’Tis almost morning; I would have thee gone, And yet no farther than a wanton’s bird, That lets it hop a little from her hand, Like a poor prisoner in his twisted gyves, And with a silk thread plucks it back again, So loving-jealous of his liberty.
passages.vernacular: 天快亮喇;我要你走,卻唔能夠比任性女孩嘅小鳥更遠,佢讓佢從手上跳開啲,像可憐嘅囚徒戴住纏繞嘅鐐銬,又用絲線把佢拉回嚟,對佢嘅自由嗰樣愛護又嫉妒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天快亮了;我要你走,卻不能比任性女孩的小鳥更遠,她讓它從手上跳開一點,像可憐的囚徒戴著纏繞的鐐銬,又用絲線把它拉回來,對它的自由那樣愛護又嫉妒。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I would I were thy bird.
passages.vernacular: 我願我係你嘅小鳥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我願我是你的小鳥。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Sweet, so would I: Yet I should kill thee with much cherishing.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅,我都願意:不過我會因過分寵愛而殺死你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的,我也願意:可是我會因過分寵愛而殺死你。

passages.original: Good night, good night.
passages.vernacular: 晚安,晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚安,晚安。

passages.original: Parting is such sweet sorrow That I shall say good night till it be morrow.
passages.vernacular: 離別係咁樣甜蜜嘅憂傷,我要講晚安講到天明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 離別是這樣甜蜜的憂傷,我要說晚安說到天明。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Sleep dwell upon thine eyes, peace in thy breast.
passages.vernacular: 願瞓眠安住喺你眼中,平安喺你胸中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願睡眠安住在你眼中,平安在你胸中。

passages.original: Would I were sleep and peace, so sweet to rest.
passages.vernacular: 但願我係瞓眠和平安,喺嗰樣甜蜜中安息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但願我是睡眠和平安,在那樣甜蜜中安息。

passages.original: Hence will I to my ghostly Sire’s cell, His help to crave and my dear hap to tell.
passages.vernacular: 我從呢度去我神父嘅修室,求佢幫助並告知我嘅幸運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從這裡去我神父的修室,求他幫助並告知我的幸運。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene III — Friar Lawrence’s Cell 第二幕第三場:勞倫斯神父的修室

passages.original: Enter Friar Lawrence with a basket.
passages.vernacular: [勞倫斯神父提住籃子上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [勞倫斯神父提著籃子上。]

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: The grey-ey’d morn smiles on the frowning night, Chequering the eastern clouds with streaks of light;
passages.vernacular: 灰眼嘅早晨對皺眉嘅夜晚微笑,用光線嘅條紋畀東方嘅雲彩織上格紋;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 灰眼的早晨對皺眉的夜晚微笑,用光線的條紋給東方的雲彩織上格紋;

passages.original: And fleckled darkness like a drunkard reels From forth day’s pathway, made by Titan’s fiery wheels Now, ere the sun advance his burning eye, The day to cheer, and night’s dank dew to dry, I must upfill this osier cage of ours With baleful weeds and precious-juiced flowers.
passages.vernacular: 斑駁嘅黑暗像醉漢般搖晃住,離開泰坦火輪開闢嘅白晝之路:而家,喺太陽抬起燃燒嘅眼睛,為白晝帶嚟歡樂,把夜嘅濕露烤乾之前,我必須用毒草同寶貴汁液嘅花,把我哋呢隻柳條籃裝滿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斑駁的黑暗像醉漢般搖晃著,離開泰坦火輪開闢的白晝之路:現在,在太陽抬起燃燒的眼睛,為白晝帶來歡樂,把夜的濕露烤乾之前,我必須用毒草和寶貴汁液的花,把我們這隻柳條籃裝滿。

passages.original: The earth that’s nature’s mother, is her tomb;
passages.vernacular: 大地係自然之母,都係佢嘅墳墓;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大地是自然之母,也是她的墳墓;

passages.original: What is her burying grave, that is her womb: And from her womb children of divers kind We sucking on her natural bosom find.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅葬身之地,就係佢嘅子宮:從佢子宮裡,我哋睇到各種各樣嘅細路,喺佢天然嘅胸懷上吸奶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的葬身之地,就是她的子宮:從她子宮裡,我們看到各種各樣的孩子,在她天然的胸懷上吸奶。

passages.original: Many for many virtues excellent, None but for some, and yet all different.
passages.vernacular: 許多因許多美德而卓越,冇一種冇用處,卻各不相同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 許多因許多美德而卓越,沒有一種沒有用處,卻各不相同。

passages.original: O, mickle is the powerful grace that lies In plants, herbs, stones, and their true qualities.
passages.vernacular: 啊,植物、草藥、石頭,以及佢哋真正嘅性質中,蘊含住強大嘅恩典。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,植物、草藥、石頭,以及它們真正的性質中,蘊含著強大的恩典。

passages.original: For naught so vile that on the earth doth live But to the earth some special good doth give;
passages.vernacular: 因為世上活住嘅冇一樣卑劣得不畀大地帶嚟某種特別嘅好處;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為世上活著的沒有一樣卑劣得不給大地帶來某種特別的好處;

passages.original: Nor aught so good but, strain’d from that fair use, Revolts from true birth, stumbling on abuse.
passages.vernacular: 都冇一樣好得唔會,一旦脫離嗰美好嘅用途,就背離真正嘅本性,跌入濫用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也沒有一樣好得不會,一旦脫離那美好的用途,就背離真正的本性,跌入濫用。

passages.original: Virtue itself turns vice being misapplied, And vice sometime’s by action dignified.
passages.vernacular: 美德本身被誤用就變成惡習,惡習有時都因行動而顯得高貴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美德本身被誤用就變成惡習,惡習有時也因行動而顯得高貴。

passages.original: Enter Romeo.
passages.vernacular: [羅密歐上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅密歐上。]

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Within the infant rind of this weak flower Poison hath residence, and medicine power:
passages.vernacular: 喺呢弱小花朵嘅幼嫩外皮裡,毒藥居住,良藥都有其力量:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這弱小花朵的幼嫩外皮裡,毒藥居住,良藥也有其力量:

passages.original: For this, being smelt, with that part cheers each part;
passages.vernacular: 因為聞佢,就用呢部分使各部分振奮;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為聞它,就用這部分使各部分振奮;

passages.original: Being tasted, slays all senses with the heart.
passages.vernacular: 嘗佢,就連心一起使所有感官死亡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘗它,就連心一起使所有感官死亡。

passages.original: Two such opposed kings encamp them still In man as well as herbs,—grace and rude will;
passages.vernacular: 咁樣兩個相對嘅君王總是駐紮喺人身上,都喺草藥上,——恩典同粗野嘅意志;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣兩個相對的君王總是駐紮在人身上,也在草藥上,——恩典和粗野的意志;

passages.original: And where the worser is predominant, Full soon the canker death eats up that plant.
passages.vernacular: 邊一個壞嘅占上風,蛀蟲般嘅死亡好快就食掉嗰植物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哪一個壞的占上風,蛀蟲般的死亡很快就吃掉那植物。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Good morrow, father.
passages.vernacular: 早安,神父。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早安,神父。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Benedicite!
passages.vernacular: 願上帝賜福!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上帝賜福!

passages.original: What early tongue so sweet saluteth me?
passages.vernacular: 係乜嘢咁早嘅甜蜜舌頭向我問候?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是什麼這麼早的甜蜜舌頭向我問候?

passages.original: Young son, it argues a distemper’d head So soon to bid good morrow to thy bed.
passages.vernacular: 年輕嘅細路,咁早向你嘅床講早安,講明你頭腦不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 年輕的孩子,這麼早向你的床說早安,說明你頭腦不安。

passages.original: Care keeps his watch in every old man’s eye, And where care lodges sleep will never lie;
passages.vernacular: 憂慮喺每個老人眼中守夜,憂慮所住嘅地方瞓眠永不躺臥;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憂慮在每個老人眼中守夜,憂慮所住的地方睡眠永不躺臥;

passages.original: But where unbruised youth with unstuff’d brain Doth couch his limbs, there golden sleep doth reign.
passages.vernacular: 但喺未受創傷嘅青春、腦袋空空之處,佢哋伸展四肢,金色嘅瞓眠就喺嗰度統治。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在未受創傷的青春、腦袋空空之處,他們伸展四肢,金色的睡眠就在那裡統治。

passages.original: Therefore thy earliness doth me assure Thou art uprous’d with some distemperature;
passages.vernacular: 所以你起得咁早,使我確信你係因某種不適而被驚起;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你起得這麼早,使我確信你是因某種不適而被驚起;

passages.original: Or if not so, then here I hit it right, Our Romeo hath not been in bed tonight.
passages.vernacular: 如果唔係咁樣,咁我猜對咗呢啲:我哋嘅羅密歐今晚根本冇上床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果不是這樣,那麼我猜對了這一點:我們的羅密歐今晚根本沒有上床。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: That last is true; the sweeter rest was mine.
passages.vernacular: 後面呢啲係真嘅;我得到嘅休息更甜美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後面這一點是真的;我得到的休息更甜美。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: God pardon sin.
passages.vernacular: 上帝饒恕罪過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上帝饒恕罪過。

passages.original: Wast thou with Rosaline?
passages.vernacular: 你同羅瑟琳喺一起嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你和羅瑟琳在一起嗎?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: With Rosaline, my ghostly father? No.
passages.vernacular: 同羅瑟琳,我嘅神父?不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 和羅瑟琳,我的神父?不。

passages.original: I have forgot that name, and that name’s woe.
passages.vernacular: 我已忘咗嗰個名字,同嗰個名字嘅苦痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已忘了那個名字,和那個名字的苦痛。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: That’s my good son.
passages.vernacular: 呢才係我嘅好兒子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這才是我的好兒子。

passages.original: But where hast thou been then?
passages.vernacular: 咁你去咗邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼你去了哪裡?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I’ll tell thee ere thou ask it me again.
passages.vernacular: 喺你再問我之前,我就告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在你再問我之前,我就告訴你。

passages.original: I have been feasting with mine enemy, Where on a sudden one hath wounded me That’s by me wounded.
passages.vernacular: 我一直同我嘅敵人宴飲,一個人突然傷咗我,佢都被我所傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直和我的敵人宴飲,一個人突然傷了我,她也被我所傷。

passages.original: Both our remedies Within thy help and holy physic lies.
passages.vernacular: 我哋兩人嘅醫治都喺你嘅幫助同神聖嘅醫術裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們兩人的醫治都在你的幫助和神聖的醫術裡。

passages.original: I bear no hatred, blessed man; for lo, My intercession likewise steads my foe.
passages.vernacular: 我心中冇恨,蒙福嘅人;你睇,我嘅請求同樣有益於我嘅敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我心中沒有恨,蒙福的人;你看,我的請求同樣有益於我的敵人。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Be plain, good son, and homely in thy drift; Riddling confession finds but riddling shrift.
passages.vernacular: 講清楚,好細路,直白地講你嘅意思;謎一樣嘅懺悔只能得到謎一樣嘅赦免。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說清楚,好孩子,直白地說你的意思;謎一樣的懺悔只能得到謎一樣的赦免。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Then plainly know my heart’s dear love is set On the fair daughter of rich Capulet.
passages.vernacular: 咁直白地知道,我心中親愛嘅愛,放喺富有嘅凱普雷特嘅美麗女兒身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼直白地知道,我心中親愛的愛,放在富有的凱普雷特的美麗女兒身上。

passages.original: As mine on hers, so hers is set on mine; And all combin’d, save what thou must combine By holy marriage.
passages.vernacular: 我愛佢,佢同樣愛我;一切都已融洽,只欠你要用神聖嘅婚姻把我哋結合起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛她,她同樣愛我;一切都已融洽,只欠你要用神聖的婚姻把我們結合起來。

passages.original: When, and where, and how We met, we woo’d, and made exchange of vow, I’ll tell thee as we pass;
passages.vernacular: 何時、何地、如何我哋相遇、求愛、交換誓言,我路上告訴你;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 何時、何地、如何我們相遇、求愛、交換誓言,我路上告訴你;

passages.original: but this I pray, That thou consent to marry us today.
passages.vernacular: 但我請求,你今日答應為我哋證婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我請求,你今天答應為我們證婚。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Holy Saint Francis!
passages.vernacular: 聖方濟各啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖方濟各啊!

passages.original: What a change is here!
passages.vernacular: 呢個係點樣嘅改變!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是怎樣的改變!

passages.original: Is Rosaline, that thou didst love so dear, So soon forsaken?
passages.vernacular: 你嗰樣深愛嘅羅瑟琳,咁快就被拋棄喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你那樣深愛的羅瑟琳,這麼快就被拋棄了?

passages.original: Young men’s love then lies Not truly in their hearts, but in their eyes.
passages.vernacular: 咁年輕人嘅愛,並不真正在佢哋嘅心裡,而喺佢哋嘅眼裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼年輕人的愛,並不真正在他們的心裡,而在他們的眼裡。

passages.original: Jesu Maria, what a deal of brine Hath wash’d thy sallow cheeks for Rosaline!
passages.vernacular: 耶穌瑪利亞,為羅瑟琳,多少鹽水洗過你蠟黃嘅臉頰!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 耶穌瑪利亞,為羅瑟琳,多少鹽水洗過你蠟黃的臉頰!

passages.original: How much salt water thrown away in waste, To season love, that of it doth not taste.
passages.vernacular: 多少鹹水白白浪費,用嚟畀愛調味,而愛卻啲都嘗唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多少鹹水白白浪費,用來給愛調味,而愛卻一點也嘗不到。

passages.original: The sun not yet thy sighs from heaven clears, Thy old groans yet ring in mine ancient ears.
passages.vernacular: 太陽仲冇把你嘅嘆息從天上清除,你舊日嘅呻吟仲喺我老耳中迴響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太陽還沒有把你的嘆息從天上清除,你舊日的呻吟還在我老耳中迴響。

passages.original: Lo here upon thy cheek the stain doth sit Of an old tear that is not wash’d off yet.
passages.vernacular: 睇,你臉頰上仲留住一道舊淚痕冇洗掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,你臉頰上還留著一道舊淚痕沒有洗掉。

passages.original: If ere thou wast thyself, and these woes thine, Thou and these woes were all for Rosaline, And art thou chang’d?
passages.vernacular: 如果你曾經係你自己,呢啲悲傷係你嘅,你同呢啲悲傷都係為了羅瑟琳,你竟變咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你曾經是你自己,這些悲傷是你的,你和這些悲傷都是為了羅瑟琳,你竟變了嗎?

passages.original: Pronounce this sentence then, Women may fall, when there’s no strength in men.
passages.vernacular: 嗰就宣告呢個判決吧:當男人冇力量時,女人都會跌倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就宣告這個判決吧:當男人沒有力量時,女人也會跌倒。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Thou chidd’st me oft for loving Rosaline.
passages.vernacular: 你常常責備我愛羅瑟琳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你常常責備我愛羅瑟琳。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: For doting, not for loving, pupil mine.
passages.vernacular: 責備你癡迷,唔係責備你愛,我嘅學生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 責備你癡迷,不是責備你愛,我的學生。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: And bad’st me bury love.
passages.vernacular: 你仲叫我埋葬愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你還叫我埋葬愛。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Not in a grave To lay one in, another out to have.
passages.vernacular: 唔係要埋進墳墓,好讓另一個爬出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是要埋進墳墓,好讓另一個爬出來。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I pray thee chide me not, her I love now Doth grace for grace and love for love allow.
passages.vernacular: 請你別責備我,而家我愛嘅佢,畀我恩典換恩典,愛換愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你別責備我,現在我愛的她,給我恩典換恩典,愛換愛。

passages.original: The other did not so.
passages.vernacular: 另一個冇咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一個沒有這樣。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: O, she knew well Thy love did read by rote, that could not spell.
passages.vernacular: 啊,佢深知你嘅愛係死記硬背,連拼寫都唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,她深知你的愛是死記硬背,連拼寫都不會。

passages.original: But come young waverer, come go with me, In one respect I’ll thy assistant be;
passages.vernacular: 不過嚟吧,年輕嘅搖擺者,跟我嚟,喺啲上我會幫你;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過來吧,年輕的搖擺者,跟我來,在一點上我會幫你;

passages.original: For this alliance may so happy prove, To turn your households’ rancour to pure love.
passages.vernacular: 因為呢門親事或者會咁樣幸運,把你哋兩家嘅怨恨轉成純粹嘅愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為這門親事也許會這樣幸運,把你們兩家的怨恨轉成純粹的愛。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: O let us hence; I stand on sudden haste.
passages.vernacular: 啊,讓我哋離開呢度;我好急。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,讓我們離開這裡;我很急。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Wisely and slow; they stumble that run fast.
passages.vernacular: 要明智而緩慢;跑得快嘅人容易跌倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要明智而緩慢;跑得快的人容易跌倒。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene IV — A Street 第二幕第四場:街道

passages.original: Enter Benvolio and Mercutio.
passages.vernacular: [班伏里奧同茂丘西奧上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [班伏里奧與茂丘西奧上。]

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Where the devil should this Romeo be?
passages.vernacular: 呢個羅密歐到底喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個羅密歐到底在哪裡?

passages.original: Came he not home tonight?
passages.vernacular: 佢今晚冇回家嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他今晚沒回家嗎?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Not to his father’s; I spoke with his man.
passages.vernacular: 冇回佢父親嗰度;我跟佢嘅僕人談過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒回他父親那裡;我跟他的僕人談過。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Why, that same pale hard-hearted wench, that Rosaline, torments him so that he will sure run mad.
passages.vernacular: 哎,係嗰個蒼白嘅鐵石心腸嘅丫頭羅瑟琳,把佢折磨得一定會發瘋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,是那個蒼白的鐵石心腸的丫頭羅瑟琳,把他折磨得一定會發瘋。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Tybalt, the kinsman to old Capulet, hath sent a letter to his father’s house.
passages.vernacular: 提伯特,老凱普雷特嘅親戚,畀佢父親嘅家送咗封信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提伯特,老凱普雷特的親戚,給他父親的家送了封信。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: A challenge, on my life.
passages.vernacular: 我敢講,係挑戰書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢說,是挑戰書。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Romeo will answer it.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐會答覆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐會答覆。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Any man that can write may answer a letter.
passages.vernacular: 任何會寫字嘅人都能回信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何會寫字的人都能回信。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Nay, he will answer the letter’s master, how he dares, being dared.
passages.vernacular: 不,佢會答覆寫信嘅主人,如何敢應戰,既然被挑戰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,他會答覆寫信的主人,如何敢應戰,既然被挑戰。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Alas poor Romeo, he is already dead, stabbed with a white wench’s black eye;
passages.vernacular: 唉,可憐嘅羅密歐,佢已經死喇,被一個白皮膚女孩嘅黑眼睛刺殺;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,可憐的羅密歐,他已經死了,被一個白皮膚女孩的黑眼睛刺殺;

passages.original: run through the ear with a love song, the very pin of his heart cleft with the blind bow-boy’s butt-shaft.
passages.vernacular: 被一首情歌貫穿咗耳朵,心臟嘅靶心被瞎眼射手嘅鈍箭劈開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被一首情歌貫穿了耳朵,心臟的靶心被瞎眼射手的鈍箭劈開。

passages.original: And is he a man to encounter Tybalt?
passages.vernacular: 佢係對付提伯特嘅人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是對付提伯特的人嗎?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Why, what is Tybalt?
passages.vernacular: 哎,提伯特係乜嘢人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,提伯特是什麼人?

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: More than Prince of cats.
passages.vernacular: 比貓王子仲厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比貓王子還厲害。

passages.original: O, he’s the courageous captain of compliments.
passages.vernacular: 啊,佢係繁文縟節嘅勇敢隊長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,他是繁文縟節的勇敢隊長。

passages.original: He fights as you sing prick-song, keeps time, distance, and proportion.
passages.vernacular: 佢打架像你唱樂譜:守拍子、距離同比例。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他打架像你唱樂譜:守拍子、距離和比例。

passages.original: He rests his minim rest, one, two, and the third in your bosom:
passages.vernacular: 佢停一個二分休止符,一,二,第三下就刺進你嘅胸膛:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他停一個二分休止符,一,二,第三下就刺進你的胸膛:

passages.original: the very butcher of a silk button, a duellist, a duellist;
passages.vernacular: 佢係個能砍斷絲鈕釦嘅屠夫,一個決鬥家,一個決鬥家;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個能砍斷絲鈕釦的屠夫,一個決鬥家,一個決鬥家;

passages.original: a gentleman of the very first house, of the first and second cause.
passages.vernacular: 一位最高貴家族嘅紳士,精通第一同第二起因。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一位最高貴家族的紳士,精通第一和第二起因。

passages.original: Ah, the immortal passado, the punto reverso, the hay.
passages.vernacular: 啊,嗰不朽嘅前進刺、反手刺、直刺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,那不朽的前進刺、反手刺、直刺。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: The what?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼?

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: The pox of such antic lisping, affecting phantasies;
passages.vernacular: 呢種古怪咬字、矯揉造作嘅幻想,真係瘟疫;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種古怪咬字、矯揉造作的幻想,真是瘟疫;

passages.original: these new tuners of accent.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲新嘅口音調音師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些新的口音調音師。

passages.original: By Jesu, a very good blade, a very tall man, a very good whore.
passages.vernacular: 天呀,一把好劍,一個高個子,一個好妓女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,一把好劍,一個高個子,一個好妓女。

passages.original: Why, is not this a lamentable thing, grandsire, that we should be thus afflicted with these strange flies, these fashion-mongers, these pardon-me’s, who stand so much on the new form that they cannot sit at ease on the old bench?
passages.vernacular: 哎,呢唔係件可悲嘅事嗎,爺爺,我哋竟被呢啲奇怪嘅蒼蠅,呢啲時髦販子,呢啲「請原諒我」先生哋所折磨,佢哋咁重視新形式,以致喺舊長凳上唔能夠舒服地坐住?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,這不是件可悲的事嗎,爺爺,我們竟被這些奇怪的蒼蠅,這些時髦販子,這些「請原諒我」先生們所折磨,他們那麼重視新形式,以致在舊長凳上不能舒服地坐著?

passages.original: O their bones, their bones!
passages.vernacular: 啊,佢哋嘅骨頭,佢哋嘅骨頭!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,他們的骨頭,他們的骨頭!

passages.original: Enter Romeo.
passages.vernacular: [羅密歐上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅密歐上。]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Here comes Romeo, here comes Romeo!
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐嚟喇,羅密歐嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐來了,羅密歐來了!

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Without his roe, like a dried herring.
passages.vernacular: 冇佢嘅魚子,像條乾鯡魚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有他的魚子,像條乾鯡魚。

passages.original: O flesh, flesh, how art thou fishified!
passages.vernacular: 啊肉體,肉體,你點變成咗魚!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊肉體,肉體,你怎麼變成了魚!

passages.original: Now is he for the numbers that Petrarch flowed in.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢正適合彼特拉克流淌嘅詩句。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他正適合彼特拉克流淌的詩句。

passages.original: Laura, to his lady, was but a kitchen wench,—marry, she had a better love to berhyme her:
passages.vernacular: 勞拉,跟佢嘅女士相比,只係個廚房丫頭,——講真嘅,佢有個更好嘅情人為佢作詩:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勞拉,跟他的女士相比,只是個廚房丫頭,——說真的,她有個更好的情人為她作詩:

passages.original: Dido a dowdy; Cleopatra a gypsy; Helen and Hero hildings and harlots;
passages.vernacular: 狄多係個邋遢女人;克麗奧佩特拉係個吉卜賽女人;海倫同希羅係賤貨同妓女;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狄多是個邋遢女人;克麗奧佩特拉是個吉卜賽女人;海倫和希羅是賤貨和妓女;

passages.original: Thisbe a grey eye or so, but not to the purpose.
passages.vernacular: 提斯柏係灰眼睛乜嘢嘅,但不相干。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提斯柏是灰眼睛什麼的,但不相干。

passages.original: Signior Romeo, bonjour!
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐先生,早安!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐先生,早安!

passages.original: There’s a French salutation to your French slop.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係畀你法國褲子嘅法語問候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是給你法國褲子的法語問候。

passages.original: You gave us the counterfeit fairly last night.
passages.vernacular: 琴晚你好好畀我哋嚟咗個假貨(溜掉)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨晚你好好給我們來了個假貨(溜掉)。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Good morrow to you both.
passages.vernacular: 兩位早安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩位早安。

passages.original: What counterfeit did I give you?
passages.vernacular: 我畀咗你哋乜嘢假貨?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給了你們什麼假貨?

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: The slip sir, the slip; can you not conceive?
passages.vernacular: 溜掉(假貨),先生,溜掉;你不明白嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溜掉(假貨),先生,溜掉;你不明白嗎?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Pardon, good Mercutio, my business was great, and in such a case as mine a man may strain courtesy.
passages.vernacular: 請原諒,好茂丘西奧,我嘅事好大,喺我呢種情形下,人可以不拘禮節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請原諒,好茂丘西奧,我的事很大,在我這種情形下,人可以不拘禮節。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: That’s as much as to say, such a case as yours constrains a man to bow in the hams.
passages.vernacular: 嗰就等於講,你呢種情形逼人彎下膝窩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就等於說,你這種情形逼人彎下膝窩。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Meaning, to curtsy.
passages.vernacular: 意思係,行屈膝禮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 意思是,行屈膝禮。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Thou hast most kindly hit it.
passages.vernacular: 你最親切地猜中喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你最親切地猜中了。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: A most courteous exposition.
passages.vernacular: 一個最有禮貌嘅解釋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個最有禮貌的解釋。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Nay, I am the very pink of courtesy.
passages.vernacular: 不,我係禮貌嘅石竹(精華)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我是禮貌的石竹(精華)。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Pink for flower.
passages.vernacular: 石竹係花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 石竹是花。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Right.
passages.vernacular: 對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Why, then is my pump well flowered.
passages.vernacular: 咁我嘅舞鞋開滿咗花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼我的舞鞋開滿了花。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Sure wit, follow me this jest now, till thou hast worn out thy pump, that when the single sole of it is worn, the jest may remain after the wearing, solely singular.
passages.vernacular: 可靠嘅機智,跟我玩呢個笑話,直到你磨破你嘅舞鞋,等佢嘅單層鞋底磨損喇,笑話喺磨損後仲能留下,獨一無二。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可靠的機智,跟我玩這個笑話,直到你磨破你的舞鞋,等它的單層鞋底磨損了,笑話在磨損後還能留下,獨一無二。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: O single-soled jest, solely singular for the singleness!
passages.vernacular: 啊,單層鞋底嘅笑話,因其單薄而獨一無二!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,單層鞋底的笑話,因其單薄而獨一無二!

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Come between us, good Benvolio; my wits faint.
passages.vernacular: 喺我哋之間調解一下,好班伏里奧;我嘅機智暈喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我們之間調解一下,好班伏里奧;我的機智暈了。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Swits and spurs, swits and spurs; or I’ll cry a match.
passages.vernacular: 鞭子同馬刺,鞭子同馬刺;否則我要喊我贏喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鞭子與馬刺,鞭子與馬刺;否則我要喊我贏了。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Nay, if thy wits run the wild-goose chase, I am done.
passages.vernacular: 不,如果你嘅機智去追野鵝,我就完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,如果你的機智去追野鵝,我就完了。

passages.original: For thou hast more of the wild-goose in one of thy wits, than I am sure, I have in my whole five.
passages.vernacular: 因為你一個機智裡嘅野鵝,比我整個五個機智裡所有嘅仲多,我確信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你一個機智裡的野鵝,比我整個五個機智裡所有的還多,我確信。

passages.original: Was I with you there for the goose?
passages.vernacular: 我嗰時係唔係因為鵝而同你喺一起?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我那時是不是因為鵝而和你在一起?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Thou wast never with me for anything, when thou wast not there for the goose.
passages.vernacular: 你從來不因為任何事同我喺一起,除非你因為鵝而喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你從來不因為任何事和我在一起,除非你因為鵝而在。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: I will bite thee by the ear for that jest.
passages.vernacular: 為嗰個笑話我要咬你嘅耳朵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為那個笑話我要咬你的耳朵。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Nay, good goose, bite not.
passages.vernacular: 不,好鵝,別咬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,好鵝,別咬。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Thy wit is a very bitter sweeting, it is a most sharp sauce.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅機智係好苦嘅甜蘋果,係好辛辣嘅醬汁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的機智是很苦的甜蘋果,是很辛辣的醬汁。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: And is it not then well served in to a sweet goose?
passages.vernacular: 嗰佢不正適合配上一隻甜鵝嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那它不正適合配上一隻甜鵝嗎?

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: O here’s a wit of cheveril, that stretches from an inch narrow to an ell broad.
passages.vernacular: 啊,呢個係羊皮做嘅機智,從一寸窄伸展到一碼寬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,這是羊皮做的機智,從一寸窄伸展到一碼寬。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I stretch it out for that word broad, which added to the goose, proves thee far and wide a broad goose.
passages.vernacular: 我為「寬」呢個詞把佢伸展開,加到鵝上,證明你係個遠近聞名嘅寬鵝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為「寬」這個詞把它伸展開,加到鵝上,證明你是個遠近聞名的寬鵝。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Why, is not this better now than groaning for love?
passages.vernacular: 哎,呢不比為愛呻吟好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,這不比為愛呻吟好嗎?

passages.original: Now art thou sociable, now art thou Romeo; now art thou what thou art, by art as well as by nature.
passages.vernacular: 而家你合群喇,而家你係羅密歐;而家你係你本來嘅樣子,不但出於天性,都出於技巧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你合群了,現在你是羅密歐;現在你是你本來的樣子,不但出於天性,也出於技巧。

passages.original: For this drivelling love is like a great natural, that runs lolling up and down to hide his bauble in a hole.
passages.vernacular: 因為呢流口水嘅愛,就像一個大傻子,四處亂跑,吐住舌頭,把佢嘅小玩意兒藏進洞裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為這流口水的愛,就像一個大傻子,四處亂跑,吐著舌頭,把他的小玩意兒藏進洞裡。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Stop there, stop there.
passages.vernacular: 停喺嗰度,停喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 停在那裡,停在那裡。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Thou desirest me to stop in my tale against the hair.
passages.vernacular: 你要我喺講故事時逆住毛停下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要我在講故事時逆著毛停下。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Thou wouldst else have made thy tale large.
passages.vernacular: 不然你會把你嘅故事講大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不然你會把你的故事講大了。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: O, thou art deceived; I would have made it short, for I was come to the whole depth of my tale, and meant indeed to occupy the argument no longer.
passages.vernacular: 啊,你弄錯喇;我本想講短嘅,因為我已講到我故事嘅底喇,確實不打算再佔用呢個話題喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,你弄錯了;我本想講短的,因為我已說到我故事的底了,確實不打算再佔用這個話題了。

passages.original: Enter Nurse and Peter.
passages.vernacular: [奶媽同彼得上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奶媽與彼得上。]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Here’s goodly gear!
passages.vernacular: 好大嘅傢伙!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好大的傢伙!

passages.original: A sail, a sail!
passages.vernacular: 一艘帆,一艘帆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一艘帆,一艘帆!

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Two, two; a shirt and a smock.
passages.vernacular: 兩艘,兩艘;一件男襯衣,一件女襯衣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩艘,兩艘;一件男襯衣,一件女襯衣。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Peter!
passages.vernacular: 彼得!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得!

passages.title: Peter 彼得
passages.original: Anon.
passages.vernacular: 嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來了。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: My fan, Peter.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅扇子,彼得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的扇子,彼得。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Good Peter, to hide her face; for her fan’s the fairer face.
passages.vernacular: 好彼得,幫佢遮臉;因為佢嘅扇子比佢嘅臉漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好彼得,幫她遮臉;因為她的扇子比她的臉漂亮。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: God ye good morrow, gentlemen.
passages.vernacular: 願上帝賜你哋早安,先生哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上帝賜你們早安,先生們。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: God ye good-den, fair gentlewoman.
passages.vernacular: 願上帝賜你晚安(午安),美麗嘅女士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上帝賜你晚安(午安),美麗的女士。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Is it good-den?
passages.vernacular: 係午安嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是午安嗎?

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: ’Tis no less, I tell ye; for the bawdy hand of the dial is now upon the prick of noon.
passages.vernacular: 不早不晚,我告訴你;因為日晷上嗰淫蕩嘅指針,正指喺正午嘅刺上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不早不晚,我告訴你;因為日晷上那淫蕩的指針,正指在正午的刺上。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Out upon you!
passages.vernacular: 滾開!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滾開!

passages.original: What a man are you?
passages.vernacular: 你係乜嘢人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是什麼人?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: One, gentlewoman, that God hath made for himself to mar.
passages.vernacular: 一個,女士,上帝為佢自己創造嚟毀壞嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個,女士,上帝為他自己創造來毀壞的。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: By my troth, it is well said; for himself to mar, quoth a?
passages.vernacular: 我發誓,講得好;為佢自己毀壞,佢講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發誓,說得好;為他自己毀壞,他說?

passages.original: Gentlemen, can any of you tell me where I may find the young Romeo?
passages.vernacular: 先生哋,你哋邊個能告訴我邊度能找到年輕嘅羅密歐?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生們,你們誰能告訴我哪裡能找到年輕的羅密歐?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I can tell you: but young Romeo will be older when you have found him than he was when you sought him.
passages.vernacular: 我能告訴你:不過你找到佢嘅時候,年輕嘅羅密歐會比你找佢時老些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我能告訴你:可是你找到他的時候,年輕的羅密歐會比你找他時老些。

passages.original: I am the youngest of that name, for fault of a worse.
passages.vernacular: 我係呢名字中最年輕嘅,因為冇更壞嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是這名字中最年輕的,因為沒有更壞的了。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: You say well.
passages.vernacular: 你講得好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說得好。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Yea, is the worst well?
passages.vernacular: 係啊,最壞嘅都算好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是啊,最壞的也算好嗎?

passages.original: Very well took, i’faith; wisely, wisely.
passages.vernacular: 理解得好好,講真嘅;聰明,聰明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 理解得很好,說真的;聰明,聰明。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: If you be he, sir, I desire some confidence with you.
passages.vernacular: 如果你係佢,先生,我想同你私下講幾句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你是他,先生,我想和你私下說幾句話。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: She will endite him to some supper.
passages.vernacular: 佢要邀佢去食晚飯。
