passages.vernacularMandarin: 她要邀他去吃晚飯。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: A bawd, a bawd, a bawd! So ho!
passages.vernacular: 一個鴇母,一個鴇母,一個鴇母!嗬嗬!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個鴇母,一個鴇母,一個鴇母!嗬嗬!

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: What hast thou found?
passages.vernacular: 你發現咗乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你發現了什麼?

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: No hare, sir; unless a hare, sir, in a lenten pie, that is something stale and hoar ere it be spent. [Sings.]
passages.vernacular: 唔係野兔,先生;除非係四旬齋餡餅裡嘅野兔,喺食完以前,有點陳舊發霉。[唱。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是野兔,先生;除非是四旬齋餡餅裡的野兔,在吃完以前,有點陳舊發霉。[唱。]

passages.original: An old hare hoar, And an old hare hoar, Is very good meat in Lent;
passages.vernacular: 一隻老野兔發霉,一隻老野兔發霉,喺四旬齋裡係好好嘅肉;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻老野兔發霉,一隻老野兔發霉,在四旬齋裡是很好的肉;

passages.original: But a hare that is hoar Is too much for a score When it hoars ere it be spent.
passages.vernacular: 不過一隻發霉嘅野兔,對二十個銅錢來講太過喇,如果佢喺食完之前就發霉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是一隻發霉的野兔,對二十個銅錢來說太過了,如果它在吃完之前就發霉。

passages.original: Romeo, will you come to your father’s?
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐,你要去你父親家嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐,你要去你父親家嗎?

passages.original: We’ll to dinner thither.
passages.vernacular: 我哋到嗰度食午飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們到那裡吃午飯。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I will follow you.
passages.vernacular: 我隨後就嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我隨後就來。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Farewell, ancient lady; farewell, lady, lady, lady.
passages.vernacular: 再會,老夫人;再會,夫人,夫人,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會,老夫人;再會,夫人,夫人,夫人。

passages.original: [Exeunt Mercutio and Benvolio.]
passages.vernacular: [茂丘西奧同班伏里奧下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茂丘西奧與班伏里奧下。]

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: I pray you, sir, what saucy merchant was this that was so full of his ropery?
passages.vernacular: 請問,先生,呢位滿嘴下流話嘅放肆商人係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請問,先生,這位滿嘴下流話的放肆商人是誰?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: A gentleman, Nurse, that loves to hear himself talk, and will speak more in a minute than he will stand to in a month.
passages.vernacular: 一位紳士,奶媽,愛聽自己講話,一分鐘講嘅話比佢一個月能站得住嘅仲多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一位紳士,奶媽,愛聽自己說話,一分鐘說的話比他一個月能站得住的還多。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: And a speak anything against me, I’ll take him down, and a were lustier than he is, and twenty such Jacks.
passages.vernacular: 佢若敢講一句對我不利嘅話,我就收拾佢,邊怕佢比佢更壯,邊怕有二十個咁樣嘅小子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他若敢說一句對我不利的話,我就收拾他,哪怕他比他更壯,哪怕有二十個這樣的小子。

passages.original: And if I cannot, I’ll find those that shall.
passages.vernacular: 如果我辦唔到,我就找辦得到嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我辦不到,我就找辦得到的人。

passages.original: Scurvy knave!
passages.vernacular: 下流混蛋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下流混蛋!

passages.original: I am none of his flirt-gills; I am none of his skains-mates.—And thou must stand by too and suffer every knave to use me at his pleasure!
passages.vernacular: 我唔係佢嘅蕩婦;我唔係佢嘅惡棍夥伴。——你仲站喺一旁,讓每個流氓隨意擺佈我!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是他的蕩婦;我不是他的惡棍夥伴。——你還站在一旁,讓每個流氓隨意擺佈我!

passages.title: Peter 彼得
passages.original: I saw no man use you at his pleasure; if I had, my weapon should quickly have been out.
passages.vernacular: 我冇見任何人隨意擺佈你;如果見喇,我嘅武器早就出鞘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒見任何人隨意擺佈你;如果見了,我的武器早就出鞘了。

passages.original: I warrant you, I dare draw as soon as another man, if I see occasion in a good quarrel, and the law on my side.
passages.vernacular: 我保證,我敢跟別人一樣快拔劍,只要睇到有正當嘅爭吵,法律又站喺我呢邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我保證,我敢跟別人一樣快拔劍,只要看到有正當的爭吵,法律又站在我這邊。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Now, afore God, I am so vexed that every part about me quivers.
passages.vernacular: 而家,憑上帝,我氣得全身每個部分都發抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,憑上帝,我氣得全身每個部分都發抖。

passages.original: Scurvy knave.
passages.vernacular: 下流混蛋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下流混蛋。

passages.original: Pray you, sir, a word: and as I told you, my young lady bid me enquire you out;
passages.vernacular: 請你,先生,聽一句話:我跟你講過,我小姐叫我找你;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,先生,聽一句話:我跟你說過,我小姐叫我找你;

passages.original: what she bade me say, I will keep to myself.
passages.vernacular: 佢叫我講嘅話,我自己留住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她叫我說的話,我自己留著。

passages.original: But first let me tell ye, if ye should lead her in a fool’s paradise, as they say, it were a very gross kind of behaviour, as they say;
passages.vernacular: 但首先讓我告訴你,如果你把佢領進傻子嘅天堂,像人哋講嘅,嗰個就係好粗劣嘅行為,像人哋講嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但首先讓我告訴你,如果你把她領進傻子的天堂,像人們說的,那就是非常粗劣的行為,像人們說的;

passages.original: for the gentlewoman is young.
passages.vernacular: 因為呢位小姐年輕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為這位小姐年輕。

passages.original: And therefore, if you should deal double with her, truly it were an ill thing to be offered to any gentlewoman, and very weak dealing.
passages.vernacular: 所以,如果你對佢耍兩面手段,真嘅係對任何小姐都不該做嘅壞事,都係好軟弱嘅行徑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,如果你對她耍兩面手段,真的是對任何小姐都不該做的壞事,也是很軟弱的行徑。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Nurse, commend me to thy lady and mistress.
passages.vernacular: 奶媽,替我向你嘅小姐、你嘅主人問好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奶媽,替我向你的小姐、你的主人問好。

passages.original: I protest unto thee,—
passages.vernacular: 我向你保證,——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向你保證,——

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Good heart, and i’faith I will tell her as much.
passages.vernacular: 好心人,講真嘅我會咁告訴佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好心人,說真的我會這麼告訴她。

passages.original: Lord, Lord, she will be a joyful woman.
passages.vernacular: 天呀,天呀,佢會係個高興嘅女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,天哪,她會是個高興的女人。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: What wilt thou tell her, Nurse?
passages.vernacular: 你要告訴佢乜嘢,奶媽?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要告訴她什麼,奶媽?

passages.original: Thou dost not mark me.
passages.vernacular: 你冇注意聽我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒注意聽我。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: I will tell her, sir, that you do protest, which, as I take it, is a gentlemanlike offer.
passages.vernacular: 我會告訴佢,先生,你保證,我想,呢個係紳士嘅提議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會告訴她,先生,你保證,我想,這是紳士的提議。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Bid her devise Some means to come to shrift this afternoon, And there she shall at Friar Lawrence’ cell Be shriv’d and married.
passages.vernacular: 告訴佢想個辦法今日下午嚟懺悔,喺嗰度,喺勞倫斯神父嘅修室裡,佢將被赦免並結婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴她想個辦法今天下午來懺悔,在那裡,在勞倫斯神父的修室裡,她將被赦免並結婚。

passages.original: Here is for thy pains.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係畀你嘅辛苦錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是給你的辛苦錢。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: No truly, sir; not a penny.
passages.vernacular: 不,真嘅,先生;一個子兒都唔好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,真的,先生;一個子兒也不要。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Go to; I say you shall.
passages.vernacular: 去;我講你必須收。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去;我說你必須收。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: This afternoon, sir?
passages.vernacular: 今日下午,先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天下午,先生?

passages.original: Well, she shall be there.
passages.vernacular: 好,佢會到嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,她會到那裡。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: And stay, good Nurse, behind the abbey wall.
passages.vernacular: 好奶媽,你留喺修道院嘅牆後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好奶媽,你留在修道院的牆後面。

passages.original: Within this hour my man shall be with thee, And bring thee cords made like a tackled stair, Which to the high topgallant of my joy Must be my convoy in the secret night.
passages.vernacular: 一小時內我嘅僕人會嚟找你,畀你帶嚟做成繩梯嘅繩子,嗰將係我歡樂嘅高桅,喺秘密嘅夜裡我靠佢登上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一小時內我的僕人會來找你,給你帶來做成繩梯的繩子,那將是我歡樂的高桅,在秘密的夜裡我靠它登上去。

passages.original: Farewell, be trusty, and I’ll quit thy pains;
passages.vernacular: 再會,要忠實,我會報答你嘅辛苦;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會,要忠實,我會報答你的辛苦;

passages.original: Farewell; commend me to thy mistress.
passages.vernacular: 再會;替我向你嘅小姐問好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會;替我向你的小姐問好。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Now God in heaven bless thee.
passages.vernacular: 而家願天上嘅上帝祝福你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在願天上的上帝祝福你。

passages.original: Hark you, sir.
passages.vernacular: 聽住,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽著,先生。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: What say’st thou, my dear Nurse?
passages.vernacular: 你講乜嘢,我親愛嘅奶媽?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說什麼,我親愛的奶媽?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Is your man secret?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅僕人會保密嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的僕人會保密嗎?

passages.original: Did you ne’er hear say, Two may keep counsel, putting one away?
passages.vernacular: 你冇聽過人講,兩個人可以保守秘密,只要打發掉一個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒聽過人說,兩個人可以保守秘密,只要打發掉一個?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I warrant thee my man’s as true as steel.
passages.vernacular: 我向你保證,我嘅僕人像鋼一樣忠實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向你保證,我的僕人像鋼一樣忠實。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Well, sir, my mistress is the sweetest lady. Lord, Lord!
passages.vernacular: 好,先生,我家小姐係最甜美嘅小姐。天呀,天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,先生,我家小姐是最甜美的小姐。天哪,天哪!

passages.original: When ’twas a little prating thing,—O, there is a nobleman in town, one Paris, that would fain lay knife aboard;
passages.vernacular: 當佢定係個愛嘮叨嘅小嘢時,——啊,城裡有一位貴族,叫帕里斯,好想把刀放上船(求婚);
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當她還是個愛嘮叨的小東西時,——啊,城裡有一位貴族,叫帕里斯,很想把刀放上船(求婚);

passages.original: but she, good soul, had as lief see a toad, a very toad, as see him.
passages.vernacular: 但佢,好心嘅,寧願見一隻癩蛤蟆,一隻真正嘅癩蛤蟆,都唔願見佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她,好心的,寧願見一隻癩蛤蟆,一隻真正的癩蛤蟆,也不願見他。

passages.original: I anger her sometimes, and tell her that Paris is the properer man, but I’ll warrant you, when I say so, she looks as pale as any clout in the versal world.
passages.vernacular: 我有時惹佢生氣,講帕里斯係更體面嘅男人,不過我保證,我咁講時,佢臉色蒼白得像世上任何一塊破布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有時惹她生氣,說帕里斯是更體面的男人,可是我保證,我這麼說時,她臉色蒼白得像世上任何一塊破布。

passages.original: Doth not rosemary and Romeo begin both with a letter?
passages.vernacular: 迷迭香同羅密歐唔係都以同一個字母開頭嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 迷迭香和羅密歐不是都以同一個字母開頭嗎?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Ay, Nurse; what of that?
passages.vernacular: 係,奶媽;嗰又點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,奶媽;那又怎樣?

passages.original: Both with an R.
passages.vernacular: 都係R。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 都是R。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Ah, mocker!
passages.vernacular: 啊,愛取笑人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,愛取笑人!

passages.original: That’s the dog’s name.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係狗嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是狗的名字。

passages.original: R is for the—no, I know it begins with some other letter, and she hath the prettiest sententious of it, of you and rosemary, that it would do you good to hear it.
passages.vernacular: R係為喇——不,我知道佢係以別嘅字母開頭嘅,而佢對你同迷迭香有最漂亮嘅格言,你聽咗會好高興嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: R是為了——不,我知道它是以別的字母開頭的,而她對你和迷迭香有最漂亮的格言,你聽了會很高興的。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Commend me to thy lady.
passages.vernacular: 替我向你嘅小姐問好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 替我向你的小姐問好。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Ay, a thousand times. Peter!
passages.vernacular: 好,一千遍。彼得!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,一千遍。彼得!

passages.original: [Exit Romeo.]
passages.vernacular: [羅密歐下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅密歐下。]

passages.title: Peter 彼得
passages.original: Anon.
passages.vernacular: 嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來了。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Before and apace.
passages.vernacular: 前面走,快走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 前面走,快走。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene V — Capulet’s Garden 第二幕第五場:凱普雷特花園

passages.original: Enter Juliet.
passages.vernacular: [茱麗葉上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茱麗葉上。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: The clock struck nine when I did send the Nurse, In half an hour she promised to return.
passages.vernacular: 我派奶媽去時鐘敲九點,佢答應半小時內回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我派奶媽去時鐘敲九點,她答應半小時內回來。

passages.original: Perchance she cannot meet him.
passages.vernacular: 或者佢遇唔到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許她遇不到他。

passages.original: That’s not so.
passages.vernacular: 唔係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是這樣。

passages.original: O, she is lame.
passages.vernacular: 啊,佢係跛嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,她是跛的。

passages.original: Love’s heralds should be thoughts, Which ten times faster glides than the sun’s beams, Driving back shadows over lowering hills:
passages.vernacular: 愛嘅信使應該係思想,佢比陽光滑行得快十倍,把陰影驅趕回陰沉嘅山丘上:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛的信使應該是思想,它比陽光滑行得快十倍,把陰影驅趕回陰沉的山丘上:

passages.original: Therefore do nimble-pinion’d doves draw love, And therefore hath the wind-swift Cupid wings.
passages.vernacular: 所以輕翼嘅鴿子拉住愛,所以快似風嘅丘比特長住翅膀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以輕翼的鴿子拉著愛,所以快似風的丘比特長著翅膀。

passages.original: Now is the sun upon the highmost hill Of this day’s journey, and from nine till twelve Is three long hours, yet she is not come.
passages.vernacular: 而家太陽已喺今日行程嘅最高山上,從九點到十二點係三個長長嘅小時,佢仲冇嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在太陽已在今日行程的最高山上,從九點到十二點是三個長長的小時,她還沒來。

passages.original: Had she affections and warm youthful blood, She’d be as swift in motion as a ball;
passages.vernacular: 佢若有情感同溫熱嘅青春血液,就會像球一樣迅速移動;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她若有情感和溫熱的青春血液,就會像球一樣迅速移動;

passages.original: My words would bandy her to my sweet love, And his to me.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅話會把佢拋畀我嘅甜蜜愛人,佢嘅話再拋畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的話會把她拋給我的甜蜜愛人,他的話再拋給我。

passages.original: But old folks, many feign as they were dead; Unwieldy, slow, heavy and pale as lead.
passages.vernacular: 但老年人,許多都裝得像死咗一般;笨重、遲緩、沉重,蒼白如鉛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但老年人,許多都裝得像死了一般;笨重、遲緩、沉重,蒼白如鉛。

passages.original: Enter Nurse and Peter.
passages.vernacular: [奶媽同彼得上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奶媽與彼得上。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O God, she comes.
passages.vernacular: 啊上帝,佢嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊上帝,她來了。

passages.original: O honey Nurse, what news?
passages.vernacular: 啊,甜蜜嘅奶媽,有乜嘢消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,甜蜜的奶媽,有什麼消息?

passages.original: Hast thou met with him?
passages.vernacular: 你遇見佢咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你遇見他了嗎?

passages.original: Send thy man away.
passages.vernacular: 打發你嘅僕人走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 打發你的僕人走。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Peter, stay at the gate.
passages.vernacular: 彼得,你喺門口等住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得,你在門口等著。

passages.original: [Exit Peter.]
passages.vernacular: [彼得下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [彼得下。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Now, good sweet Nurse,—O Lord, why look’st thou sad?
passages.vernacular: 而家,好甜嘅奶媽,——天呀,你點解睇起嚟咁樣悲傷?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,好甜的奶媽,——天哪,你為什麼看起來這樣悲傷?

passages.original: Though news be sad, yet tell them merrily; If good, thou sham’st the music of sweet news By playing it to me with so sour a face.
passages.vernacular: 即使消息悲傷,都要快樂地講;如果係好嘅,你用咁酸嘅臉嚟向我奏佢,就辱冇咗好消息嘅音樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使消息悲傷,也要快樂地說;如果是好的,你用這麼酸的臉來向我奏它,就辱沒了好消息的音樂。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: I am aweary, give me leave awhile; Fie, how my bones ache!
passages.vernacular: 我累喇,讓我歇一會兒;哎,我嘅骨頭幾咁痛!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我累了,讓我歇一會兒;哎,我的骨頭多麼痛!

passages.original: What a jaunt have I had!
passages.vernacular: 我跑咗點樣嘅一趟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我跑了怎樣的一趟!

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: I would thou hadst my bones, and I thy news: Nay come, I pray thee speak; good, good Nurse, speak.
passages.vernacular: 我希望你有我嘅骨頭,我有你嘅消息:不,嚟,求你講;好奶媽,講吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你有我的骨頭,我有你的消息:不,來,求你說;好奶媽,說吧。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Jesu, what haste?
passages.vernacular: 耶穌,幾咁急躁!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 耶穌,多麼急躁!

passages.original: Can you not stay a while?
passages.vernacular: 你唔能夠等一會兒嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不能等一會兒嗎?

passages.original: Do you not see that I am out of breath?
passages.vernacular: 你冇睇見我上氣不接下氣嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒看見我上氣不接下氣嗎?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: How art thou out of breath, when thou hast breath To say to me that thou art out of breath?
passages.vernacular: 你點會上氣不接下氣,既然你有氣講你上氣不接下氣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼會上氣不接下氣,既然你有氣說你上氣不接下氣?

passages.original: The excuse that thou dost make in this delay Is longer than the tale thou dost excuse.
passages.vernacular: 你拖延時用嘅藉口,比你所辯解嘅故事仲長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你拖延時用的藉口,比你所辯解的故事還長。

passages.original: Is thy news good or bad?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅消息係好係壞?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的消息是好是壞?

passages.original: Answer to that; Say either, and I’ll stay the circumstance.
passages.vernacular: 回答呢個;講邊一個都行,我就不管細節喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回答這個;說哪一個都行,我就不管細節了。

passages.original: Let me be satisfied, is’t good or bad?
passages.vernacular: 讓我滿意,係好係壞?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我滿意,是好是壞?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Well, you have made a simple choice; you know not how to choose a man. Romeo? No, not he.
passages.vernacular: 好,你做咗個簡單嘅選擇;你不懂得點樣挑男人。羅密歐?不,唔係佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,你做了個簡單的選擇;你不懂得怎樣挑男人。羅密歐?不,不是他。

passages.original: Though his face be better than any man’s, yet his leg excels all men’s, and for a hand and a foot, and a body, though they be not to be talked on, yet they are past compare.
passages.vernacular: 雖然佢嘅臉比任何男人都好,不過佢嘅腿勝過所有男人,至於手、腳同身體,雖然不值一提,卻無可比擬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然他的臉比任何男人都好,可是他的腿勝過所有男人,至於手、腳和身體,雖然不值一提,卻無可比擬。

passages.original: He is not the flower of courtesy, but I’ll warrant him as gentle as a lamb.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係禮貌嘅精華,但我保證佢像羔羊一樣溫和。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不是禮貌的精華,但我保證他像羔羊一樣溫和。

passages.original: Go thy ways, wench, serve God.
passages.vernacular: 走你嘅路,丫頭,侍奉上帝去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走你的路,丫頭,侍奉上帝去。

passages.original: What, have you dined at home?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,你喺家食過飯咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,你在家吃過飯了嗎?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: No, no.
passages.vernacular: 冇,冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,沒有。

passages.original: But all this did I know before.
passages.vernacular: 呢一切我早就知道喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一切我早就知道了。

passages.original: What says he of our marriage?
passages.vernacular: 佢對我哋嘅婚事點講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對我們的婚事怎麼說?

passages.original: What of that?
passages.vernacular: 嗰算乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那算什麼?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Lord, how my head aches!
passages.vernacular: 天呀,我嘅頭多痛!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,我的頭多痛!

passages.original: What a head have I!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅頭點咁樣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的頭怎麼這樣!

passages.original: It beats as it would fall in twenty pieces.
passages.vernacular: 佢跳得好像要裂成二十塊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它跳得好像要裂成二十塊。

passages.original: My back o’ t’other side,—O my back, my back!
passages.vernacular: 我另一邊係背,——啊我嘅背,我嘅背!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我另一邊是背,——啊我的背,我的背!

passages.original: Beshrew your heart for sending me about To catch my death with jauncing up and down.
passages.vernacular: 該詛咒你嘅心,打發我到處跑,要喺上上下下顛簸中送命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 該詛咒你的心,打發我到處跑,要在上上下下顛簸中送命。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: I’faith, I am sorry that thou art not well.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,我好抱歉你不舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,我很抱歉你不舒服。

passages.original: Sweet, sweet, sweet Nurse, tell me, what says my love?
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅,親愛嘅,親愛嘅奶媽,告訴我,我嘅愛人講乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的,親愛的,親愛的奶媽,告訴我,我的愛人說什麼?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Your love says like an honest gentleman, And a courteous, and a kind, and a handsome, And I warrant a virtuous,—Where is your mother?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅愛人講得像個誠實嘅紳士,又有禮、又和善、又英俊,而且我保證又有德,——你母親喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的愛人說得像個誠實的紳士,又有禮、又和善、又英俊,而且我保證又有德,——你母親在哪裡?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Where is my mother?
passages.vernacular: 我母親喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我母親在哪裡?

passages.original: Why, she is within.
passages.vernacular: 哎,佢喺裡面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,她在裡面。

passages.original: Where should she be?
passages.vernacular: 佢仲能喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她還能在哪裡?

passages.original: How oddly thou repliest.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅回答幾咁古怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的回答多麼古怪。

passages.original: ‘Your love says, like an honest gentleman, ‘Where is your mother?’
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅愛人講得像個誠實嘅紳士,『你母親喺邊度?』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的愛人說得像個誠實的紳士,『你母親在哪裡?』」

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: O God’s lady dear, Are you so hot?
passages.vernacular: 啊聖母,你咁火急嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊聖母,你這麼火急嗎?

passages.original: Marry, come up, I trow.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,真嚟勁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,真來勁。

passages.original: Is this the poultice for my aching bones?
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係我痠痛骨頭嘅膏藥嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是我痠痛骨頭的膏藥嗎?

passages.original: Henceforward do your messages yourself.
passages.vernacular: 以後你自己去傳話吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以後你自己去傳話吧。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Here’s such a coil.
passages.vernacular: 好大嘅吵鬧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好大的吵鬧。

passages.original: Come, what says Romeo?
passages.vernacular: 嚟,羅密歐講乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,羅密歐說什麼?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Have you got leave to go to shrift today?
passages.vernacular: 你得到准許今日去懺悔咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你得到准許今天去懺悔了嗎?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: I have.
passages.vernacular: 得到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 得到了。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Then hie you hence to Friar Lawrence’ cell; There stays a husband to make you a wife.
passages.vernacular: 咁趕緊去勞倫斯神父嘅修室;嗰度有個丈夫等住使你成為妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼趕緊去勞倫斯神父的修室;那裡有個丈夫等著使你成為妻子。

passages.original: Now comes the wanton blood up in your cheeks, They’ll be in scarlet straight at any news.
passages.vernacular: 而家你臉頰上浮起咗任性嘅血,一聽到消息就會即刻變成緋紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你臉頰上浮起了任性的血,一聽到消息就會立刻變成緋紅。

passages.original: Hie you to church.
passages.vernacular: 趕緊去教堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 趕緊去教堂。

passages.original: I must another way, To fetch a ladder by the which your love Must climb a bird’s nest soon when it is dark.
passages.vernacular: 我必須走另一條路,去取一把梯子,你嘅愛人不久天黑時要靠佢爬上鳥巢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須走另一條路,去取一把梯子,你的愛人不久天黑時要靠它爬上鳥巢。

passages.original: I am the drudge, and toil in your delight; But you shall bear the burden soon at night. Go.
passages.vernacular: 我係苦工,為你嘅歡樂辛勞;但你不久晚上就要承受重擔。去吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是苦工,為你的歡樂辛勞;但你不久晚上就要承受重擔。去吧。

passages.original: I’ll to dinner; hie you to the cell.
passages.vernacular: 我去食飯;你趕緊去修室。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去吃飯;你趕緊去修室。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Hie to high fortune!
passages.vernacular: 趕去迎接高貴嘅運氣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 趕去迎接高貴的運氣!

passages.original: Honest Nurse, farewell.
passages.vernacular: 誠實嘅奶媽,再會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誠實的奶媽,再會。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene VI — Friar Lawrence’s Cell 第二幕第六場:勞倫斯神父的修室

passages.original: Enter Friar Lawrence and Romeo.
passages.vernacular: [勞倫斯神父同羅密歐上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [勞倫斯神父與羅密歐上。]

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: So smile the heavens upon this holy act That after-hours with sorrow chide us not.
passages.vernacular: 願上天對呢神聖嘅行為微笑,使往後嘅時辰唔好用悲傷責備我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上天對這神聖的行為微笑,使往後的時辰不要用悲傷責備我們。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Amen, amen, but come what sorrow can, It cannot countervail the exchange of joy That one short minute gives me in her sight.
passages.vernacular: 阿哋,阿哋,但無論乜嘢悲傷降臨,都抵不上我一眼見到佢嘅嗰短短一分鐘所畀我嘅歡樂交換。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿們,阿們,但無論什麼悲傷降臨,都抵不上我一眼見到她的那短短一分鐘所給我的歡樂交換。

passages.original: Do thou but close our hands with holy words, Then love-devouring death do what he dare, It is enough I may but call her mine.
passages.vernacular: 只要你用神聖嘅話把我哋嘅手連喺一起,然後讓吞噬愛嘅死亡儘管放膽去做,只要我能稱佢為我嘅,就足夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要你用神聖的話把我們的手連在一起,然後讓吞噬愛的死亡儘管放膽去做,只要我能稱她為我的,就足夠了。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: These violent delights have violent ends, And in their triumph die;
passages.vernacular: 呢啲激烈嘅歡樂有激烈嘅結局,喺勝利中死亡;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些激烈的歡樂有激烈的結局,在勝利中死亡;

passages.original: like fire and powder, Which as they kiss consume.
passages.vernacular: 像火同火藥,一親吻就同歸於盡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像火與火藥,一親吻就同歸於盡。

passages.original: The sweetest honey Is loathsome in his own deliciousness, And in the taste confounds the appetite.
passages.vernacular: 最甜嘅蜜糖喺佢自己嘅美味中令人作嘔,一嘗就敗咗胃口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最甜的蜜糖在它自己的美味中令人作嘔,一嘗就敗了胃口。

passages.original: Therefore love moderately: long love doth so;
passages.vernacular: 所以要適度地愛:長久嘅愛就係咁樣;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以要適度地愛:長久的愛就是這樣;

passages.original: Too swift arrives as tardy as too slow.
passages.vernacular: 太快到達同太慢一樣遲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太快到達和太慢一樣遲。

passages.original: Enter Juliet.
passages.vernacular: [茱麗葉上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茱麗葉上。]

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Here comes the lady.
passages.vernacular: 小姐嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姐來了。

passages.original: O, so light a foot Will ne’er wear out the everlasting flint.
passages.vernacular: 啊,咁輕嘅腳步,永遠磨不損嗰永恆嘅燧石。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,這麼輕的腳步,永遠磨不損那永恆的燧石。

passages.original: A lover may bestride the gossamers That idles in the wanton summer air And yet not fall; so light is vanity.
passages.vernacular: 戀人可以騎喺遊絲上,嗰喺放蕩嘅夏日空氣中飄蕩嘅遊絲,卻唔會掉下去;虛幻就係如此輕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戀人可以騎在遊絲上,那在放蕩的夏日空氣中飄蕩的遊絲,卻不會掉下去;虛幻就是如此輕。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Good even to my ghostly confessor.
passages.vernacular: 向我嘅神父懺悔師道聲晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 向我的神父懺悔師道聲晚安。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Romeo shall thank thee, daughter, for us both.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐會替我哋兩人謝你,女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐會替我們兩人謝你,女兒。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: As much to him, else is his thanks too much.
passages.vernacular: 我都同樣謝佢,否則佢嘅謝意就太多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也同樣謝他,否則他的謝意就太多了。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Ah, Juliet, if the measure of thy joy Be heap’d like mine, and that thy skill be more To blazon it, then sweeten with thy breath This neighbour air, and let rich music’s tongue Unfold the imagin’d happiness that both Receive in either by this dear encounter.
passages.vernacular: 啊,茱麗葉,如果你嘅歡樂嘅量像我嘅一樣堆積,而你嘅技巧更高,能把佢宣告出嚟,咁就用你嘅氣息使呢鄰近嘅空氣更甜,讓豐富音樂嘅舌頭,展現我哋兩人喺呢珍貴嘅相遇中彼此得到嘅想像中嘅幸福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,茱麗葉,如果你的歡樂的量像我的一樣堆積,而你的技巧更高,能把它宣告出來,那麼就用你的氣息使這鄰近的空氣更甜,讓豐富音樂的舌頭,展現我們兩人在這珍貴的相遇中彼此得到的想像中的幸福。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Conceit more rich in matter than in words, Brags of his substance, not of ornament.
passages.vernacular: 內涵比言辭更豐富嘅想法,誇耀佢嘅實質,而非裝飾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 內涵比言辭更豐富的想法,誇耀它的實質,而非裝飾。

passages.original: They are but beggars that can count their worth;
passages.vernacular: 只有乞丐才能數清自己嘅財富;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有乞丐才能數清自己的財富;

passages.original: But my true love is grown to such excess, I cannot sum up sum of half my wealth.
passages.vernacular: 但我真摯嘅愛已增長到如此過度,我連一半財富嘅總數都數不清。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我真摯的愛已增長到如此過度,我連一半財富的總數都數不清。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Come, come with me, and we will make short work, For, by your leaves, you shall not stay alone Till holy church incorporate two in one.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,跟我嚟,我哋要速戰速決,因為,恕我直言,喺神聖嘅教會把二人合為一體之前,你哋不可單獨待住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,跟我來,我們要速戰速決,因為,恕我直言,在神聖的教會把二人合為一體之前,你們不可單獨待著。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene I — A Public Place 第三幕第一場:公共場所

passages.original: Enter Mercutio, Benvolio, Page and Servants.
passages.vernacular: [茂丘西奧、班伏里奧、侍童同僕人哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茂丘西奧、班伏里奧、侍童和僕人們上。]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: I pray thee, good Mercutio, let’s retire: The day is hot, the Capulets abroad, And if we meet, we shall not scape a brawl, For now these hot days, is the mad blood stirring.
passages.vernacular: 求你,好茂丘西奧,我哋退下吧:天氣熱,凱普雷特家嘅人喺外,如果遇見,我哋逃不掉一場打鬥,因為呢啲大熱天,瘋狂嘅血正在湧動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求你,好茂丘西奧,我們退下吧:天氣熱,凱普雷特家的人在外,如果遇見,我們逃不掉一場打鬥,因為這些大熱天,瘋狂的血正在湧動。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Thou art like one of these fellows that, when he enters the confines of a tavern, claps me his sword upon the table, and says ‘God send me no need of thee!’
passages.vernacular: 你像嗰啲傢伙之一,一進酒館嘅範圍,就把劍啪地放喺桌上,講「上帝保佑我不需要你!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你像那些傢伙之一,一進酒館的範圍,就把劍啪地放在桌上,說「上帝保佑我不需要你!」

passages.original: and by the operation of the second cup draws him on the drawer, when indeed there is no need.
passages.vernacular: 而第二杯酒一發作,就對酒保拔劍,其實根本冇需要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而第二杯酒一發作,就對酒保拔劍,其實根本沒有需要。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Am I like such a fellow?
passages.vernacular: 我像呢種傢伙嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我像這種傢伙嗎?

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Come, come, thou art as hot a Jack in thy mood as any in Italy;
passages.vernacular: 嚟,嚟,你嘅脾氣比意大利任何人都火爆;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,來,你的脾氣比意大利任何人都火爆;

passages.original: and as soon moved to be moody, and as soon moody to be moved.
passages.vernacular: 一被惹怒就變得暴躁,一暴躁就被惹怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一被惹怒就變得暴躁,一暴躁就被惹怒。

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: And what to?
passages.vernacular: 然後呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後呢?

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Nay, an there were two such, we should have none shortly, for one would kill the other. Thou?
passages.vernacular: 不,要係有兩個咁樣嘅人,我哋好快就一個都冇喇,因為一個會殺死另一個。你?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,要是有兩個這樣的人,我們很快就一個也沒有了,因為一個會殺死另一個。你?

passages.original: Why, thou wilt quarrel with a man that hath a hair more or a hair less in his beard than thou hast.
passages.vernacular: 哎,你會跟鬍子比你多一根或少一根頭髮嘅人吵架。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,你會跟鬍子比你多一根或少一根頭髮的人吵架。

passages.original: Thou wilt quarrel with a man for cracking nuts, having no other reason but because thou hast hazel eyes.
passages.vernacular: 你會因為一個人剝堅果而跟佢吵,除咗你有榛色嘅眼睛之外冇別嘅理由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會因為一個人剝堅果而跟他吵,除了你有榛色的眼睛之外沒有別的理由。

passages.original: What eye but such an eye would spy out such a quarrel?
passages.vernacular: 除咗咁樣嘅眼睛,仲有乜嘢眼睛能窺出咁樣嘅爭吵?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了這樣的眼睛,還有什麼眼睛能窺出這樣的爭吵?

passages.original: Thy head is as full of quarrels as an egg is full of meat, and yet thy head hath been beaten as addle as an egg for quarrelling.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅腦袋裡爭吵多得像蛋裡嘅蛋黃,不過你嘅腦袋因為爭吵被打得像臭蛋一樣爛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的腦袋裡爭吵多得像蛋裡的蛋黃,可是你的腦袋因為爭吵被打得像臭蛋一樣爛。

passages.original: Thou hast quarrelled with a man for coughing in the street, because he hath wakened thy dog that hath lain asleep in the sun.
passages.vernacular: 你曾因一個人喺街上咳嗽而跟佢吵,因為佢吵醒咗喺太陽下瞓覺嘅你嘅狗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你曾因一個人在街上咳嗽而跟他吵,因為他吵醒了在太陽下睡覺的你的狗。

passages.original: Didst thou not fall out with a tailor for wearing his new doublet before Easter?
passages.vernacular: 你唔係跟一個裁縫吵過,因為佢喺復活節前穿新上衣嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不是跟一個裁縫吵過,因為他在復活節前穿新上衣嗎?

passages.original: with another for tying his new shoes with an old riband?
passages.vernacular: 跟另一個吵,因為佢用舊絲帶繫新鞋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟另一個吵,因為他用舊絲帶繫新鞋?

passages.original: And yet thou wilt tutor me from quarrelling!
passages.vernacular: 不過你仲要教我戒掉吵架!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是你還要教我戒掉吵架!

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: And I were so apt to quarrel as thou art, any man should buy the fee simple of my life for an hour and a quarter.
passages.vernacular: 如果我像你一樣愛吵架,任何人都能花一小時一刻鐘買下我生命嘅完全產權。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我像你一樣愛吵架,任何人都能花一小時一刻鐘買下我生命的完全產權。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: The fee simple! O simple!
passages.vernacular: 完全產權!啊,簡單!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 完全產權!啊,簡單!

passages.original: Enter Tybalt and others.
passages.vernacular: [提伯特同其他人上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [提伯特與其他人上。]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: By my head, here comes the Capulets.
passages.vernacular: 憑我嘅頭,凱普雷特家嘅人嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑我的頭,凱普雷特家的人來了。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: By my heel, I care not.
passages.vernacular: 憑我嘅腳跟,我不在乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑我的腳跟,我不在乎。

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: Follow me close, for I will speak to them.
passages.vernacular: 緊跟住我,因為我要跟佢哋講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 緊跟著我,因為我要跟他們說話。

passages.original: Gentlemen, good-den: a word with one of you.
passages.vernacular: 先生哋,晚安:跟你哋其中一位講句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生們,晚安:跟你們其中一位說句話。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: And but one word with one of us?
passages.vernacular: 只跟我哋中嘅一個講一句話?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只跟我們中的一個說一句話?

passages.original: Couple it with something; make it a word and a blow.
passages.vernacular: 加點別嘅;讓佢係一句話加一拳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 加點別的;讓它是一句話加一拳。

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: You shall find me apt enough to that, sir, and you will give me occasion.
passages.vernacular: 你會發現我好願意,先生,只要你畀我機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會發現我很願意,先生,只要你給我機會。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Could you not take some occasion without giving?
passages.vernacular: 你唔能夠唔使別人畀,自己找個機會嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不能不用別人給,自己找個機會嗎?

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: Mercutio, thou consortest with Romeo.
passages.vernacular: 茂丘西奧,你同羅密歐係一夥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 茂丘西奧,你和羅密歐是一夥。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Consort?
passages.vernacular: 一夥?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一夥?

passages.original: What, dost thou make us minstrels?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,你把我哋當樂師嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,你把我們當樂師嗎?

passages.original: And thou make minstrels of us, look to hear nothing but discords.
passages.vernacular: 你若把我哋當樂師,就等住聽到乜嘢都冇,只有不和諧嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你若把我們當樂師,就等著聽到什麼都沒有,只有不和諧的聲音。

passages.original: Here’s my fiddlestick, here’s that shall make you dance.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我嘅琴弓,呢就會讓你跳舞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我的琴弓,這就會讓你跳舞。

passages.original: Zounds, consort!
passages.vernacular: 天呀,一夥!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,一夥!

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: We talk here in the public haunt of men.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺呢度係喺人群出冇嘅公共場所講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在這裡是在人群出沒的公共場所說話。

passages.original: Either withdraw unto some private place, And reason coldly of your grievances, Or else depart;
passages.vernacular: 要麼退到一個私人地方,冷靜地論你哋嘅怨恨,要麼就走開;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要麼退到一個私人地方,冷靜地論你們的怨恨,要麼就走開;

passages.original: here all eyes gaze on us.
passages.vernacular: 呢度所有眼睛都喺盯住我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡所有眼睛都在盯著我們。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Men’s eyes were made to look, and let them gaze.
passages.vernacular: 人嘅眼睛生來就係睇嘅,讓佢哋睇吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人的眼睛生來就是看的,讓他們看吧。

passages.original: I will not budge for no man’s pleasure, I.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會為任何人嘅高興挪動一步,我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會為任何人的高興挪動一步,我。

passages.original: Enter Romeo.
passages.vernacular: [羅密歐上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅密歐上。]

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: Well, peace be with you, sir, here comes my man.
passages.vernacular: 好,願平安同你同喺,先生,我要找嘅人嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,願平安與你同在,先生,我要找的人來了。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: But I’ll be hanged, sir, if he wear your livery.
passages.vernacular: 但我若係上吊,先生,佢穿你嘅號衣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我若是上吊,先生,他穿你的號衣。

passages.original: Marry, go before to field, he’ll be your follower;
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,先走到決鬥場去,佢會係你嘅跟隨者;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,先走到決鬥場去,他會是你的跟隨者;

passages.original: Your worship in that sense may call him man.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢個意義上,閣下可以稱佢為「你嘅人」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這個意義上,閣下可以稱他為「你的人」。

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: Romeo, the love I bear thee can afford No better term than this: Thou art a villain.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐,我對你嘅愛,只能畀你呢個稱呼:你係個惡棍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐,我對你的愛,只能給你這個稱呼:你是個惡棍。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Tybalt, the reason that I have to love thee Doth much excuse the appertaining rage To such a greeting.
passages.vernacular: 提伯特,我有理由愛你,足以大大原諒對呢種招呼應有嘅憤怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提伯特,我有理由愛你,足以大大原諒對這種招呼應有的憤怒。

passages.original: Villain am I none; Therefore farewell; I see thou know’st me not.
passages.vernacular: 我唔係惡棍;所以再會;我睇你不認識我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是惡棍;所以再會;我看你不認識我。

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: Boy, this shall not excuse the injuries That thou hast done me, therefore turn and draw.
passages.vernacular: 細路,呢唔能夠原諒你對我所做嘅傷害,所以轉身拔劍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子,這不能原諒你對我所做的傷害,所以轉身拔劍。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I do protest I never injur’d thee, But love thee better than thou canst devise Till thou shalt know the reason of my love.
passages.vernacular: 我鄭重聲明我從未傷害你,卻比你所能想像嘅更愛你,直到你知道我愛嘅理由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我鄭重聲明我從未傷害你,卻比你所能想像的更愛你,直到你知道我愛的理由。

passages.original: And so good Capulet, which name I tender As dearly as mine own, be satisfied.
passages.vernacular: 所以好凱普雷特,呢個姓我像愛自己嘅一樣珍視,請滿意吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以好凱普雷特,這個姓我像愛自己的一樣珍視,請滿意吧。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: O calm, dishonourable, vile submission! [Draws.]
passages.vernacular: 啊,平靜、無恥、卑鄙嘅屈服![拔劍。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,平靜、無恥、卑鄙的屈服![拔劍。]

passages.original: Alla stoccata carries it away.
passages.vernacular: 阿拉斯托卡塔(刺擊)決定喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿拉斯托卡塔(刺擊)決定了。

passages.original: Tybalt, you rat-catcher, will you walk?
passages.vernacular: 提伯特,你呢捕鼠人,你要走一趟嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提伯特,你這捕鼠人,你要走一趟嗎?

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: What wouldst thou have with me?
passages.vernacular: 你想從我呢得到乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想從我這得到什麼?

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Good King of Cats, nothing but one of your nine lives;
passages.vernacular: 好貓王,只要你九條命中嘅一條;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好貓王,只要你九條命中的一條;

passages.original: that I mean to make bold withal, and, as you shall use me hereafter, dry-beat the rest of the eight.
passages.vernacular: 我打算冒昧攞佢,並且視你以後點樣對我,把其餘八條都痛打乾淨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我打算冒昧拿它,並且視你以後怎樣對我,把其餘八條也痛打乾淨。

passages.original: Will you pluck your sword out of his pilcher by the ears?
passages.vernacular: 你要把你嘅劍從佢嘅劍鞘(魚桶)裡拔耳朵拉出嚟嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要把你的劍從它的劍鞘(魚桶)裡拔耳朵拉出來嗎?

passages.original: Make haste, lest mine be about your ears ere it be out.
passages.vernacular: 快點,免得我嘅劍喺你拔出之前就落喺你耳邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快點,免得我的劍在你拔出之前就落在你耳邊。

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: [Drawing.]
passages.vernacular: [拔劍。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [拔劍。]

passages.original: I am for you.
passages.vernacular: 我奉陪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我奉陪。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Gentle Mercutio, put thy rapier up.
passages.vernacular: 溫和嘅茂丘西奧,收起你嘅劍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫和的茂丘西奧,收起你的劍。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Come, sir, your passado.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,先生,你嘅前進刺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,先生,你的前進刺。

passages.original: [They fight.]
passages.vernacular: [二人交戰。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [二人交戰。]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Draw, Benvolio; beat down their weapons.
passages.vernacular: 拔劍,班伏里奧;打落佢哋嘅武器。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拔劍,班伏里奧;打落他們的武器。

passages.original: Gentlemen, for shame, forbear this outrage, Tybalt, Mercutio, the Prince expressly hath Forbid this bandying in Verona streets.
passages.vernacular: 先生哋,真丟臉,住手呢種暴行,提伯特,茂丘西奧,親王已明令禁止喺維洛嗰街頭呢種互相揮劍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生們,真丟臉,住手這種暴行,提伯特,茂丘西奧,親王已明令禁止在維洛那街頭這種互相揮劍。

passages.original: Hold, Tybalt!
passages.vernacular: 住手,提伯特!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 住手,提伯特!

passages.original: Good Mercutio!
passages.vernacular: 好茂丘西奧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好茂丘西奧!

passages.original: [Exeunt Tybalt with his Partizans.]
passages.vernacular: [提伯特同佢嘅黨徒下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [提伯特與他的黨徒下。]

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: I am hurt.
passages.vernacular: 我受傷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我受傷了。

passages.original: A plague o’ both your houses. I am sped.
passages.vernacular: 願兩家都遭瘟疫。我完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願兩家都遭瘟疫。我完了。

passages.original: Is he gone, and hath nothing?
passages.vernacular: 佢走喇,乜嘢都冇受傷嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走了,什麼也沒受傷嗎?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: What, art thou hurt?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,你受傷咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,你受傷了嗎?

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Ay, ay, a scratch, a scratch.
passages.vernacular: 係,係,一道擦傷,一道擦傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,是,一道擦傷,一道擦傷。

passages.original: Marry, ’tis enough.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,夠了。

passages.original: Where is my page?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅侍童喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的侍童在哪裡?

passages.original: Go villain, fetch a surgeon.
passages.vernacular: 去,混蛋,去請外科醫生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,混蛋,去請外科醫生。

passages.original: [Exit Page.]
passages.vernacular: [侍童下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [侍童下。]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Courage, man; the hurt cannot be much.
passages.vernacular: 勇敢點,老兄;傷唔會太重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勇敢點,老兄;傷不會太重。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: No, ’tis not so deep as a well, nor so wide as a church door, but ’tis enough, ’twill serve.
passages.vernacular: 不,不像井咁深,不像教堂門咁寬,但夠喇,足夠用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,不像井那麼深,不像教堂門那麼寬,但夠了,足夠用。

passages.original: Ask for me tomorrow, and you shall find me a grave man.
passages.vernacular: 聽日嚟問我,你會發現我係個「沉重」(墳墓)嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明天來問我,你會發現我是個「沉重」(墳墓)的人。

passages.original: I am peppered, I warrant, for this world.
passages.vernacular: 我被灑咗胡椒,我保證,對呢世界來講完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被灑了胡椒,我保證,對這世界來說完了。

passages.original: A plague o’ both your houses.
passages.vernacular: 願兩家都遭瘟疫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願兩家都遭瘟疫。

passages.original: Zounds, a dog, a rat, a mouse, a cat, to scratch a man to death.
passages.vernacular: 天呀,一條狗,一隻老鼠,一隻小鼠,一隻貓,竟能抓死一個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,一條狗,一隻老鼠,一隻小鼠,一隻貓,竟能抓死一個人。

passages.original: A braggart, a rogue, a villain, that fights by the book of arithmetic!—Why the devil came you between us?
passages.vernacular: 一個吹牛嘅,一個無賴,一個惡棍,按算術書打架!——魔鬼點解介入我哋之間?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個吹牛的,一個無賴,一個惡棍,按算術書打架!——魔鬼為什麼介入我們之間?

passages.original: I was hurt under your arm.
passages.vernacular: 我係喺你胳膊下被刺傷嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是在你胳膊下被刺傷的。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I thought all for the best.
passages.vernacular: 我以為都係為了最好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以為都是為了最好。

passages.title: Mercutio 茂丘西奧
passages.original: Help me into some house, Benvolio, Or I shall faint.
passages.vernacular: 扶我進邊間屋子,班伏里奧,否則我要暈喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 扶我進哪間屋子,班伏里奧,否則我要暈了。

passages.original: A plague o’ both your houses.
passages.vernacular: 願兩家都遭瘟疫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願兩家都遭瘟疫。

passages.original: They have made worms’ meat of me.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋把我變成咗蛆嘅食物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們把我變成了蛆的食物。

passages.original: I have it, and soundly too.
passages.vernacular: 我受咗傷,而且傷得好重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我受了傷,而且傷得很重。

passages.original: Your houses!
passages.vernacular: 你哋兩家!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們兩家!

passages.original: [Exeunt Mercutio and Benvolio.]
passages.vernacular: [茂丘西奧同班伏里奧下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茂丘西奧與班伏里奧下。]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: This gentleman, the Prince’s near ally, My very friend, hath got his mortal hurt In my behalf;
passages.vernacular: 呢位紳士,親王嘅近親,我真正嘅朋友,為了我而受咗致命傷;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這位紳士,親王的近親,我真正的朋友,為了我而受了致命傷;

passages.original: my reputation stain’d With Tybalt’s slander,—Tybalt, that an hour Hath been my cousin.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅名譽被提伯特嘅誹謗玷污,——提伯特,一小時前定係我嘅親戚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的名譽被提伯特的誹謗玷污,——提伯特,一小時前還是我的親戚。

passages.original: O sweet Juliet, Thy beauty hath made me effeminate And in my temper soften’d valour’s steel.
passages.vernacular: 啊,親愛嘅茱麗葉,你嘅美使我變得女氣,軟化咗我性情中勇氣嘅鋼鐵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,親愛的茱麗葉,你的美使我變得女氣,軟化了我性情中勇氣的鋼鐵。

passages.original: Re-enter Benvolio.
passages.vernacular: [班伏里奧重上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [班伏里奧重上。]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: O Romeo, Romeo, brave Mercutio’s dead, That gallant spirit hath aspir’d the clouds, Which too untimely here did scorn the earth.
passages.vernacular: 啊羅密歐,羅密歐,勇敢嘅茂丘西奧死喇,嗰高尚嘅靈魂已升入雲霄,佢太早喺呢度蔑視大地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊羅密歐,羅密歐,勇敢的茂丘西奧死了,那高尚的靈魂已升入雲霄,他太早在這裡蔑視大地。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: This day’s black fate on mo days doth depend;
passages.vernacular: 今日嘅黑暗命運仲要牽連更多嘅日子;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天的黑暗命運還要牽連更多的日子;

passages.original: This but begins the woe others must end.
passages.vernacular: 呢不過係開始,其他人必須結束呢悲哀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不過是開始,其他人必須結束這悲哀。

passages.original: Re-enter Tybalt.
passages.vernacular: [提伯特重上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [提伯特重上。]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Here comes the furious Tybalt back again.
passages.vernacular: 狂怒嘅提伯特又回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狂怒的提伯特又回來了。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Again in triumph, and Mercutio slain?
passages.vernacular: 又嚟得意洋洋,而茂丘西奧被殺?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又來得意洋洋,而茂丘西奧被殺?

passages.original: Away to heaven respective lenity, And fire-ey’d fury be my conduct now!
passages.vernacular: 把顧忌嘅寬厚送去天上,讓火眼嘅狂怒做我而家嘅嚮導!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把顧忌的寬厚送去天上,讓火眼的狂怒做我現在的嚮導!

passages.original: Now, Tybalt, take the ‘villain’ back again That late thou gav’st me, for Mercutio’s soul Is but a little way above our heads, Staying for thine to keep him company.
passages.vernacular: 而家,提伯特,把你頭先畀我嘅「惡棍」收回去,因為茂丘西奧嘅靈魂就喺我哋頭上不遠處,等住你嘅靈魂去作伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,提伯特,把你剛才給我的「惡棍」收回去,因為茂丘西奧的靈魂就在我們頭上不遠處,等著你的靈魂去作伴。

passages.original: Either thou or I, or both, must go with him.
passages.vernacular: 要麼你,要麼我,要麼兩個人,都得跟佢去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要麼你,要麼我,要麼兩個人,都得跟他去。

passages.title: Tybalt 提伯特
passages.original: Thou wretched boy, that didst consort him here, Shalt with him hence.
passages.vernacular: 你呢個同佢為伍嘅可憐細路,將同佢一起離開呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這個與他為伍的可憐孩子,將與他一起離開這裡。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: This shall determine that.
passages.vernacular: 呢個將決定嗰個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個將決定那個。

passages.original: [They fight; Tybalt falls.]
passages.vernacular: [二人交戰;提伯特倒下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [二人交戰;提伯特倒下。]

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Romeo, away, be gone!
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐,快走,離開!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐,快走,離開!

passages.original: The citizens are up, and Tybalt slain.
passages.vernacular: 市民哋都起嚟喇,提伯特被殺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 市民們都起來了,提伯特被殺。

passages.original: Stand not amaz’d.
passages.vernacular: 別愣喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別愣在那裡。

passages.original: The Prince will doom thee death If thou art taken.
passages.vernacular: 如果你被捕,親王會判你死刑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你被捕,親王會判你死刑。

passages.original: Hence, be gone, away!
passages.vernacular: 快走,離開,走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快走,離開,走!

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: O, I am fortune’s fool!
passages.vernacular: 啊,我係命運嘅傻瓜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我是命運的傻瓜!

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Why dost thou stay?
passages.vernacular: 你點解仲站住?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼還站著?

passages.original: [Exit Romeo.]
passages.vernacular: [羅密歐下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅密歐下。]

passages.original: Enter Citizens.
passages.vernacular: [市民哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [市民們上。]

passages.title: First Citizen 第一市民
passages.original: Which way ran he that kill’d Mercutio?
passages.vernacular: 殺死茂丘西奧嘅人往邊邊跑喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殺死茂丘西奧的人往哪邊跑了?

passages.original: Tybalt, that murderer, which way ran he?
passages.vernacular: 提伯特,嗰個兇手,往邊邊跑喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提伯特,那個兇手,往哪邊跑了?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: There lies that Tybalt.
passages.vernacular: 提伯特躺喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提伯特躺在那裡。

passages.title: First Citizen 第一市民
passages.original: Up, sir, go with me.
passages.vernacular: 起嚟,先生,跟我走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起來,先生,跟我走。

passages.original: I charge thee in the Prince’s name obey.
passages.vernacular: 我以親王嘅名義命令你服從。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以親王的名義命令你服從。

passages.original: Enter Prince, attended; Montague, Capulet, their Wives and others.
passages.vernacular: [親王偕侍從上;蒙太古、凱普雷特、佢哋嘅夫人同其他人上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [親王偕侍從上;蒙太古、凱普雷特、他們的夫人和其他人上。]

passages.title: Prince 親王
passages.original: Where are the vile beginners of this fray?
passages.vernacular: 呢場鬥毆嘅惡劣肇事者喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這場鬥毆的惡劣肇事者在哪裡?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: O noble Prince, I can discover all The unlucky manage of this fatal brawl.
passages.vernacular: 啊高貴嘅親王,我能揭露呢場致命鬥毆不幸嘅全部經過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊高貴的親王,我能揭露這場致命鬥毆不幸的全部經過。

passages.original: There lies the man, slain by young Romeo, That slew thy kinsman, brave Mercutio.
passages.vernacular: 嗰度躺住被年輕羅密歐所殺嘅人,佢殺咗你嘅親戚,勇敢嘅茂丘西奧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡躺著被年輕羅密歐所殺的人,他殺了你的親戚,勇敢的茂丘西奧。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Tybalt, my cousin!
passages.vernacular: 提伯特,我嘅侄兒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提伯特,我的侄兒!

passages.original: O my brother’s child! O Prince! O husband!
passages.vernacular: 啊我哥哥嘅細路!啊親王!啊丈夫!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊我哥哥的孩子!啊親王!啊丈夫!

passages.original: O, the blood is spill’d Of my dear kinsman!
passages.vernacular: 啊,我親愛嘅親戚嘅血被流喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我親愛的親戚的血被流了!

passages.original: Prince, as thou art true, For blood of ours shed blood of Montague.
passages.vernacular: 親王,如你係公正嘅,為我哋嘅血,讓蒙太古嘅血流吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親王,如你是公正的,為我們的血,讓蒙太古的血流吧。

passages.original: O cousin, cousin.
passages.vernacular: 啊堂兄,堂兄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊堂兄,堂兄。

passages.title: Prince 親王
passages.original: Benvolio, who began this bloody fray?
passages.vernacular: 班伏里奧,邊個挑起呢場血腥嘅鬥毆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班伏里奧,誰挑起這場血腥的鬥毆?

passages.title: Benvolio 班伏里奧
passages.original: Tybalt, here slain, whom Romeo’s hand did slay;
passages.vernacular: 提伯特,喺呢度被殺,佢被羅密歐嘅手所殺;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提伯特,在這裡被殺,他被羅密歐的手所殺;

passages.original: Romeo, that spoke him fair, bid him bethink How nice the quarrel was, and urg’d withal Your high displeasure.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐好言勸佢,叫佢想想呢爭吵幾咁微不足道,並且提到您嘅重大不悅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐好言勸他,叫他想想這爭吵多麼微不足道,並且提到您的重大不悅。

passages.original: All this uttered With gentle breath, calm look, knees humbly bow’d Could not take truce with the unruly spleen Of Tybalt, deaf to peace, but that he tilts With piercing steel at bold Mercutio’s breast, Who, all as hot, turns deadly point to point, And, with a martial scorn, with one hand beats Cold death aside, and with the other sends It back to Tybalt, whose dexterity Retorts it.
passages.vernacular: 呢一切用溫和嘅氣息、平靜嘅神情、謙卑彎下嘅膝蓋講出,卻無法同提伯特不馴嘅脾氣達成停戰,佢聽不進和平,卻用鋒利嘅鋼劍直刺勇敢嘅茂丘西奧嘅胸膛,茂丘西奧同樣火爆,以致命嘅劍尖還擊,帶住軍人嘅輕蔑,一隻手撥開冰冷嘅死亡,另一隻手把佢送回提伯特,提伯特以靈巧回敬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一切用溫和的氣息、平靜的神情、謙卑彎下的膝蓋說出,卻無法與提伯特不馴的脾氣達成停戰,他聽不進和平,卻用鋒利的鋼劍直刺勇敢的茂丘西奧的胸膛,茂丘西奧同樣火爆,以致命的劍尖還擊,帶著軍人的輕蔑,一隻手撥開冰冷的死亡,另一隻手把它送回提伯特,提伯特以靈巧回敬。

passages.original: Romeo he cries aloud, ‘Hold, friends!
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐大聲喊:「住手,朋友哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐大聲喊:「住手,朋友們!

passages.original: Friends, part!’
passages.vernacular: 朋友哋,分開!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 朋友們,分開!」

passages.original: and swifter than his tongue, His agile arm beats down their fatal points, And ’twixt them rushes;
passages.vernacular: 佢比舌頭更快,用敏捷嘅手臂打落佢哋致命嘅劍尖,衝到佢哋中間;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他比舌頭更快,用敏捷的手臂打落他們致命的劍尖,衝到他們中間;

passages.original: underneath whose arm An envious thrust from Tybalt hit the life Of stout Mercutio, and then Tybalt fled.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢嘅手臂下,提伯特一記惡毒嘅刺擊刺中咗壯實嘅茂丘西奧嘅生命,然後提伯特逃走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他的手臂下,提伯特一記惡毒的刺擊刺中了壯實的茂丘西奧的生命,然後提伯特逃走。

passages.original: But by and by comes back to Romeo, Who had but newly entertain’d revenge, And to’t they go like lightning;
passages.vernacular: 但不久又回嚟找羅密歐,嗰時羅密歐才啱啱想要報仇,兩人像閃電般打起嚟;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但不久又回來找羅密歐,那時羅密歐才剛剛想要報仇,兩人像閃電般打起來;

passages.original: for, ere I Could draw to part them was stout Tybalt slain;
passages.vernacular: 因為,喺我拔劍去分開佢哋之前,壯實嘅提伯特就被殺喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為,在我拔劍去分開他們之前,壯實的提伯特就被殺了;

passages.original: And as he fell did Romeo turn and fly.
passages.vernacular: 佢倒下時,羅密歐轉身逃走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他倒下時,羅密歐轉身逃走。

passages.original: This is the truth, or let Benvolio die.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係真話,否則讓班伏里奧去死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是真話,否則讓班伏里奧去死。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: He is a kinsman to the Montague.
passages.vernacular: 佢係蒙太古嘅親戚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是蒙太古的親戚。

passages.original: Affection makes him false, he speaks not true.
passages.vernacular: 感情使佢講假話,佢講嘅唔係真話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 感情使他說假話,他說的不是真話。

passages.original: Some twenty of them fought in this black strife, And all those twenty could but kill one life.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋大約二十個人參加咗呢場黑暗嘅爭鬥,而呢二十人合起嚟只殺咗一條命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們大約二十個人參加了這場黑暗的爭鬥,而這二十人合起來只殺了一條命。

passages.original: I beg for justice, which thou, Prince, must give;
passages.vernacular: 我乞求公正,親王,您必須畀予;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我乞求公正,親王,您必須給予;

passages.original: Romeo slew Tybalt, Romeo must not live.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐殺咗提伯特,羅密歐唔能夠活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐殺了提伯特,羅密歐不能活。

passages.title: Prince 親王
passages.original: Romeo slew him, he slew Mercutio.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐殺咗佢,佢殺咗茂丘西奧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐殺了他,他殺了茂丘西奧。

passages.original: Who now the price of his dear blood doth owe?
passages.vernacular: 而家邊個嚟償還佢寶貴之血嘅代價?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在誰來償還他寶貴之血的代價?

passages.title: Montague 蒙太古
passages.original: Not Romeo, Prince, he was Mercutio’s friend; His fault concludes but what the law should end, The life of Tybalt.
passages.vernacular: 唔係羅密歐,親王,佢係茂丘西奧嘅朋友;佢嘅過錯只結束咗法律本該結束嘅,提伯特嘅生命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是羅密歐,親王,他是茂丘西奧的朋友;他的過錯只結束了法律本該結束的,提伯特的生命。

passages.title: Prince 親王
passages.original: And for that offence Immediately we do exile him hence.
passages.vernacular: 為了嗰個罪過,我哋即刻放逐佢離開呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了那個罪過,我們立刻放逐他離開這裡。

passages.original: I have an interest in your hate’s proceeding, My blood for your rude brawls doth lie a-bleeding.
passages.vernacular: 我同你哋嘅恨有利害關係,我嘅血因你哋粗野嘅鬥毆而流淌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我與你們的恨有利害關係,我的血因你們粗野的鬥毆而流淌。

passages.original: But I’ll amerce you with so strong a fine That you shall all repent the loss of mine.
passages.vernacular: 但我要罰你哋咁樣重嘅罰款,使你哋都為我嘅損失後悔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我要罰你們這樣重的罰款,使你們都為我的損失後悔。

passages.original: I will be deaf to pleading and excuses; Nor tears nor prayers shall purchase out abuses.
passages.vernacular: 我對懇求同藉口充耳不聞;眼淚同祈禱都唔能夠贖回罪過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對懇求和藉口充耳不聞;眼淚和祈禱都不能贖回罪過。

passages.original: Therefore use none.
passages.vernacular: 所以唔好用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以不要用。

passages.original: Let Romeo hence in haste, Else, when he is found, that hour is his last.
passages.vernacular: 讓羅密歐趕快離開,否則,一旦被發現,嗰一刻就係佢嘅末日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓羅密歐趕快離開,否則,一旦被發現,那一刻就是他的末日。

passages.original: Bear hence this body, and attend our will.
passages.vernacular: 把呢具屍體抬走,聽候我哋嘅旨意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把這具屍體抬走,聽候我們的旨意。

passages.original: Mercy but murders, pardoning those that kill.
passages.vernacular: 憐憫只係謀殺,若寬恕殺人者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憐憫只是謀殺,若寬恕殺人者。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene II — A Room in Capulet’s House 第三幕第二場:凱普雷特家一室

passages.original: Enter Juliet.
passages.vernacular: [茱麗葉上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茱麗葉上。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Gallop apace, you fiery-footed steeds, Towards Phoebus’ lodging.
passages.vernacular: 奔馳吧,你哋火足嘅駿馬,奔向福玻斯嘅住處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奔馳吧,你們火足的駿馬,奔向福玻斯的住處。

passages.original: Such a waggoner As Phaeton would whip you to the west And bring in cloudy night immediately.
passages.vernacular: 像法厄同嗰樣嘅車夫會鞭打你哋向西,即刻帶嚟多雲嘅夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像法厄同那樣的車夫會鞭打你們向西,立刻帶來多雲的夜晚。

passages.original: Spread thy close curtain, love-performing night, That runaway’s eyes may wink, and Romeo Leap to these arms, untalk’d of and unseen.
passages.vernacular: 張開你緊密嘅帷幕吧,成全愛情嘅夜,讓逃亡者嘅眼睛閉上,讓羅密歐跳進呢雙臂,無人談論,無人睇見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 張開你緊密的帷幕吧,成全愛情的夜,讓逃亡者的眼睛閉上,讓羅密歐跳進這雙臂,無人談論,無人看見。

passages.original: Lovers can see to do their amorous rites By their own beauties:
passages.vernacular: 戀人憑自己嘅美就能睇清,做佢哋愛嘅儀式:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戀人憑自己的美就能看清,做他們愛的儀式:

passages.original: or, if love be blind, It best agrees with night.
passages.vernacular: 或者,如果愛係盲嘅,佢跟夜晚最相配。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,如果愛是盲的,它跟夜晚最相配。

passages.original: Come, civil night, Thou sober-suited matron, all in black, And learn me how to lose a winning match, Play’d for a pair of stainless maidenhoods.
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧,文雅嘅夜,你呢身穿黑衣、莊重嘅主婦,教我點樣輸掉一場必勝嘅賽局,賭注係一對無瑕嘅童貞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧,文雅的夜,你這身穿黑衣、莊重的主婦,教我怎樣輸掉一場必勝的賽局,賭注是一對無瑕的童貞。

passages.original: Hood my unmann’d blood, bating in my cheeks, With thy black mantle, till strange love, grow bold, Think true love acted simple modesty.
passages.vernacular: 用你嘅黑斗篷蒙住我喺臉頰上撲騰嘅未馴之血,直到陌生嘅愛變得大膽,以為真愛嘅行動係純樸嘅羞澀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用你的黑斗篷蒙住我在臉頰上撲騰的未馴之血,直到陌生的愛變得大膽,以為真愛的行動是純樸的羞澀。

passages.original: Come, night, come Romeo; come, thou day in night;
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧,夜,嚟吧羅密歐;嚟吧,你呢夜中嘅白晝;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧,夜,來吧羅密歐;來吧,你這夜中的白晝;

passages.original: For thou wilt lie upon the wings of night Whiter than new snow upon a raven’s back.
passages.vernacular: 因為你將躺喺夜嘅翅膀上,比烏鴉背上嘅新雪仲白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你將躺在夜的翅膀上,比烏鴉背上的新雪還白。

passages.original: Come gentle night, come loving black-brow’d night, Give me my Romeo, and when I shall die, Take him and cut him out in little stars, And he will make the face of heaven so fine That all the world will be in love with night, And pay no worship to the garish sun.
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧溫柔嘅夜,嚟吧多情嘅黑眉嘅夜,把我嘅羅密歐畀我,當我死時,把佢取去,剪成小星星,佢會使天空嘅臉如此美麗,以致全世界都愛上夜晚,唔再崇拜嗰刺眼嘅太陽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧溫柔的夜,來吧多情的黑眉的夜,把我的羅密歐給我,當我死時,把他取去,剪成小星星,他會使天空的臉如此美麗,以致全世界都愛上夜晚,不再崇拜那刺眼的太陽。

passages.original: O, I have bought the mansion of a love, But not possess’d it;
passages.vernacular: 啊,我已買下愛嘅大廈,卻仲冇佔有;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我已買下愛的大廈,卻還沒佔有;

passages.original: and though I am sold, Not yet enjoy’d.
passages.vernacular: 我雖已被賣掉,卻仲冇被享用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我雖已被賣掉,卻還沒被享用。

passages.original: So tedious is this day As is the night before some festival To an impatient child that hath new robes And may not wear them.
passages.vernacular: 呢一天如此冗長,像節日前夜對一個耐不住嘅細路,佢有新衣裳卻唔能夠穿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一天如此冗長,像節日前夜對一個耐不住的孩子,他有新衣裳卻不能穿。

passages.original: O, here comes my Nurse, And she brings news, and every tongue that speaks But Romeo’s name speaks heavenly eloquence.
passages.vernacular: 啊,我嘅奶媽嚟喇,佢帶嚟消息,每一條講話嘅舌頭,只要講到羅密歐嘅名字,就講出天堂般嘅雄辯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我的奶媽來了,她帶來消息,每一條說話的舌頭,只要說到羅密歐的名字,就說出天堂般的雄辯。

passages.original: Enter Nurse, with cords.
passages.vernacular: [奶媽帶住繩子上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奶媽帶著繩子上。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Now, Nurse, what news?
passages.vernacular: 而家,奶媽,乜嘢消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,奶媽,什麼消息?

passages.original: What hast thou there?
passages.vernacular: 你嗰度攞嘅係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你那裡拿的是什麼?

passages.original: The cords that Romeo bid thee fetch?
passages.vernacular: 係羅密歐叫你去取嘅繩子嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是羅密歐叫你去取的繩子嗎?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Ay, ay, the cords.
passages.vernacular: 對,對,係繩子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,對,是繩子。

passages.original: [Throws them down.]
passages.vernacular: [把繩子扔喺地上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [把繩子扔在地上。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Ay me, what news?
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,乜嘢消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,什麼消息?

passages.original: Why dost thou wring thy hands?
passages.vernacular: 你點解絞著手?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼絞著手?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Ah, well-a-day, he’s dead, he’s dead, he’s dead!
passages.vernacular: 啊,不幸啊,佢死喇,佢死喇,佢死喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,不幸啊,他死了,他死了,他死了!

passages.original: We are undone, lady, we are undone.
passages.vernacular: 我哋完喇,小姐,我哋完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們完了,小姐,我們完了。

passages.original: Alack the day, he’s gone, he’s kill’d, he’s dead.
passages.vernacular: 唉,呢一天,佢走喇,佢被殺喇,佢死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,這一天,他走了,他被殺了,他死了。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Can heaven be so envious?
passages.vernacular: 天上能咁樣嫉妒嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天上能這樣嫉妒嗎?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Romeo can, Though heaven cannot.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐能,雖然天上唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐能,雖然天上不能。

passages.original: O Romeo, Romeo.
passages.vernacular: 啊羅密歐,羅密歐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊羅密歐,羅密歐。

passages.original: Who ever would have thought it? Romeo!
passages.vernacular: 邊個會想到呢?羅密歐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰會想到呢?羅密歐!

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: What devil art thou, that dost torment me thus?
passages.vernacular: 你係乜嘢魔鬼,咁樣折磨我?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是什麼魔鬼,這樣折磨我?

passages.original: This torture should be roar’d in dismal hell.
passages.vernacular: 呢種酷刑該喺陰沉嘅地獄裡咆哮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種酷刑該在陰沉的地獄裡咆哮。

passages.original: Hath Romeo slain himself?
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐自殺咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐自殺了嗎?

passages.original: Say thou but Ay, And that bare vowel I shall poison more Than the death-darting eye of cockatrice.
passages.vernacular: 只要你講一聲「係」,呢個光禿禿嘅字,我會比眼神致死嘅蛇怪更要毒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要你說一聲「是」,這個光禿禿的字,我會比眼神致死的蛇怪更要毒。

passages.original: I am not I if there be such an I; Or those eyes shut that make thee answer Ay.
passages.vernacular: 如果真有咁樣嘅「係」,我就唔係我喇;否則就讓嗰使你回答「係」嘅眼睛閉上吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果真有這樣的「是」,我就不是我了;否則就讓那使你回答「是」的眼睛閉上吧。

passages.original: If he be slain, say Ay; or if not, No.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢被殺,講「係」;如果冇,講「不」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他被殺,說「是」;如果沒有,說「不」。

passages.original: Brief sounds determine of my weal or woe.
passages.vernacular: 簡短嘅聲音決定我嘅福或禍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡短的聲音決定我的福或禍。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: I saw the wound, I saw it with mine eyes, God save the mark!—here on his manly breast.
passages.vernacular: 我睇見咗傷口,我親眼睇見嘅,願上帝保佑!——就喺佢男子氣概嘅胸膛上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看見了傷口,我親眼看見的,願上帝保佑!——就在他男子氣概的胸膛上。

passages.original: A piteous corse, a bloody piteous corse; Pale, pale as ashes, all bedaub’d in blood, All in gore-blood.
passages.vernacular: 一具可憐嘅屍體,一具血淋淋可憐嘅屍體;蒼白,蒼白如灰,全身糊滿咗血,全係凝血。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一具可憐的屍體,一具血淋淋可憐的屍體;蒼白,蒼白如灰,全身糊滿了血,全是凝血。

passages.original: I swounded at the sight.
passages.vernacular: 我一見就昏倒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一見就昏倒了。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O, break, my heart.
passages.vernacular: 啊,裂開吧,我嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,裂開吧,我的心。

passages.original: Poor bankrout, break at once.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅破產者,即刻裂開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的破產者,馬上裂開。

passages.original: To prison, eyes; ne’er look on liberty.
passages.vernacular: 眼睛,進監獄去;永遠唔好再睇自由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 眼睛,進監獄去;永遠別再看自由。

passages.original: Vile earth to earth resign; end motion here, And thou and Romeo press one heavy bier.
passages.vernacular: 卑賤嘅泥土歸於泥土;喺此停止運動,你同羅密歐同壓一副沉重嘅靈柩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 卑賤的泥土歸於泥土;在此停止運動,你和羅密歐同壓一副沉重的靈柩。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: O Tybalt, Tybalt, the best friend I had.
passages.vernacular: 啊提伯特,提伯特,我最好嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊提伯特,提伯特,我最好的朋友。

passages.original: O courteous Tybalt, honest gentleman!
passages.vernacular: 啊有禮嘅提伯特,誠實嘅紳士!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊有禮的提伯特,誠實的紳士!

passages.original: That ever I should live to see thee dead.
passages.vernacular: 我竟活住睇到你死去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我竟活著看到你死去。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: What storm is this that blows so contrary?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係乜嘢風暴,吹得咁樣逆向?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是什麼風暴,吹得這樣逆向?

passages.original: Is Romeo slaughter’d and is Tybalt dead?
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐被殺,提伯特都死喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐被殺,提伯特也死了?

passages.original: My dearest cousin, and my dearer lord?
passages.vernacular: 我最親愛嘅堂兄,同更親愛嘅丈夫?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我最親愛的堂兄,和更親愛的丈夫?

passages.original: Then dreadful trumpet sound the general doom, For who is living, if those two are gone?
passages.vernacular: 咁,可怕嘅號角啊,吹響末日審判吧,因為如果呢兩人都走喇,邊個仲活住?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,可怕的號角啊,吹響末日審判吧,因為如果這兩人都走了,誰還活著?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Tybalt is gone, and Romeo banished, Romeo that kill’d him, he is banished.
passages.vernacular: 提伯特走喇,羅密歐被放逐,殺佢嘅羅密歐,佢被放逐喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提伯特走了,羅密歐被放逐,殺他的羅密歐,他被放逐了。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O God!
passages.vernacular: 啊上帝!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊上帝!

passages.original: Did Romeo’s hand shed Tybalt’s blood?
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐嘅手流咗提伯特嘅血嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐的手流了提伯特的血嗎?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: It did, it did; alas the day, it did.
passages.vernacular: 係,係;唉,呢一天,係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,是;唉,這一天,是的。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O serpent heart, hid with a flowering face!
passages.vernacular: 啊,蛇一樣嘅心,藏喺開花嘅臉下!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,蛇一樣的心,藏在開花的臉下!

passages.original: Did ever dragon keep so fair a cave?
passages.vernacular: 邊條龍曾守住咁樣美嘅洞穴?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哪條龍曾守著這樣美的洞穴?

passages.original: Beautiful tyrant, fiend angelical, Dove-feather’d raven, wolvish-ravening lamb!
passages.vernacular: 美麗嘅暴君,天使般嘅魔鬼,鴿子羽毛嘅烏鴉,豺狼般貪婪嘅羔羊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美麗的暴君,天使般的魔鬼,鴿子羽毛的烏鴉,豺狼般貪婪的羔羊!

passages.original: Despised substance of divinest show!
passages.vernacular: 被鄙視嘅實質,卻有最神聖嘅外表!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被鄙視的實質,卻有最神聖的外表!

passages.original: Just opposite to what thou justly seem’st, A damned saint, an honourable villain!
passages.vernacular: 恰好同你理所當然顯得嘅相反,一個該詛咒嘅聖徒,一個光榮嘅惡棍!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 恰好與你理所當然顯得的相反,一個該詛咒的聖徒,一個光榮的惡棍!

passages.original: O nature, what hadst thou to do in hell When thou didst bower the spirit of a fiend In mortal paradise of such sweet flesh?
passages.vernacular: 啊自然,當你把魔鬼嘅靈魂安置喺咁樣甜美肉體嘅凡間天堂裡時,你到地獄去幹乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊自然,當你把魔鬼的靈魂安置在這樣甜美肉體的凡間天堂裡時,你到地獄去幹什麼?

passages.original: Was ever book containing such vile matter So fairly bound?
passages.vernacular: 邊本書曾含有咁樣卑劣嘅內容,卻裝訂得如此美麗?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哪本書曾含有這樣卑劣的內容,卻裝訂得如此美麗?

passages.original: O, that deceit should dwell In such a gorgeous palace.
passages.vernacular: 啊,欺騙竟住喺咁樣輝煌嘅宮殿裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,欺騙竟住在這樣輝煌的宮殿裡。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: There’s no trust, No faith, no honesty in men.
passages.vernacular: 男人中冇信任,冇信義,冇誠實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男人中沒有信任,沒有信義,沒有誠實。

passages.original: All perjur’d, All forsworn, all naught, all dissemblers.
passages.vernacular: 全係偽誓者,全係背誓者,全係壞蛋,全係偽君子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全是偽誓者,全是背誓者,全是壞蛋,全是偽君子。

passages.original: Ah, where’s my man?
passages.vernacular: 啊,我嘅僕人喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我的僕人在哪裡?

passages.original: Give me some aqua vitae.
passages.vernacular: 畀我啲烈酒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我一些烈酒。

passages.original: These griefs, these woes, these sorrows make me old.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲悲傷,呢啲災禍,呢啲憂愁使我老喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些悲傷,這些災禍,這些憂愁使我老了。

passages.original: Shame come to Romeo.
passages.vernacular: 願羞恥臨到羅密歐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願羞恥臨到羅密歐。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Blister’d be thy tongue For such a wish!
passages.vernacular: 願你嘅舌頭因咁樣嘅願望起水泡!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願你的舌頭因這樣的願望起水泡!

passages.original: He was not born to shame.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係生來受羞辱嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不是生來受羞辱的。

passages.original: Upon his brow shame is asham’d to sit; For ’tis a throne where honour may be crown’d Sole monarch of the universal earth.
passages.vernacular: 羞恥喺佢額頭上都羞於坐下;因為嗰個係一個寶座,榮譽可以喺上面被加冕為全世界唯一嘅君主。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羞恥在他額頭上也羞於坐下;因為那是一個寶座,榮譽可以在上面被加冕為全世界唯一的君主。

passages.original: O, what a beast was I to chide at him!
passages.vernacular: 啊,我責罵佢係幾咁蠢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我責罵他是多麼蠢!

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Will you speak well of him that kill’d your cousin?
passages.vernacular: 你要為殺咗你堂兄嘅人講好話嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要為殺了你堂兄的人說好話嗎?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Shall I speak ill of him that is my husband?
passages.vernacular: 我要講我丈夫嘅壞話嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要說我丈夫的壞話嗎?

passages.original: Ah, poor my lord, what tongue shall smooth thy name, When I thy three-hours’ wife have mangled it?
passages.vernacular: 啊,可憐嘅夫君,乜嘢舌頭能撫平你嘅名聲,當我呢個你三小時嘅妻子已把佢撕碎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,可憐的夫君,什麼舌頭能撫平你的名聲,當我這個你三小時的妻子已把它撕碎?

passages.original: But wherefore, villain, didst thou kill my cousin?
passages.vernacular: 不過,惡棍,你點解殺咗我堂兄?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是,惡棍,你為什麼殺了我堂兄?

passages.original: That villain cousin would have kill’d my husband.
passages.vernacular: 嗰惡棍堂兄本來要殺我丈夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那惡棍堂兄本來要殺我丈夫。

passages.original: Back, foolish tears, back to your native spring, Your tributary drops belong to woe, Which you mistaking offer up to joy.
passages.vernacular: 回去吧,傻眼淚,回到你哋嘅原泉去,你哋嘅進貢之滴屬於悲傷,你哋卻錯誤地獻畀歡喜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回去吧,傻眼淚,回到你們的原泉去,你們的進貢之滴屬於悲傷,你們卻錯誤地獻給歡喜。

passages.original: My husband lives, that Tybalt would have slain, And Tybalt’s dead, that would have slain my husband.
passages.vernacular: 我丈夫活住,提伯特本來要殺佢,提伯特死喇,佢本來要殺我丈夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我丈夫活著,提伯特本來要殺他,提伯特死了,他本來要殺我丈夫。

passages.original: All this is comfort; wherefore weep I then?
passages.vernacular: 呢一切都係安慰;嗰我點解哭?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一切都是安慰;那我為什麼哭?

passages.original: Some word there was, worser than Tybalt’s death, That murder’d me.
passages.vernacular: 有一個字,比提伯特嘅死更糟,謀殺咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一個字,比提伯特的死更糟,謀殺了我。

passages.original: I would forget it fain, But O, it presses to my memory Like damned guilty deeds to sinners’ minds.
passages.vernacular: 我好想忘記佢,不過啊,佢壓喺我嘅記憶上,像該詛咒嘅罪行壓喺罪人心上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很想忘記它,可是啊,它壓在我的記憶上,像該詛咒的罪行壓在罪人心上。

passages.original: Tybalt is dead, and Romeo banished.
passages.vernacular: 提伯特死喇,羅密歐被放逐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提伯特死了,羅密歐被放逐。

passages.original: That ‘banished,’ that one word ‘banished,’ Hath slain ten thousand Tybalts.
passages.vernacular: 嗰「放逐」,嗰一個詞「放逐」,殺死咗一萬個提伯特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那「放逐」,那一個詞「放逐」,殺死了一萬個提伯特。

passages.original: Tybalt’s death Was woe enough, if it had ended there.
passages.vernacular: 提伯特嘅死已夠悲傷,如果到此為止嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提伯特的死已夠悲傷,如果到此為止的話。

passages.original: Or if sour woe delights in fellowship, And needly will be rank’d with other griefs, Why follow’d not, when she said Tybalt’s dead, Thy father or thy mother, nay or both, Which modern lamentation might have mov’d?
passages.vernacular: 或者,如果酸楚嘅悲傷鍾意有伴,必須同其他悲痛排喺一起,點解佢講提伯特死咗嘅時候,不接住講你嘅父親或母親,不,或兩者都死,嗰本可引起平常嘅哀悼?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,如果酸楚的悲傷喜歡有伴,必須與其他悲痛排在一起,為什麼她說提伯特死了的時候,不接著說你的父親或母親,不,或兩者都死,那本可引起平常的哀悼?

passages.original: But with a rear-ward following Tybalt’s death, ‘Romeo is banished’—to speak that word Is father, mother, Tybalt, Romeo, Juliet, All slain, all dead.
passages.vernacular: 但喺提伯特死之後緊跟殿後嘅一句「羅密歐被放逐」——講出呢個詞,就係父親、母親、提伯特、羅密歐、茱麗葉,全被殺,全死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在提伯特死之後緊跟殿後的一句「羅密歐被放逐」——說出這個詞,就是父親、母親、提伯特、羅密歐、茱麗葉,全被殺,全死了。

passages.original: Romeo is banished, There is no end, no limit, measure, bound, In that word’s death, no words can that woe sound.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐被放逐,喺嗰個詞嘅死亡中冇終點,冇界限、尺度、邊際,冇言語能測出嗰悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐被放逐,在那個詞的死亡中沒有終點,沒有界限、尺度、邊際,沒有言語能測出那悲傷。

passages.original: Where is my father and my mother, Nurse?
passages.vernacular: 我父親同母親喺邊度,奶媽?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我父親和母親在哪裡,奶媽?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Weeping and wailing over Tybalt’s corse.
passages.vernacular: 喺提伯特嘅屍體旁哭泣悲號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在提伯特的屍體旁哭泣悲號。

passages.original: Will you go to them?
passages.vernacular: 你要去佢哋嗰度嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要去他們那裡嗎?

passages.original: I will bring you thither.
passages.vernacular: 我帶你去嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我帶你去那裡。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Wash they his wounds with tears.
passages.vernacular: 讓佢哋用眼淚洗佢嘅傷口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓他們用眼淚洗他的傷口。

passages.original: Mine shall be spent, When theirs are dry, for Romeo’s banishment.
passages.vernacular: 等佢哋嘅淚乾喇,我嘅將為羅密歐嘅放逐而流。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等他們的淚乾了,我的將為羅密歐的放逐而流。

passages.original: Take up those cords.
passages.vernacular: 把嗰啲繩子攞起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把那些繩子拿起來。

passages.original: Poor ropes, you are beguil’d, Both you and I; for Romeo is exil’d.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅繩索,你哋被騙喇,你同我;因為羅密歐被流放。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的繩索,你們被騙了,你和我;因為羅密歐被流放。

passages.original: He made you for a highway to my bed, But I, a maid, die maiden-widowed.
passages.vernacular: 佢把你做成通往我床嘅大道,不過我,一個少女,死時卻係處女寡婦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把你做成通往我床的大道,可是我,一個少女,死時卻是處女寡婦。

passages.original: Come cords, come Nurse, I’ll to my wedding bed, And death, not Romeo, take my maidenhead.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,繩子,嚟,奶媽,我要去我嘅婚床,讓死亡,而唔係羅密歐,奪去我嘅童貞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,繩子,來,奶媽,我要去我的婚床,讓死亡,而不是羅密歐,奪去我的童貞。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Hie to your chamber.
passages.vernacular: 趕緊回你嘅房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 趕緊回你的房間。

passages.original: I’ll find Romeo To comfort you.
passages.vernacular: 我去找羅密歐嚟安慰你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去找羅密歐來安慰你。

passages.original: I wot well where he is.
passages.vernacular: 我好清楚佢喺邊度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很清楚他在哪裡。

passages.original: Hark ye, your Romeo will be here at night.
passages.vernacular: 聽住,你嘅羅密歐今晚會嚟呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽著,你的羅密歐今晚會來這裡。

passages.original: I’ll to him, he is hid at Lawrence’ cell.
passages.vernacular: 我去找佢,佢藏喺勞倫斯嘅修室。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去找他,他藏在勞倫斯的修室。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O find him, give this ring to my true knight, And bid him come to take his last farewell.
passages.vernacular: 啊,找到佢,把呢枚戒指畀我真心嘅騎士,叫佢嚟作最後嘅告別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,找到他,把這枚戒指給我真心的騎士,叫他來作最後的告別。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene III — Friar Lawrence’s Cell 第三幕第三場:勞倫斯神父的修室

passages.original: Enter Friar Lawrence.
passages.vernacular: [勞倫斯神父上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [勞倫斯神父上。]

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Romeo, come forth; come forth, thou fearful man.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐,出嚟;出嚟,你呢膽小嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐,出來;出來,你這膽小的人。

passages.original: Affliction is enanmour’d of thy parts And thou art wedded to calamity.
passages.vernacular: 苦難愛上咗你嘅品質,你同災禍結咗婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 苦難愛上了你的品質,你和災禍結了婚。

passages.original: Enter Romeo.
passages.vernacular: [羅密歐上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅密歐上。]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Father, what news?
passages.vernacular: 神父,有乜嘢消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 神父,有什麼消息?

passages.original: What is the Prince’s doom?
passages.vernacular: 親王嘅判決係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親王的判決是什麼?

passages.original: What sorrow craves acquaintance at my hand, That I yet know not?
passages.vernacular: 仲有乜嘢悲傷要同我結識,係我仲唔知道嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有什麼悲傷要與我結識,是我還不知道的?

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Too familiar Is my dear son with such sour company.
passages.vernacular: 我親愛嘅細路同咁樣酸楚嘅伴侶太熟悉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我親愛的孩子與這樣酸楚的伴侶太熟悉了。

passages.original: I bring thee tidings of the Prince’s doom.
passages.vernacular: 我畀你帶嚟親王判決嘅消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給你帶來親王判決的消息。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: What less than doomsday is the Prince’s doom?
passages.vernacular: 親王嘅判決,除咗末日審判仲有乜嘢更輕嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親王的判決,除了末日審判還有什麼更輕的?

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: A gentler judgment vanish’d from his lips, Not body’s death, but body’s banishment.
passages.vernacular: 更溫和嘅判決從佢唇邊溜出:唔係身體嘅死,而係身體嘅放逐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 更溫和的判決從他唇邊溜出:不是身體的死,而是身體的放逐。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Ha, banishment?
passages.vernacular: 哈,放逐?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈,放逐?

passages.original: Be merciful, say death; For exile hath more terror in his look, Much more than death.
passages.vernacular: 發發慈悲,講死吧;因為流放睇上去比死更可怕得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 發發慈悲,說死吧;因為流放看上去比死更可怕得多。

passages.original: Do not say banishment.
passages.vernacular: 唔好講放逐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要說放逐。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Hence from Verona art thou banished.
passages.vernacular: 你被逐出維洛嗰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你被逐出維洛那。

passages.original: Be patient, for the world is broad and wide.
passages.vernacular: 要耐心,因為世界又寬又廣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要耐心,因為世界又寬又廣。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: There is no world without Verona walls, But purgatory, torture, hell itself.
passages.vernacular: 維洛嗰城牆之外冇世界,只有煉獄、酷刑、地獄本身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 維洛那城牆之外沒有世界,只有煉獄、酷刑、地獄本身。

passages.original: Hence banished is banish’d from the world, And world’s exile is death.
passages.vernacular: 從呢度被放逐,就係被逐出世界,而世界嘅流放就係死亡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從這裡被放逐,就是被逐出世界,而世界的流放就是死亡。

passages.original: Then banished Is death misterm’d.
passages.vernacular: 咁,「放逐」不過係死亡被叫錯咗名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,「放逐」不過是死亡被叫錯了名字。

passages.original: Calling death banished, Thou cutt’st my head off with a golden axe, And smilest upon the stroke that murders me.
passages.vernacular: 你把死亡叫作放逐,係用金斧砍我嘅頭,仲對謀殺我嘅一擊微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把死亡叫作放逐,是用金斧砍我的頭,還對謀殺我的一擊微笑。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: O deadly sin, O rude unthankfulness!
passages.vernacular: 啊,致命嘅罪,啊,粗魯嘅忘恩負義!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,致命的罪,啊,粗魯的忘恩負義!

passages.original: Thy fault our law calls death, but the kind Prince, Taking thy part, hath brush’d aside the law, And turn’d that black word death to banishment.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅過錯,我哋嘅法律判為死刑,但仁慈嘅親王站喺你呢邊,撥開咗法律,把嗰黑暗嘅「死」字改成咗放逐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的過錯,我們的法律判為死刑,但仁慈的親王站在你這邊,撥開了法律,把那黑暗的「死」字改成了放逐。

passages.original: This is dear mercy, and thou see’st it not.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係寶貴嘅慈悲,你卻睇唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是寶貴的慈悲,你卻看不到。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: ’Tis torture, and not mercy.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係酷刑,唔係慈悲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是酷刑,不是慈悲。

passages.original: Heaven is here Where Juliet lives, and every cat and dog, And little mouse, every unworthy thing, Live here in heaven and may look on her, But Romeo may not.
passages.vernacular: 天堂就喺茱麗葉活住嘅地方,每一隻貓同狗,每一隻小老鼠,每一樣不配嘅嘢,都喺呢度天堂中生活,可以睇佢,而羅密歐卻不可以。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天堂就在茱麗葉活著的地方,每一隻貓和狗,每一隻小老鼠,每一樣不配的東西,都在這裡天堂中生活,可以看她,而羅密歐卻不可以。

passages.original: More validity, More honourable state, more courtship lives In carrion flies than Romeo.
passages.vernacular: 腐肉上嘅蒼蠅,比羅密歐擁有更多嘅特權、更榮耀嘅地位、更多嘅求愛機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 腐肉上的蒼蠅,比羅密歐擁有更多的特權、更榮耀的地位、更多的求愛機會。

passages.original: They may seize On the white wonder of dear Juliet’s hand, And steal immortal blessing from her lips, Who, even in pure and vestal modesty Still blush, as thinking their own kisses sin.
passages.vernacular: 牠哋可以抓住親愛嘅茱麗葉嗰手嘅白色奇蹟,從佢嘅嘴唇偷取永恆嘅祝福,佢嘅嘴唇即使喺純潔貞女般嘅羞澀中,仍會臉紅,以為自己嘅相吻係罪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牠們可以抓住親愛的茱麗葉那手的白色奇蹟,從她的嘴唇偷取永恆的祝福,她的嘴唇即使在純潔貞女般的羞澀中,仍會臉紅,以為自己的相吻是罪。

passages.original: But Romeo may not, he is banished.
passages.vernacular: 但羅密歐不可以,佢被放逐喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但羅密歐不可以,他被放逐了。

passages.original: This may flies do, when I from this must fly.
passages.vernacular: 蒼蠅可以咁樣做,而我得從呢度逃走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒼蠅可以這樣做,而我得從這裡逃走。

passages.original: They are free men but I am banished.
passages.vernacular: 牠哋係自由人,而我被放逐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牠們是自由人,而我被放逐。
