passages.original: And say’st thou yet that exile is not death?
passages.vernacular: 你仲講流放唔係死嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你還說流放不是死嗎?

passages.original: Hadst thou no poison mix’d, no sharp-ground knife, No sudden mean of death, though ne’er so mean, But banished to kill me? Banished?
passages.vernacular: 難道你冇調好嘅毒藥,冇磨利嘅刀,冇突然嘅致死之法,邊怕再卑賤,卻只用放逐嚟殺我?放逐?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難道你沒有調好的毒藥,沒有磨利的刀,沒有突然的致死之法,哪怕再卑賤,卻只用放逐來殺我?放逐?

passages.original: O Friar, the damned use that word in hell.
passages.vernacular: 啊神父,下地獄嘅人才喺地獄裡用嗰個詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊神父,下地獄的人才在地獄裡用那個詞。

passages.original: Howling attends it.
passages.vernacular: 伴隨佢嘅係嚎叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伴隨它的是嚎叫。

passages.original: How hast thou the heart, Being a divine, a ghostly confessor, A sin-absolver, and my friend profess’d, To mangle me with that word banished?
passages.vernacular: 你身為神職人員,係神聖嘅懺悔師,赦罪者,又自稱係我嘅朋友,點忍心用「放逐」呢個詞嚟撕碎我?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你身為神職人員,是神聖的懺悔師,赦罪者,又自稱是我的朋友,怎麼忍心用「放逐」這個詞來撕碎我?

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Thou fond mad man, hear me speak a little,
passages.vernacular: 你呢愚昧瘋狂嘅人,聽我講幾句,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這愚昧瘋狂的人,聽我說幾句,

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: O, thou wilt speak again of banishment.
passages.vernacular: 啊,你又要講放逐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,你又要說放逐。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: I’ll give thee armour to keep off that word, Adversity’s sweet milk, philosophy, To comfort thee, though thou art banished.
passages.vernacular: 我畀你一副盔甲嚟抵擋嗰個詞,逆境嘅甜奶——哲學,安慰你,雖然你被放逐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給你一副盔甲來抵擋那個詞,逆境的甜奶——哲學,安慰你,雖然你被放逐。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Yet banished?
passages.vernacular: 定係放逐?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還是放逐?

passages.original: Hang up philosophy.
passages.vernacular: 把哲學掛起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把哲學掛起來。

passages.original: Unless philosophy can make a Juliet, Displant a town, reverse a Prince’s doom, It helps not, it prevails not, talk no more.
passages.vernacular: 除非哲學能造出一個茱麗葉,移走一座城,推翻親王嘅判決,否則冇用,冇效力,唔好再講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除非哲學能造出一個茱麗葉,移走一座城,推翻親王的判決,否則沒用,沒效力,別再說了。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: O, then I see that mad men have no ears.
passages.vernacular: 啊,咁我睇出瘋子冇耳朵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,那麼我看出瘋子沒有耳朵。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: How should they, when that wise men have no eyes?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋點會有,既然智者冇眼睛?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們怎麼會有,既然智者沒有眼睛?

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Let me dispute with thee of thy estate.
passages.vernacular: 讓我跟你討論你嘅處境。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我跟你討論你的處境。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Thou canst not speak of that thou dost not feel.
passages.vernacular: 你唔能夠談你冇感受過嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不能談你沒感受過的事。

passages.original: Wert thou as young as I, Juliet thy love, An hour but married, Tybalt murdered, Doting like me, and like me banished, Then mightst thou speak, then mightst thou tear thy hair, And fall upon the ground as I do now, Taking the measure of an unmade grave.
passages.vernacular: 如果你像我一樣年輕,茱麗葉係你嘅愛人,剛結婚一小時,提伯特被殺,像我一樣癡戀,像我一樣被放逐,嗰時你才可以講,嗰時你才可以扯頭髮,像我而家咁樣倒喺地上,量一座仲冇挖好嘅墳墓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你像我一樣年輕,茱麗葉是你的愛人,剛結婚一小時,提伯特被殺,像我一樣癡戀,像我一樣被放逐,那時你才可以說,那時你才可以扯頭髮,像我現在這樣倒在地上,量一座還沒挖好的墳墓。

passages.original: [Knocking within.]
passages.vernacular: [內有敲門聲。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內有敲門聲。]

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Arise; one knocks.
passages.vernacular: 起嚟;有人敲門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起來;有人敲門。

passages.original: Good Romeo, hide thyself.
passages.vernacular: 好羅密歐,藏起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好羅密歐,藏起來。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Not I, unless the breath of heartsick groans Mist-like infold me from the search of eyes.
passages.vernacular: 我不,除非心痛嘅呻吟像霧一樣把我包起嚟,不讓人嘅眼睛搜尋到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不,除非心痛的呻吟像霧一樣把我包起來,不讓人的眼睛搜尋到。

passages.original: [Knocking.]
passages.vernacular: [敲門。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [敲門。]

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Hark, how they knock!—Who’s there?—Romeo, arise, Thou wilt be taken.—Stay awhile.—Stand up.
passages.vernacular: 聽,佢哋點敲!——邊個喺嗰度?——羅密歐,起嚟,你會被捕嘅。——等一等。——站起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽,他們怎麼敲!——誰在那裡?——羅密歐,起來,你會被捕的。——等一等。——站起來。

passages.original: [Knocking.]
passages.vernacular: [敲門。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [敲門。]

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Run to my study.—By-and-by.—God’s will, What simpleness is this.—I come, I come.
passages.vernacular: 跑到我嘅書房去。——即刻。——天呀,呢個係幾咁愚蠢。——我嚟喇,我嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跑到我的書房去。——馬上。——天哪,這是多麼愚蠢。——我來了,我來了。

passages.original: [Knocking.]
passages.vernacular: [敲門。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [敲門。]

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Who knocks so hard?
passages.vernacular: 邊個敲得咁重?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰敲得這麼重?

passages.original: Whence come you, what’s your will?
passages.vernacular: 你從邊度嚟,有乜嘢事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你從哪裡來,有什麼事?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: [Within.]
passages.vernacular: [在內。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [在內。]

passages.original: Let me come in, and you shall know my errand.
passages.vernacular: 讓我進去,你就會知道我嘅嚟意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我進去,你就會知道我的來意。

passages.original: I come from Lady Juliet.
passages.vernacular: 我從茱麗葉小姐嗰度嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從茱麗葉小姐那裡來。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Welcome then.
passages.vernacular: 咁歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼歡迎。

passages.original: Enter Nurse.
passages.vernacular: [奶媽上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奶媽上。]

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: O holy Friar, O, tell me, holy Friar, Where is my lady’s lord, where’s Romeo?
passages.vernacular: 啊聖潔嘅神父,啊,告訴我,聖潔嘅神父,我小姐嘅丈夫喺邊度,羅密歐喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊聖潔的神父,啊,告訴我,聖潔的神父,我小姐的丈夫在哪裡,羅密歐在哪裡?

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: There on the ground, with his own tears made drunk.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰邊地上,被佢自己嘅眼淚灌醉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那邊地上,被他自己的眼淚灌醉了。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: O, he is even in my mistress’ case.
passages.vernacular: 啊,佢同我主人處境一模一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,他和我主人處境一模一樣。

passages.original: Just in her case!
passages.vernacular: 一模一樣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一模一樣!

passages.original: O woeful sympathy!
passages.vernacular: 啊悲哀嘅同感!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊悲哀的同感!

passages.original: Piteous predicament.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅困境。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的困境。

passages.original: Even so lies she, Blubbering and weeping, weeping and blubbering.
passages.vernacular: 佢都係咁樣躺住,抽泣哭泣,哭泣抽泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她也是這樣躺著,抽泣哭泣,哭泣抽泣。

passages.original: Stand up, stand up; stand, and you be a man.
passages.vernacular: 站起嚟,站起嚟;站起嚟,如果你係個男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 站起來,站起來;站起來,如果你是個男人。

passages.original: For Juliet’s sake, for her sake, rise and stand.
passages.vernacular: 為了茱麗葉,為了佢,起嚟站住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了茱麗葉,為了她,起來站著。

passages.original: Why should you fall into so deep an O?
passages.vernacular: 你點解跌入咁深嘅一個「啊」?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼跌入這麼深的一個「啊」?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Nurse.
passages.vernacular: 奶媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奶媽。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Ah sir, ah sir, death’s the end of all.
passages.vernacular: 啊先生,啊先生,死亡係一切嘅終結。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊先生,啊先生,死亡是一切的終結。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Spakest thou of Juliet?
passages.vernacular: 你講到茱麗葉嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說到茱麗葉嗎?

passages.original: How is it with her?
passages.vernacular: 佢點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她怎麼樣?

passages.original: Doth not she think me an old murderer, Now I have stain’d the childhood of our joy With blood remov’d but little from her own?
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係把我當作老謀殺犯嗎,而家我用離佢自己嘅血相去無幾嘅血,玷污咗我哋歡樂嘅童年?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不是把我當作老謀殺犯嗎,現在我用離她自己的血相去無幾的血,玷污了我們歡樂的童年?

passages.original: Where is she?
passages.vernacular: 佢喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在哪裡?

passages.original: And how doth she?
passages.vernacular: 佢點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她怎麼樣?

passages.original: And what says My conceal’d lady to our cancell’d love?
passages.vernacular: 我嗰隱秘嘅夫人,對我哋被取消嘅愛講乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我那隱秘的夫人,對我們被取消的愛說什麼?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: O, she says nothing, sir, but weeps and weeps;
passages.vernacular: 啊,佢乜嘢都冇講,先生,只係哭啊哭;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,她什麼也沒說,先生,只是哭啊哭;

passages.original: And now falls on her bed, and then starts up, And Tybalt calls, and then on Romeo cries, And then down falls again.
passages.vernacular: 一會兒倒喺床上,一會兒跳起嚟,叫住提伯特,然後又喊羅密歐,然後又倒下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一會兒倒在床上,一會兒跳起來,叫著提伯特,然後又喊羅密歐,然後又倒下。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: As if that name, Shot from the deadly level of a gun, Did murder her, as that name’s cursed hand Murder’d her kinsman.
passages.vernacular: 彷彿嗰個名字,從致命槍口射出,謀殺咗佢,就像嗰名字嘅該詛咒嘅手謀殺咗佢嘅親戚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彷彿那個名字,從致命槍口射出,謀殺了她,就像那名字的該詛咒的手謀殺了她的親戚。

passages.original: O, tell me, Friar, tell me, In what vile part of this anatomy Doth my name lodge?
passages.vernacular: 啊,告訴我,神父,告訴我,喺呢副軀體嘅邊個卑劣部位,住我嘅名字?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,告訴我,神父,告訴我,在這副軀體的哪個卑劣部位,住著我的名字?

passages.original: Tell me, that I may sack The hateful mansion.
passages.vernacular: 告訴我,好讓我洗劫嗰可恨嘅住所。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴我,好讓我洗劫那可恨的住所。

passages.original: [Drawing his sword.]
passages.vernacular: [拔劍。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [拔劍。]

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Hold thy desperate hand.
passages.vernacular: 住手你嗰絕望嘅手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 住手你那絕望的手。

passages.original: Art thou a man?
passages.vernacular: 你係個男人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是個男人嗎?

passages.original: Thy form cries out thou art.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅外形喊住你係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的外形喊著你是。

passages.original: Thy tears are womanish, thy wild acts denote The unreasonable fury of a beast.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅眼淚像女人,你嘅狂亂舉動表明野獸不講理嘅狂怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的眼淚像女人,你的狂亂舉動表明野獸不講理的狂怒。

passages.original: Unseemly woman in a seeming man, And ill-beseeming beast in seeming both!
passages.vernacular: 睇似男人嘅唔得體嘅女人,又係兩者皆似嘅不相稱嘅野獸!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看似男人的不得體的女人,又是兩者皆似的不相稱的野獸!

passages.original: Thou hast amaz’d me.
passages.vernacular: 你使我食驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你使我吃驚。

passages.original: By my holy order, I thought thy disposition better temper’d.
passages.vernacular: 憑我神聖嘅修會起誓,我原以為你嘅性情調和得更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑我神聖的修會起誓,我原以為你的性情調和得更好。

passages.original: Hast thou slain Tybalt?
passages.vernacular: 你殺咗提伯特?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你殺了提伯特?

passages.original: Wilt thou slay thyself?
passages.vernacular: 你仲要殺你自己?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你還要殺你自己?

passages.original: And slay thy lady, that in thy life lives, By doing damned hate upon thyself?
passages.vernacular: 仲要殺你嘅夫人,佢活喺你嘅生命裡,你對自己行呢該詛咒嘅仇恨?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還要殺你的夫人,她活在你的生命裡,你對自己行這該詛咒的仇恨?

passages.original: Why rail’st thou on thy birth, the heaven and earth?
passages.vernacular: 你點解咒罵你嘅出生、天同地?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼咒罵你的出生、天和地?

passages.original: Since birth, and heaven and earth, all three do meet In thee at once;
passages.vernacular: 既然出生、天、地三者同時喺你身上相遇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然出生、天、地三者同時在你身上相遇;

passages.original: which thou at once wouldst lose.
passages.vernacular: 你卻想一下子全部失去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你卻想一下子全部失去。

passages.original: Fie, fie, thou sham’st thy shape, thy love, thy wit, Which, like a usurer, abound’st in all, And usest none in that true use indeed Which should bedeck thy shape, thy love, thy wit.
passages.vernacular: 呸,呸,你羞辱咗你嘅外形、你嘅愛、你嘅智慧,你像高利貸者一樣乜嘢都豐富,卻不把佢哋用喺嗰本該裝飾你嘅外形、愛同智慧嘅真正用途上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呸,呸,你羞辱了你的外形、你的愛、你的智慧,你像高利貸者一樣什麼都豐富,卻不把它們用在那本該裝飾你的外形、愛和智慧的真正用途上。

passages.original: Thy noble shape is but a form of wax, Digressing from the valour of a man;
passages.vernacular: 你高貴嘅外形只係蠟做嘅形狀,離開咗男子嘅勇氣;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你高貴的外形只是蠟做的形狀,離開了男子的勇氣;

passages.original: Thy dear love sworn but hollow perjury, Killing that love which thou hast vow’d to cherish;
passages.vernacular: 你親愛嘅愛情所發嘅誓成咗空洞嘅偽誓,殺死你曾發誓珍愛嘅愛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你親愛的愛情所發的誓成了空洞的偽誓,殺死你曾發誓珍愛的愛;

passages.original: Thy wit, that ornament to shape and love, Misshapen in the conduct of them both, Like powder in a skilless soldier’s flask, Is set afire by thine own ignorance, And thou dismember’d with thine own defence.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅智慧,嗰對外形同愛嘅裝飾,喺呢兩者嘅運用上都走咗樣,像笨拙士兵火藥瓶中嘅火藥,被你自己嘅無知點燃,你被自己嘅防衛炸得四分五裂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的智慧,那對外形與愛的裝飾,在這兩者的運用上都走了樣,像笨拙士兵火藥瓶中的火藥,被你自己的無知點燃,你被自己的防衛炸得四分五裂。

passages.original: What, rouse thee, man.
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,振作起嚟,老兄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,振作起來,老兄。

passages.original: Thy Juliet is alive, For whose dear sake thou wast but lately dead.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅茱麗葉活住,為了佢,你不久前仲想死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的茱麗葉活著,為了她,你不久前還想死。

passages.original: There art thou happy.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢啲上你係幸運嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這一點上你是幸運的。

passages.original: Tybalt would kill thee, But thou slew’st Tybalt; there art thou happy.
passages.vernacular: 提伯特要殺你,但你殺咗提伯特;喺呢啲上你係幸運嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提伯特要殺你,但你殺了提伯特;在這一點上你是幸運的。

passages.original: The law that threaten’d death becomes thy friend, And turns it to exile; there art thou happy.
passages.vernacular: 威脅死亡嘅法律成咗你嘅朋友,把佢改成流放;喺呢啲上你係幸運嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威脅死亡的法律成了你的朋友,把它改成流放;在這一點上你是幸運的。

passages.original: A pack of blessings light upon thy back; Happiness courts thee in her best array;
passages.vernacular: 一大堆福氣落喺你背上;幸福以佢最好嘅盛裝向你求愛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一大堆福氣落在你背上;幸福以她最好的盛裝向你求愛;

passages.original: But like a misshaped and sullen wench, Thou putt’st up thy Fortune and thy love.
passages.vernacular: 不過你像個不成形嘅、悶悶不樂嘅丫頭,噘住嘴拒絕你嘅運氣同你嘅愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是你像個不成形的、悶悶不樂的丫頭,噘著嘴拒絕你的運氣和你的愛。

passages.original: Take heed, take heed, for such die miserable.
passages.vernacular: 當心,當心,因為咁樣嘅人死得好悲慘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當心,當心,因為這樣的人死得很悲慘。

passages.original: Go, get thee to thy love as was decreed, Ascend her chamber, hence and comfort her.
passages.vernacular: 去,按約定去見你嘅愛人,爬上佢嘅房間,從嗰度去安慰佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,按約定去見你的愛人,爬上她的房間,從那裡去安慰她。

passages.original: But look thou stay not till the watch be set, For then thou canst not pass to Mantua;
passages.vernacular: 但要留心,別待到守夜人站崗,因為嗰時你就過不去曼圖亞喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但要留心,別待到守夜人站崗,因為那時你就過不去曼圖亞了;

passages.original: Where thou shalt live till we can find a time To blaze your marriage, reconcile your friends, Beg pardon of the Prince, and call thee back With twenty hundred thousand times more joy Than thou went’st forth in lamentation.
passages.vernacular: 你將喺嗰度住下,直到我哋找到時機公布你哋嘅婚姻,使你哋嘅朋友和解,向親王請求赦免,並把你召回,帶住比你離開時悲歎多二百萬倍嘅歡喜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你將在那裡住下,直到我們找到時機公布你們的婚姻,使你們的朋友和解,向親王請求赦免,並把你召回,帶著比你離開時悲歎多二百萬倍的歡喜。

passages.original: Go before, Nurse.
passages.vernacular: 奶媽,你先走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奶媽,你先走。

passages.original: Commend me to thy lady, And bid her hasten all the house to bed, Which heavy sorrow makes them apt unto.
passages.vernacular: 替我向你嘅小姐問好,叫佢催全家人早瞓,沉重嘅悲傷使佢哋容易入瞓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 替我向你的小姐問好,叫她催全家人早睡,沉重的悲傷使他們容易入睡。

passages.original: Romeo is coming.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐就嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐就來。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: O Lord, I could have stay’d here all the night To hear good counsel.
passages.vernacular: 啊天呀,我本可以喺呢度待一整夜,聽咁樣好嘅勸告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊天哪,我本可以在這裡待一整夜,聽這樣好的勸告。

passages.original: O, what learning is!
passages.vernacular: 啊,學問係幾咁好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,學問是多麼好!

passages.original: My lord, I’ll tell my lady you will come.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我去告訴小姐您會嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我去告訴小姐您會來。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Do so, and bid my sweet prepare to chide.
passages.vernacular: 去吧,告訴我嘅甜心準備責罵我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去吧,告訴我的甜心準備責罵我。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Here sir, a ring she bid me give you, sir.
passages.vernacular: 先生,呢度有一枚戒指,佢叫我交畀你,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,這裡有一枚戒指,她叫我交給你,先生。

passages.original: Hie you, make haste, for it grows very late.
passages.vernacular: 快去,趕緊,因為夜好深喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快去,趕緊,因為夜很深了。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: How well my comfort is reviv’d by this.
passages.vernacular: 呢真使我嘅安慰幾咁好地恢復。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這真使我的安慰多麼好地恢復。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Go hence, good night, and here stands all your state:
passages.vernacular: 離開呢度,晚安,你嘅全部命運就喺呢度:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 離開這裡,晚安,你的全部命運就在這裡:

passages.original: Either be gone before the watch be set, Or by the break of day disguis’d from hence.
passages.vernacular: 要麼喺守夜人站崗前走掉,要麼喺黎明時分喬裝離開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要麼在守夜人站崗前走掉,要麼在黎明時分喬裝離開。

passages.original: Sojourn in Mantua.
passages.vernacular: 去曼圖亞住下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去曼圖亞住下。

passages.original: I’ll find out your man, And he shall signify from time to time Every good hap to you that chances here.
passages.vernacular: 我會找到你嘅僕人,佢會不時告訴你呢度發生嘅每一件好事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會找到你的僕人,他會不時告訴你這裡發生的每一件好事。

passages.original: Give me thy hand; ’tis late; farewell; good night.
passages.vernacular: 把你嘅手畀我;天晚喇;再會;晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把你的手給我;天晚了;再會;晚安。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: But that a joy past joy calls out on me, It were a grief so brief to part with thee. Farewell.
passages.vernacular: 要唔係有一種超越歡喜嘅歡喜召喚我,同你咁樣匆匆分別真係痛苦。再會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要不是有一種超越歡喜的歡喜召喚我,與你這樣匆匆分別真是痛苦。再會。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene IV — A Room in Capulet’s House 第三幕第四場:凱普雷特家一室

passages.original: Enter Capulet, Lady Capulet and Paris.
passages.vernacular: [凱普雷特、凱普雷特夫人同帕里斯上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱普雷特、凱普雷特夫人與帕里斯上。]

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Things have fallen out, sir, so unluckily That we have had no time to move our daughter.
passages.vernacular: 事情發生得咁樣不幸,先生,我哋冇時間去勸講我哋嘅女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事情發生得這樣不幸,先生,我們沒時間去勸說我們的女兒。

passages.original: Look you, she lov’d her kinsman Tybalt dearly, And so did I.
passages.vernacular: 您瞧,佢好愛佢嘅堂兄提伯特,我都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您瞧,她很愛她的堂兄提伯特,我也是。

passages.original: Well, we were born to die.
passages.vernacular: 好,我哋生來就係要死嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,我們生來就是要死的。

passages.original: ’Tis very late; she’ll not come down tonight.
passages.vernacular: 夜好深喇;佢今晚唔會下嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夜很深了;她今晚不會下來了。

passages.original: I promise you, but for your company, I would have been abed an hour ago.
passages.vernacular: 我向您保證,若唔係為了陪您,我一小時前就已上床喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向您保證,若不是為了陪您,我一小時前就已上床了。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: These times of woe afford no tune to woo.
passages.vernacular: 呢悲哀嘅時候冇求愛嘅心情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這悲哀的時候沒有求愛的心情。

passages.original: Madam, good night.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,晚安。

passages.original: Commend me to your daughter.
passages.vernacular: 替我向令嬡問候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 替我向令嬡問候。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: I will, and know her mind early tomorrow; Tonight she’s mew’d up to her heaviness.
passages.vernacular: 我會嘅,聽日一早就探知佢嘅心意;今晚佢被關喺佢嘅憂傷裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會的,明天一早就探知她的心意;今晚她被關在她的憂傷裡。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Sir Paris, I will make a desperate tender Of my child’s love.
passages.vernacular: 帕里斯大人,我要冒昧地提出我細路嘅愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帕里斯大人,我要冒昧地提出我孩子的愛。

passages.original: I think she will be rul’d In all respects by me;
passages.vernacular: 我想佢喺一切方面都會聽我嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想她在一切方面都會聽我的;

passages.original: nay more, I doubt it not.
passages.vernacular: 不,而且我毫不懷疑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,而且我毫不懷疑。

passages.original: Wife, go you to her ere you go to bed, Acquaint her here of my son Paris’ love, And bid her, mark you me, on Wednesday next, But, soft, what day is this?
passages.vernacular: 妻子,你瞓前去見佢,告訴佢我兒子帕里斯嘅愛,並叫佢,聽住,下星期三,——但係,慢住,今日係星期幾?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 妻子,你睡前去見她,告訴她我兒子帕里斯的愛,並叫她,聽著,下星期三,——但是,慢著,今天是星期幾?

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: Monday, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 星期一,老爺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期一,老爺。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Monday! Ha, ha!
passages.vernacular: 星期一!哈,哈!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期一!哈,哈!

passages.original: Well, Wednesday is too soon, A Thursday let it be;
passages.vernacular: 好,星期三太早,就定星期四吧;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,星期三太早,就定星期四吧;

passages.original: a Thursday, tell her, She shall be married to this noble earl.
passages.vernacular: 告訴佢,星期四佢要嫁畀呢位高貴嘅伯爵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴她,星期四她要嫁給這位高貴的伯爵。

passages.original: Will you be ready?
passages.vernacular: 你準備好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你準備好嗎?

passages.original: Do you like this haste?
passages.vernacular: 你鍾意咁樣倉促嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你喜歡這樣倉促嗎?

passages.original: We’ll keep no great ado,—a friend or two, For, hark you, Tybalt being slain so late, It may be thought we held him carelessly, Being our kinsman, if we revel much.
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔會大操大辦,——一兩個朋友,因為,聽住,提伯特啱啱被殺,如果我哋大肆慶祝,人哋會以為我哋不把佢當親戚睇重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不會大操大辦,——一兩個朋友,因為,聽著,提伯特剛剛被殺,如果我們大肆慶祝,人們會以為我們不把他當親戚看重。

passages.original: Therefore we’ll have some half a dozen friends, And there an end.
passages.vernacular: 所以我哋請六個左右嘅朋友,就此為止。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我們請六個左右的朋友,就此為止。

passages.original: But what say you to Thursday?
passages.vernacular: 但你對星期四點講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你對星期四怎麼說?

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: My lord, I would that Thursday were tomorrow.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我但願星期四就係聽日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我但願星期四就是明天。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Well, get you gone.
passages.vernacular: 好,你走吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,你走吧。

passages.original: A Thursday be it then.
passages.vernacular: 嗰就星期四。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就星期四。

passages.original: Go you to Juliet ere you go to bed, Prepare her, wife, against this wedding day.
passages.vernacular: 你瞓前去見茱麗葉,為呢婚禮之日讓佢準備好,妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你睡前去見茱麗葉,為這婚禮之日讓她準備好,妻子。

passages.original: Farewell, my lord.—Light to my chamber, ho!
passages.vernacular: 再會,大人。——畀我嘅臥室點燈,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會,大人。——給我的臥室點燈,喂!

passages.original: Afore me, it is so very very late that we May call it early by and by. Good night.
passages.vernacular: 憑我嘅性命,時間已如此之晚,我哋可以講成係一會兒就算早喇。晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑我的性命,時間已如此之晚,我們可以說成是一會兒就算早了。晚安。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene V — An Open Gallery to Juliet’s Chamber 第三幕第五場:茱麗葉閨房外的露台

passages.original: Enter Romeo and Juliet.
passages.vernacular: [羅密歐同茱麗葉上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅密歐與茱麗葉上。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Wilt thou be gone?
passages.vernacular: 你要走咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要走了嗎?

passages.original: It is not yet near day.
passages.vernacular: 天仲冇近亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天還沒近亮。

passages.original: It was the nightingale, and not the lark, That pierc’d the fearful hollow of thine ear;
passages.vernacular: 刺穿你驚恐耳洞嘅係夜鶯,唔係雲雀;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 刺穿你驚恐耳洞的是夜鶯,不是雲雀;

passages.original: Nightly she sings on yond pomegranate tree.
passages.vernacular: 佢每夜喺嗰邊嘅石榴樹上歌唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她每夜在那邊的石榴樹上歌唱。

passages.original: Believe me, love, it was the nightingale.
passages.vernacular: 相信我,愛人,嗰個係夜鶯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信我,愛人,那是夜鶯。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: It was the lark, the herald of the morn, No nightingale.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係雲雀,黎明嘅使者,唔係夜鶯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是雲雀,黎明的使者,不是夜鶯。

passages.original: Look, love, what envious streaks Do lace the severing clouds in yonder east.
passages.vernacular: 睇,愛人,嗰邊東方,嫉妒嘅條紋點樣鑲住分開嘅雲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,愛人,那邊東方,嫉妒的條紋怎樣鑲著分開的雲。

passages.original: Night’s candles are burnt out, and jocund day Stands tiptoe on the misty mountain tops.
passages.vernacular: 夜嘅蠟燭已燃盡,歡快嘅白晝踮住腳尖站喺霧濛濛嘅山頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夜的蠟燭已燃盡,歡快的白晝踮著腳尖站在霧濛濛的山頂。

passages.original: I must be gone and live, or stay and die.
passages.vernacular: 我必須走掉才能活,或留下而死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須走掉才能活,或留下而死。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Yond light is not daylight, I know it, I.
passages.vernacular: 嗰邊嘅光唔係日光,我知道,我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那邊的光不是日光,我知道,我。

passages.original: It is some meteor that the sun exhales To be to thee this night a torchbearer And light thee on thy way to Mantua.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係太陽呼出嘅某種流星,今夜為你擎燈,照你前往曼圖亞嘅路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是太陽呼出的某種流星,今夜為你擎燈,照你前往曼圖亞的路。

passages.original: Therefore stay yet, thou need’st not to be gone.
passages.vernacular: 所以再留一會兒,你唔使走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以再留一會兒,你不必走。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Let me be ta’en, let me be put to death, I am content, so thou wilt have it so.
passages.vernacular: 讓我被捕,讓我被處死,我甘願,只要你希望如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我被捕,讓我被處死,我甘願,只要你希望如此。

passages.original: I’ll say yon grey is not the morning’s eye, ’Tis but the pale reflex of Cynthia’s brow.
passages.vernacular: 我就講嗰邊嘅灰色唔係黎明嘅眼睛,只係辛西婭額頭蒼白嘅反光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就說那邊的灰色不是黎明的眼睛,只是辛西婭額頭蒼白的反光。

passages.original: Nor that is not the lark whose notes do beat The vaulty heaven so high above our heads.
passages.vernacular: 嗰都唔係雲雀,佢嘅歌聲震動我哋頭上咁高嘅穹蒼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那也不是雲雀,它的歌聲震動我們頭上那麼高的穹蒼。

passages.original: I have more care to stay than will to go.
passages.vernacular: 我留下嘅心意比離開嘅意願更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我留下的心意比離開的意願更多。

passages.original: Come, death, and welcome.
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧,死亡,歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧,死亡,歡迎。

passages.original: Juliet wills it so.
passages.vernacular: 茱麗葉願意咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 茱麗葉願意這樣。

passages.original: How is’t, my soul? Let’s talk.
passages.vernacular: 點樣喇,我嘅靈魂?我哋講話吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎樣了,我的靈魂?我們說話吧。

passages.original: It is not day.
passages.vernacular: 仲唔係白天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還不是白天。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: It is, it is!
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,係嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,是的!

passages.original: Hie hence, be gone, away.
passages.vernacular: 快走,離開,走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快走,離開,走。

passages.original: It is the lark that sings so out of tune, Straining harsh discords and unpleasing sharps.
passages.vernacular: 唱得咁走調嘅係雲雀,拼命發出刺耳嘅不和諧音同令人不快嘅升調。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唱得這麼走調的是雲雀,拼命發出刺耳的不和諧音與令人不快的升調。

passages.original: Some say the lark makes sweet division; This doth not so, for she divideth us.
passages.vernacular: 有人講雲雀嘅曲調婉轉;呢隻卻唔係,因為佢把我哋分開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人說雲雀的曲調婉轉;這隻卻不是,因為她把我們分開。

passages.original: Some say the lark and loathed toad change eyes.
passages.vernacular: 有人講雲雀同可恨嘅蟾蜍交換咗眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人說雲雀和可恨的蟾蜍交換了眼睛。

passages.original: O, now I would they had chang’d voices too, Since arm from arm that voice doth us affray, Hunting thee hence with hunt’s-up to the day.
passages.vernacular: 啊,而家我希望佢哋都交換咗聲音,因為嗰聲音把我哋從彼此臂彎中驚散,用晨獵號曲把你趕往白晝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,現在我希望它們也交換了聲音,因為那聲音把我們從彼此臂彎中驚散,用晨獵號曲把你趕往白晝。

passages.original: O now be gone, more light and light it grows.
passages.vernacular: 啊,而家快走,光越嚟越亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,現在快走,光越來越亮。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: More light and light, more dark and dark our woes.
passages.vernacular: 光越嚟越亮,我哋嘅憂傷越嚟越黑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 光越來越亮,我們的憂傷越來越黑。

passages.original: Enter Nurse.
passages.vernacular: [奶媽上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奶媽上。]

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Madam.
passages.vernacular: 小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姐。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Nurse?
passages.vernacular: 奶媽?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奶媽?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Your lady mother is coming to your chamber.
passages.vernacular: 你母親夫人正嚟你嘅房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你母親夫人正來你的房間。

passages.original: The day is broke, be wary, look about.
passages.vernacular: 天亮喇,小心,睇睇四周。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天亮了,小心,看看四周。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Then, window, let day in, and let life out.
passages.vernacular: 咁,窗戶,讓白晝進嚟,讓生命出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,窗戶,讓白晝進來,讓生命出去。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Farewell, farewell, one kiss, and I’ll descend.
passages.vernacular: 再見,再見,一個吻,我就下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見,再見,一個吻,我就下去。

passages.original: [Descends.]
passages.vernacular: [下去。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [下去。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Art thou gone so?
passages.vernacular: 你就咁樣走咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你就這樣走了嗎?

passages.original: Love, lord, ay husband, friend, I must hear from thee every day in the hour, For in a minute there are many days.
passages.vernacular: 愛人,主人,係,丈夫,朋友,我必須每天每小時聽到你嘅消息,因為一分鐘裡有許多天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛人,主人,是,丈夫,朋友,我必須每天每小時聽到你的消息,因為一分鐘裡有許多天。

passages.original: O, by this count I shall be much in years Ere I again behold my Romeo.
passages.vernacular: 啊,照咁樣算,我再見到我嘅羅密歐之前,會年紀大得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,照這樣算,我再見到我的羅密歐之前,會年紀大得多。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: Farewell!
passages.vernacular: 再見!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見!

passages.original: I will omit no opportunity That may convey my greetings, love, to thee.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會錯過任何可以把我嘅問候傳畀你嘅機會,愛人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會錯過任何可以把我的問候傳給你的機會,愛人。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O thinkest thou we shall ever meet again?
passages.vernacular: 啊,你認為我哋仲會再見嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,你認為我們還會再見嗎?

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: I doubt it not, and all these woes shall serve For sweet discourses in our time to come.
passages.vernacular: 我毫不懷疑,呢一切嘅悲傷將成為我哋日後甜蜜嘅談資。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我毫不懷疑,這一切的悲傷將成為我們日後甜蜜的談資。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O God!
passages.vernacular: 啊上帝!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊上帝!

passages.original: I have an ill-divining soul!
passages.vernacular: 我有一個不祥嘅預感嘅靈魂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有一個不祥的預感的靈魂!

passages.original: Methinks I see thee, now thou art so low, As one dead in the bottom of a tomb.
passages.vernacular: 我好像睇見你,而家你咁樣低,像一個死人喺墓底。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我好像看見你,現在你這樣低,像一個死人在墓底。

passages.original: Either my eyesight fails, or thou look’st pale.
passages.vernacular: 要麼我嘅視力衰退,要麼你臉色蒼白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要麼我的視力衰退,要麼你臉色蒼白。

passages.title: Romeo 羅密歐
passages.original: And trust me, love, in my eye so do you.
passages.vernacular: 相信我,愛人,喺我眼中你都係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信我,愛人,在我眼中你也是這樣。

passages.original: Dry sorrow drinks our blood.
passages.vernacular: 乾燥嘅悲傷飲乾我哋嘅血。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 乾燥的悲傷飲乾我們的血。

passages.original: Adieu, adieu.
passages.vernacular: 再會,再會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會,再會。

passages.original: [Exit below.]
passages.vernacular: [從下面下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [從下面下。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O Fortune, Fortune!
passages.vernacular: 啊命運,命運!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊命運,命運!

passages.original: All men call thee fickle, If thou art fickle, what dost thou with him That is renown’d for faith?
passages.vernacular: 所有人都講你反覆無常,如果你反覆無常,你對一個以忠誠聞名嘅人做乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有人都說你反覆無常,如果你反覆無常,你對一個以忠誠聞名的人做什麼?

passages.original: Be fickle, Fortune; For then, I hope thou wilt not keep him long But send him back.
passages.vernacular: 反覆無常吧,命運;因為嗰樣,我希望你唔會長久留住佢,而把佢送回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 反覆無常吧,命運;因為那樣,我希望你不會長久留住他,而把他送回來。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: [Within.]
passages.vernacular: [在內。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [在內。]

passages.original: Ho, daughter, are you up?
passages.vernacular: 喂,女兒,你起嚟咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂,女兒,你起來了嗎?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Who is’t that calls?
passages.vernacular: 邊個喺叫?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰在叫?

passages.original: Is it my lady mother?
passages.vernacular: 係我母親夫人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是我母親夫人嗎?

passages.original: Is she not down so late, or up so early?
passages.vernacular: 佢係咁晚仲冇瞓,定係咁早就起嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是這麼晚還沒睡,還是這麼早就起來?

passages.original: What unaccustom’d cause procures her hither?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢不尋常嘅原因把佢帶到呢度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼不尋常的原因把她帶到這裡?

passages.original: Enter Lady Capulet.
passages.vernacular: [凱普雷特夫人上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱普雷特夫人上。]

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Why, how now, Juliet?
passages.vernacular: 點喇,茱麗葉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,茱麗葉?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Madam, I am not well.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,我不舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,我不舒服。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Evermore weeping for your cousin’s death?
passages.vernacular: 仲喺為你堂兄嘅死哭嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還在為你堂兄的死哭嗎?

passages.original: What, wilt thou wash him from his grave with tears?
passages.vernacular: 點,你想用眼淚把佢從墳墓裡洗出嚟嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,你想用眼淚把他從墳墓裡洗出來嗎?

passages.original: And if thou couldst, thou couldst not make him live.
passages.vernacular: 就算你能,你都唔能夠讓佢活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就算你能,你也不能讓他活。

passages.original: Therefore have done: some grief shows much of love, But much of grief shows still some want of wit.
passages.vernacular: 所以算咗吧:啲悲傷顯出好多愛,但太多悲傷總顯出缺少智慧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以算了吧:一點悲傷顯出很多愛,但太多悲傷總顯出缺少智慧。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Yet let me weep for such a feeling loss.
passages.vernacular: 但讓我為咁樣切膚嘅損失哭吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但讓我為這樣切膚的損失哭吧。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: So shall you feel the loss, but not the friend Which you weep for.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣你會感受到損失,卻唔係你所哭嘅嗰個朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣你會感受到損失,卻不是你所哭的那個朋友。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Feeling so the loss, I cannot choose but ever weep the friend.
passages.vernacular: 既然感受到呢損失,我就唔能夠不永遠為嗰朋友哭泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然感受到這損失,我就不能不永遠為那朋友哭泣。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Well, girl, thou weep’st not so much for his death As that the villain lives which slaughter’d him.
passages.vernacular: 好,女孩,你哭並唔係為佢嘅死,而係為殺佢嘅惡棍仲活住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,女孩,你哭並不是為他的死,而是為殺他的惡棍還活著。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: What villain, madam?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢惡棍,夫人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼惡棍,夫人?

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: That same villain Romeo.
passages.vernacular: 就係嗰個惡棍羅密歐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是那個惡棍羅密歐。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Villain and he be many miles asunder.
passages.vernacular: 惡棍同佢相隔好幾英里遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 惡棍和他相隔好幾英里遠。

passages.original: God pardon him.
passages.vernacular: 願上帝饒恕佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上帝饒恕他。

passages.original: I do, with all my heart.
passages.vernacular: 我全心全意咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我全心全意這樣。

passages.original: And yet no man like he doth grieve my heart.
passages.vernacular: 不過冇人像佢一樣使我心痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是沒有人像他一樣使我心痛。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: That is because the traitor murderer lives.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係因為嗰個叛徒兇手仲活住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是因為那個叛徒兇手還活著。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Ay madam, from the reach of these my hands.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,夫人,喺我呢雙手夠唔到嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,夫人,在我這雙手夠不到的地方。

passages.original: Would none but I might venge my cousin’s death.
passages.vernacular: 但願只有我能為堂兄嘅死報仇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但願只有我能為堂兄的死報仇。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: We will have vengeance for it, fear thou not.
passages.vernacular: 我哋會為此報仇,你別怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們會為此報仇,你別怕。

passages.original: Then weep no more.
passages.vernacular: 咁唔好再哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼別再哭了。

passages.original: I’ll send to one in Mantua, Where that same banish’d runagate doth live, Shall give him such an unaccustom’d dram That he shall soon keep Tybalt company:
passages.vernacular: 我要派人去曼圖亞,嗰個被放逐嘅逃犯住嘅地方,畀佢一劑不尋常嘅藥水,讓佢好快去陪提伯特:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要派人去曼圖亞,那個被放逐的逃犯住的地方,給他一劑不尋常的藥水,讓他很快去陪提伯特:

passages.original: And then I hope thou wilt be satisfied.
passages.vernacular: 嗰時我希望你會滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那時我希望你會滿意。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Indeed I never shall be satisfied With Romeo till I behold him—dead— Is my poor heart so for a kinsman vex’d.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,我永遠唔會對羅密歐滿意,除非我睇到佢——死喇——我可憐嘅心才為一個親戚咁樣煩惱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,我永遠不會對羅密歐滿意,除非我看到他——死了——我可憐的心才為一個親戚這樣煩惱。

passages.original: Madam, if you could find out but a man To bear a poison, I would temper it, That Romeo should upon receipt thereof, Soon sleep in quiet.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,如果你能找到一個人帶毒藥,我嚟調配,好讓羅密歐一收到,好快就安詳瞓去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,如果你能找到一個人帶毒藥,我來調配,好讓羅密歐一收到,很快就安詳睡去。

passages.original: O, how my heart abhors To hear him nam’d, and cannot come to him, To wreak the love I bore my cousin Upon his body that hath slaughter’d him.
passages.vernacular: 啊,聽到佢嘅名字,我嘅心幾咁憎恨,卻唔能夠到佢嗰度,把我對堂兄嘅愛報復喺殺佢嘅人身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,聽到他的名字,我的心多麼憎恨,卻不能到他那裡,把我對堂兄的愛報復在殺他的人身上。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Find thou the means, and I’ll find such a man.
passages.vernacular: 你找到辦法,我就找咁樣嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你找到辦法,我就找這樣的人。

passages.original: But now I’ll tell thee joyful tidings, girl.
passages.vernacular: 但而家我要告訴你喜訊,細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在我要告訴你喜訊,孩子。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: And joy comes well in such a needy time.
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣需要嘅時候,喜悅嚟得正好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣需要的時候,喜悅來得正好。

passages.original: What are they, I beseech your ladyship?
passages.vernacular: 係乜嘢,請告訴我,夫人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是什麼,請告訴我,夫人?

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Well, well, thou hast a careful father, child;
passages.vernacular: 好,好,你有個關心你嘅父親,細路;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,好,你有個關心你的父親,孩子;

passages.original: One who to put thee from thy heaviness, Hath sorted out a sudden day of joy, That thou expects not, nor I look’d not for.
passages.vernacular: 為了讓你擺脫沉重,佢安排咗一個突然嘅歡樂日子,係你冇預料到,我都冇料到嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了讓你擺脫沉重,他安排了一個突然的歡樂日子,是你沒預料到,我也沒料到的。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Madam, in happy time, what day is that?
passages.vernacular: 夫人,嚟得正好,係邊一天?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,來得正好,是哪一天?

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Marry, my child, early next Thursday morn The gallant, young, and noble gentleman, The County Paris, at Saint Peter’s Church, Shall happily make thee there a joyful bride.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,我嘅細路,下星期四一大早,嗰位英勇、年輕、高貴嘅紳士,帕里斯伯爵,將喺聖彼得教堂,快樂地使你成為一個歡樂嘅新娘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,我的孩子,下星期四一大早,那位英勇、年輕、高貴的紳士,帕里斯伯爵,將在聖彼得教堂,快樂地使你成為一個歡樂的新娘。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Now by Saint Peter’s Church, and Peter too, He shall not make me there a joyful bride.
passages.vernacular: 憑聖彼得教堂,同彼得本人,佢唔會喺嗰度使我成為歡樂嘅新娘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑聖彼得教堂,和彼得本人,他不會在那裡使我成為歡樂的新娘。

passages.original: I wonder at this haste, that I must wed Ere he that should be husband comes to woo.
passages.vernacular: 我對呢倉促感到奇怪,我竟要喺嗰應該做丈夫嘅人嚟求婚之前出嫁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對這倉促感到奇怪,我竟要在那應該做丈夫的人來求婚之前出嫁。

passages.original: I pray you tell my lord and father, madam, I will not marry yet;
passages.vernacular: 求您告訴我嘅老爺父親,夫人,我仲不嫁;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求您告訴我的老爺父親,夫人,我還不嫁;

passages.original: and when I do, I swear It shall be Romeo, whom you know I hate, Rather than Paris.
passages.vernacular: 等我嫁時,我發誓,會係羅密歐,您知道我恨佢,而唔係帕里斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等我嫁時,我發誓,會是羅密歐,您知道我恨他,而不是帕里斯。

passages.original: These are news indeed.
passages.vernacular: 呢真係消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這真是消息。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Here comes your father, tell him so yourself, And see how he will take it at your hands.
passages.vernacular: 你父親嚟喇,你自己對佢講,睇佢點樣接受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你父親來了,你自己對他說,看他怎樣接受。

passages.original: Enter Capulet and Nurse.
passages.vernacular: [凱普雷特同奶媽上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱普雷特與奶媽上。]

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: When the sun sets, the air doth drizzle dew; But for the sunset of my brother’s son It rains downright. How now?
passages.vernacular: 太陽落時,空氣滴下露水;但為我哥哥兒子嘅日落,卻下起傾盆大雨。點喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太陽落時,空氣滴下露水;但為我哥哥兒子的日落,卻下起傾盆大雨。怎麼了?

passages.original: A conduit, girl?
passages.vernacular: 一個水管,細路?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個水管,孩子?

passages.original: What, still in tears?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,仲喺流淚?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,還在流淚?

passages.original: Evermore showering?
passages.vernacular: 一直喺淋雨?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一直在淋雨?

passages.original: In one little body Thou counterfeits a bark, a sea, a wind.
passages.vernacular: 喺一個小小嘅身體裡,你扮出一艘船、一片海、一陣風。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在一個小小的身體裡,你扮出一艘船、一片海、一陣風。

passages.original: For still thy eyes, which I may call the sea, Do ebb and flow with tears;
passages.vernacular: 因為你嘅眼睛,我可以叫做海,一直隨眼淚漲落;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你的眼睛,我可以叫做海,一直隨眼淚漲落;

passages.original: the bark thy body is, Sailing in this salt flood, the winds, thy sighs, Who raging with thy tears and they with them, Without a sudden calm will overset Thy tempest-tossed body.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅身體係船,喺呢鹹水洪流中航行,風係你嘅嘆息,同你嘅眼淚一同狂暴,若不即刻平靜,就會把你被風暴顛簸嘅身體顛覆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的身體是船,在這鹹水洪流中航行,風是你的嘆息,和你的眼淚一同狂暴,若不立刻平靜,就會把你被風暴顛簸的身體顛覆。

passages.original: How now, wife?
passages.vernacular: 點喇,妻子?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,妻子?

passages.original: Have you deliver’d to her our decree?
passages.vernacular: 你把我哋嘅決定告訴佢咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把我們的決定告訴她了嗎?

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Ay, sir; but she will none, she gives you thanks.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,老爺;但佢唔好,佢謝謝你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,老爺;但她不要,她謝謝你。

passages.original: I would the fool were married to her grave.
passages.vernacular: 我真希望呢傻瓜嫁畀佢嘅墳墓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望這傻瓜嫁給她的墳墓。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Soft.
passages.vernacular: 慢住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 慢著。

passages.original: Take me with you, take me with you, wife.
passages.vernacular: 讓我跟上你,讓我跟上你,妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我跟上你,讓我跟上你,妻子。

passages.original: How, will she none?
passages.vernacular: 點,佢唔好?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,她不要?

passages.original: Doth she not give us thanks?
passages.vernacular: 佢不謝我哋嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不謝我們嗎?

passages.original: Is she not proud?
passages.vernacular: 佢不驕傲嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不驕傲嗎?

passages.original: Doth she not count her blest, Unworthy as she is, that we have wrought So worthy a gentleman to be her bridegroom?
passages.vernacular: 佢不覺得自己蒙福嗎,雖然佢不配,我哋竟為佢找到咁樣一位配得上嘅紳士做新郎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不覺得自己蒙福嗎,雖然她不配,我們竟為她找到這樣一位配得上的紳士做新郎?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Not proud you have, but thankful that you have.
passages.vernacular: 你哋畀嘅我不驕傲,但謝謝你哋有呢份心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們給的我不驕傲,但謝謝你們有這份心。

passages.original: Proud can I never be of what I hate; But thankful even for hate that is meant love.
passages.vernacular: 對我所恨嘅我永遠唔能夠驕傲;但對嗰出自愛嘅恨,我都感謝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我所恨的我永遠不能驕傲;但對那出自愛的恨,我也感謝。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: How now, how now, chopp’d logic?
passages.vernacular: 點,點,呢剪裁嘅邏輯?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,怎麼,這剪裁的邏輯?

passages.original: What is this?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是什麼?

passages.original: Proud, and, I thank you, and I thank you not; And yet not proud.
passages.vernacular: 「驕傲」,「我謝謝你」,「我又不謝你」;又不驕傲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「驕傲」,「我謝謝你」,「我又不謝你」;又不驕傲。

passages.original: Mistress minion you, Thank me no thankings, nor proud me no prouds, But fettle your fine joints ’gainst Thursday next To go with Paris to Saint Peter’s Church, Or I will drag thee on a hurdle thither.
passages.vernacular: 你呢寵兒小姐,別對我謝嚟謝去,都別驕傲嚟驕傲去,把你嘅漂亮身子準備好,下星期四跟帕里斯去聖彼得教堂,否則我就用囚車把你拖到嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這寵兒小姐,別對我謝來謝去,也別驕傲來驕傲去,把你的漂亮身子準備好,下星期四跟帕里斯去聖彼得教堂,否則我就用囚車把你拖到那裡。

passages.original: Out, you green-sickness carrion!
passages.vernacular: 滾開,你呢萎黃病嘅死屍!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滾開,你這萎黃病的死屍!

passages.original: Out, you baggage!
passages.vernacular: 滾開,你呢賤貨!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滾開,你這賤貨!

passages.original: You tallow-face!
passages.vernacular: 你呢蠟臉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這蠟臉!

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Fie, fie!
passages.vernacular: 呸,呸!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呸,呸!

passages.original: What, are you mad?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,你瘋咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,你瘋了嗎?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Good father, I beseech you on my knees, Hear me with patience but to speak a word.
passages.vernacular: 好父親,我跪住求您,耐心聽我講一句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好父親,我跪著求您,耐心聽我說一句話。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Hang thee young baggage, disobedient wretch!
passages.vernacular: 該吊死你,年輕嘅賤貨,不聽話嘅可憐蟲!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 該吊死你,年輕的賤貨,不聽話的可憐蟲!

passages.original: I tell thee what,—get thee to church a Thursday, Or never after look me in the face.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴你,——星期四去教堂,否則以後唔好再嚟見我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴你,——星期四去教堂,否則以後別再來見我。

passages.original: Speak not, reply not, do not answer me.
passages.vernacular: 唔好講話,唔好回嘴,唔好回答我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要說話,不要回嘴,不要回答我。

passages.original: My fingers itch.
passages.vernacular: 我手指發癢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我手指發癢。

passages.original: Wife, we scarce thought us blest That God had lent us but this only child;
passages.vernacular: 妻子,我哋本以為蒙福,上帝只借畀我哋呢一個細路;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 妻子,我們本以為蒙福,上帝只借給我們這一個孩子;

passages.original: But now I see this one is one too much, And that we have a curse in having her.
passages.vernacular: 但而家我睇呢一個都太多喇,有咗佢係我哋嘅詛咒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在我看這一個也太多了,有了她是我們的詛咒。

passages.original: Out on her, hilding.
passages.vernacular: 滾開,賤嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滾開,賤東西。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: God in heaven bless her.
passages.vernacular: 天上嘅上帝保佑佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天上的上帝保佑她。

passages.original: You are to blame, my lord, to rate her so.
passages.vernacular: 您咁樣責罵佢,大人,係您不對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您這樣責罵她,大人,是您不對。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: And why, my lady wisdom?
passages.vernacular: 點解,我嘅女智者夫人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼,我的女智者夫人?

passages.original: Hold your tongue, Good prudence; smatter with your gossips, go.
passages.vernacular: 閉嘴,好謹慎;去跟你嘅閒談夥伴嘮叨吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 閉嘴,好謹慎;去跟你的閒談夥伴嘮叨吧。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: I speak no treason.
passages.vernacular: 我冇講叛逆嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有說叛逆的話。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: O God ye good-en!
passages.vernacular: 啊,願上帝賜你晚安!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,願上帝賜你晚安!

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: May not one speak?
passages.vernacular: 一個人不可以講話嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個人不可以說話嗎?

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Peace, you mumbling fool!
passages.vernacular: 住口,你呢喃喃自語嘅傻瓜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 住口,你這喃喃自語的傻瓜!

passages.original: Utter your gravity o’er a gossip’s bowl, For here we need it not.
passages.vernacular: 喺閒談夥伴嘅碗邊發表你嘅莊重吧,因為呢度我哋不需要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在閒談夥伴的碗邊發表你的莊重吧,因為這裡我們不需要。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: You are too hot.
passages.vernacular: 您太火爆喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您太火爆了。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: God’s bread, it makes me mad!
passages.vernacular: 天呀,呢使我發瘋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,這使我發瘋!

passages.original: Day, night, hour, ride, time, work, play, Alone, in company, still my care hath been To have her match’d, and having now provided A gentleman of noble parentage, Of fair demesnes, youthful, and nobly allied, Stuff’d, as they say, with honourable parts, Proportion’d as one’s thought would wish a man, And then to have a wretched puling fool, A whining mammet, in her fortune’s tender, To answer, ‘I’ll not wed, I cannot love, I am too young, I pray you pardon me.’
passages.vernacular: 白天,黑夜,時時刻刻,騎馬,時間,工作,玩耍,獨處,喺人群中,我一直操心要畀佢找個好對象,而家找到咗一位出身高貴、田產豐美、年輕、姻親高貴嘅紳士,據講滿身係光榮嘅優點,體態如人所想嘅男子,然後卻有一個可憐嘅啼哭傻瓜,一個哭哭啼啼嘅玩偶,喺佢命運嘅獻上之時,回答「我不嫁,我唔能夠愛,我太年輕,請原諒我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白天,黑夜,時時刻刻,騎馬,時間,工作,玩耍,獨處,在人群中,我一直操心要給她找個好對象,現在找到了一位出身高貴、田產豐美、年輕、姻親高貴的紳士,據說滿身是光榮的優點,體態如人所想的男子,然後卻有一個可憐的啼哭傻瓜,一個哭哭啼啼的玩偶,在她命運的獻上之時,回答「我不嫁,我不能愛,我太年輕,請原諒我。」

passages.original: But, and you will not wed, I’ll pardon you.
passages.vernacular: 但係,如果你不嫁,我原諒你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,如果你不嫁,我原諒你。

passages.original: Graze where you will, you shall not house with me.
passages.vernacular: 愛到邊度食草就去邊度,你別想跟我同住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛到哪裡吃草就去哪裡,你別想跟我同住。

passages.original: Look to’t, think on’t, I do not use to jest.
passages.vernacular: 當心,想想,我唔係開玩笑嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當心,想想,我不是開玩笑的。

passages.original: Thursday is near; lay hand on heart, advise.
passages.vernacular: 星期四近喇;手放喺心上,考慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期四近了;手放在心上,考慮。

passages.original: And you be mine, I’ll give you to my friend; And you be not, hang, beg, starve, die in the streets, For by my soul, I’ll ne’er acknowledge thee, Nor what is mine shall never do thee good.
passages.vernacular: 如果你係我嘅,我就把你畀我嘅朋友;如果唔係,就上吊、乞討、挨餓、死喺街上,因為憑我嘅靈魂,我永遠不認你,我嘅嘢都永遠唔會對你有好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你是我的,我就把你給我的朋友;如果不是,就上吊、乞討、挨餓、死在街上,因為憑我的靈魂,我永遠不認你,我的東西也永遠不會對你有好處。

passages.original: Trust to’t, bethink you, I’ll not be forsworn.
passages.vernacular: 相信吧,想想,我唔會發假誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信吧,想想,我不會發假誓。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Is there no pity sitting in the clouds, That sees into the bottom of my grief?
passages.vernacular: 天上嘅雲裡難道冇憐憫坐住,睇得見我悲傷嘅底部嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天上的雲裡難道沒有憐憫坐著,看得見我悲傷的底部嗎?

passages.original: O sweet my mother, cast me not away, Delay this marriage for a month, a week, Or, if you do not, make the bridal bed In that dim monument where Tybalt lies.
passages.vernacular: 啊,親愛嘅母親,別拋棄我,把呢婚事延遲一個月,一星期,或者,如果您唔肯,就把婚床鋪喺提伯特躺住嘅嗰個昏暗嘅墓穴裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,親愛的母親,別拋棄我,把這婚事延遲一個月,一星期,或者,如果您不肯,就把婚床鋪在提伯特躺著的那個昏暗的墓穴裡。

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: Talk not to me, for I’ll not speak a word.
passages.vernacular: 別跟我講話,因為我一句話都不講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別跟我說話,因為我一句話也不說。

passages.original: Do as thou wilt, for I have done with thee.
passages.vernacular: 隨你愛點做,我同你完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨你愛怎麼做,我和你完了。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O God!
passages.vernacular: 啊上帝!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊上帝!

passages.original: O Nurse, how shall this be prevented?
passages.vernacular: 啊奶媽,點樣才能阻止呢件事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊奶媽,怎樣才能阻止這件事?

passages.original: My husband is on earth, my faith in heaven.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅丈夫喺地上,我嘅誓言喺天上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的丈夫在地上,我的誓言在天上。

passages.original: How shall that faith return again to earth, Unless that husband send it me from heaven By leaving earth?
passages.vernacular: 嗰誓言點樣再回到地上,除非嗰丈夫離開地上,從天上把佢送畀我?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那誓言怎樣再回到地上,除非那丈夫離開地上,從天上把它送給我?

passages.original: Comfort me, counsel me.
passages.vernacular: 安慰我,指點我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安慰我,指點我。

passages.original: Alack, alack, that heaven should practise stratagems Upon so soft a subject as myself.
passages.vernacular: 唉,唉,天上竟對像我咁樣柔弱嘅對象使用計謀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,唉,天上竟對像我這樣柔弱的對象使用計謀。

passages.original: What say’st thou?
passages.vernacular: 你講乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說什麼?

passages.original: Hast thou not a word of joy?
passages.vernacular: 你就冇一句喜悅嘅話嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你就沒有一句喜悅的話嗎?

passages.original: Some comfort, Nurse.
passages.vernacular: 畀點安慰,奶媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給點安慰,奶媽。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Faith, here it is.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,呢個就係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,這就是。

passages.original: Romeo is banished; and all the world to nothing That he dares ne’er come back to challenge you.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐被放逐喇;而且全世界賭佢一無所有,佢永遠唔敢回嚟向你提出要求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐被放逐了;而且全世界賭他一無所有,他永遠不敢回來向你提出要求。

passages.original: Or if he do, it needs must be by stealth.
passages.vernacular: 或者如果佢回嚟,都必須偷偷摸摸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者如果他回來,也必須偷偷摸摸。

passages.original: Then, since the case so stands as now it doth, I think it best you married with the County.
passages.vernacular: 咁,既然情形如此,我想你最好嫁畀伯爵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,既然情形如此,我想你最好嫁給伯爵。

passages.original: O, he’s a lovely gentleman.
passages.vernacular: 啊,佢係位可愛嘅紳士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,他是位可愛的紳士。

passages.original: Romeo’s a dishclout to him.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐跟佢比,只係塊抹碗布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐跟他比,只是塊抹碗布。

passages.original: An eagle, madam, Hath not so green, so quick, so fair an eye As Paris hath.
passages.vernacular: 小姐,老鷹嘅眼睛都冇帕里斯嗰樣綠、嗰樣敏銳、嗰樣漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姐,老鷹的眼睛也沒有帕里斯那樣綠、那樣敏銳、那樣漂亮。

passages.original: Beshrew my very heart, I think you are happy in this second match, For it excels your first:
passages.vernacular: 該詛咒我嘅心,我想你喺呢第二次婚姻中會好幸福,因為佢勝過你嘅第一次:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 該詛咒我的心,我想你在這第二次婚姻中會很幸福,因為它勝過你的第一次:

passages.original: or if it did not, Your first is dead, or ’twere as good he were, As living here and you no use of him.
passages.vernacular: 或者如果冇,你嘅第一個已死,或者同死咗一樣,活喺呢度卻對你冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者如果沒有,你的第一個已死,或者和死了一樣,活在這裡卻對你沒用。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Speakest thou from thy heart?
passages.vernacular: 你呢個係出自真心講嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這是出自真心說的嗎?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: And from my soul too, Or else beshrew them both.
passages.vernacular: 都出自我嘅靈魂,否則該詛咒呢兩者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也出自我的靈魂,否則該詛咒這兩者。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Amen.
passages.vernacular: 阿哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿們。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: What?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Well, thou hast comforted me marvellous much.
passages.vernacular: 好,你畀咗我好大嘅安慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,你給了我非常大的安慰。

passages.original: Go in, and tell my lady I am gone, Having displeas’d my father, to Lawrence’ cell, To make confession and to be absolv’d.
passages.vernacular: 進去告訴我母親,我因為得罪咗我父親,去勞倫斯嘅修室喇,去懺悔並求赦免。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 進去告訴我母親,我因為得罪了我父親,去勞倫斯的修室了,去懺悔並求赦免。

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Marry, I will; and this is wisely done.
passages.vernacular: 好,我會;呢做得明智。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,我會;這做得明智。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Ancient damnation!
passages.vernacular: 老不死嘅該死!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老不死的該死!

passages.original: O most wicked fiend!
passages.vernacular: 啊最邪惡嘅魔鬼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊最邪惡的魔鬼!

passages.original: Is it more sin to wish me thus forsworn, Or to dispraise my lord with that same tongue Which she hath prais’d him with above compare So many thousand times?
passages.vernacular: 係教我背誓更有罪,定係用嗰同一條舌頭詆毀我嘅夫君,而嗰舌頭曾千千萬萬次無比地稱讚佢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是教我背誓更有罪,還是用那同一條舌頭詆毀我的夫君,而那舌頭曾千千萬萬次無比地稱讚他?

passages.original: Go, counsellor.
passages.vernacular: 去吧,謀士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去吧,謀士。

passages.original: Thou and my bosom henceforth shall be twain.
passages.vernacular: 你同我嘅心從此分開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你和我的心從此分開。

passages.original: I’ll to the Friar to know his remedy.
passages.vernacular: 我去找神父知道佢嘅補救辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去找神父知道他的補救辦法。

passages.original: If all else fail, myself have power to die.
passages.vernacular: 如果別嘅都失敗,我自己有死嘅力量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果別的都失敗,我自己有死的力量。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene I — Friar Lawrence’s Cell 第四幕第一場:勞倫斯神父的修室

passages.original: Enter Friar Lawrence and Paris.
passages.vernacular: [勞倫斯神父同帕里斯上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [勞倫斯神父與帕里斯上。]

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: On Thursday, sir?
passages.vernacular: 星期四,先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期四,先生?

passages.original: The time is very short.
passages.vernacular: 時間好短。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 時間很短。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: My father Capulet will have it so; And I am nothing slow to slack his haste.
passages.vernacular: 我岳父凱普雷特要咁樣;我都啲不遲疑去減緩佢嘅急迫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我岳父凱普雷特要這樣;我也一點不遲疑去減緩他的急迫。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: You say you do not know the lady’s mind.
passages.vernacular: 你講你唔知道小姐嘅心意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說你不知道小姐的心意。

passages.original: Uneven is the course; I like it not.
passages.vernacular: 呢路不平坦;我不鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這路不平坦;我不喜歡。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: Immoderately she weeps for Tybalt’s death, And therefore have I little talk’d of love;
passages.vernacular: 佢為提伯特嘅死哭得過度,所以我好少跟佢談愛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她為提伯特的死哭得過度,所以我很少跟她談愛;

passages.original: For Venus smiles not in a house of tears.
passages.vernacular: 因為維納斯不喺淚水之家微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為維納斯不在淚水之家微笑。

passages.original: Now, sir, her father counts it dangerous That she do give her sorrow so much sway;
passages.vernacular: 而家,先生,佢父親認為佢讓悲傷佔咁大嘅支配係危險嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,先生,她父親認為她讓悲傷佔那麼大的支配是危險的;

passages.original: And in his wisdom, hastes our marriage, To stop the inundation of her tears, Which, too much minded by herself alone, May be put from her by society.
passages.vernacular: 佢憑智慧加快我哋嘅婚事,以阻止佢眼淚嘅氾濫,佢獨自過於思量,喺有人陪伴時或者能擺脫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他憑智慧加快我們的婚事,以阻止她眼淚的氾濫,她獨自過於思量,在有人陪伴時也許能擺脫。

passages.original: Now do you know the reason of this haste.
passages.vernacular: 而家你知道呢倉促嘅原因喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你知道這倉促的原因了。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: I would I knew not why it should be slow’d.— Look, sir, here comes the lady toward my cell.
passages.vernacular: 我但願唔知道點解要減緩。——睇,先生,小姐朝我嘅修室嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我但願不知道為什麼要減緩。——看,先生,小姐朝我的修室來了。

passages.original: Enter Juliet.
passages.vernacular: [茱麗葉上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茱麗葉上。]

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: Happily met, my lady and my wife!
passages.vernacular: 幸會,我嘅小姐,我嘅妻子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幸會,我的小姐,我的妻子!

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: That may be, sir, when I may be a wife.
passages.vernacular: 嗰可以係,先生,等我能做妻子嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那可以是,先生,等我能做妻子的時候。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: That may be, must be, love, on Thursday next.
passages.vernacular: 嗰可以係,必然係,愛人,下星期四。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那可以是,必然是,愛人,下星期四。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: What must be shall be.
passages.vernacular: 必然嘅就必然發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 必然的就必然發生。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: That’s a certain text.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個確定嘅經文。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個確定的經文。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: Come you to make confession to this father?
passages.vernacular: 你係嚟向呢位神父懺悔嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是來向這位神父懺悔的嗎?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: To answer that, I should confess to you.
passages.vernacular: 要回答呢個,我就該向您懺悔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要回答這個,我就該向您懺悔。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: Do not deny to him that you love me.
passages.vernacular: 別喺佢面前否認你愛我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別在他面前否認你愛我。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: I will confess to you that I love him.
passages.vernacular: 我會向您承認我愛佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會向您承認我愛他。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: So will ye, I am sure, that you love me.
passages.vernacular: 我確信你都會承認你愛我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確信你也會承認你愛我。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: If I do so, it will be of more price, Being spoke behind your back than to your face.
passages.vernacular: 如果我咁樣做,背住您講,比當面講更有分量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我這樣做,背著您說,比當面說更有分量。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: Poor soul, thy face is much abus’d with tears.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅人,你嘅臉被眼淚糟蹋得厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的人,你的臉被眼淚糟蹋得厲害。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: The tears have got small victory by that; For it was bad enough before their spite.
passages.vernacular: 眼淚冇因此獲多大勝利;因為喺佢哋為難之前就已夠糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 眼淚沒因此獲多大勝利;因為在它們為難之前就已夠糟。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: Thou wrong’st it more than tears with that report.
passages.vernacular: 你咁樣講,比眼淚更委屈佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這樣說,比眼淚更委屈它。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: That is no slander, sir, which is a truth, And what I spake, I spake it to my face.
passages.vernacular: 先生,呢唔係誹謗,因為係真話,我講嘅我係當面對自己嘅臉講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,這不是誹謗,因為是真話,我說的我是當面對自己的臉說的。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: Thy face is mine, and thou hast slander’d it.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅臉係我嘅,你卻誹謗咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的臉是我的,你卻誹謗了它。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: It may be so, for it is not mine own.
passages.vernacular: 或者如此,因為佢唔係我自己嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許如此,因為它不是我自己的。

passages.original: Are you at leisure, holy father, now, Or shall I come to you at evening mass?
passages.vernacular: 神聖嘅神父,您而家有空嗎,定係我晚禱彌撒時再嚟找您?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 神聖的神父,您現在有空嗎,還是我晚禱彌撒時再來找您?

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: My leisure serves me, pensive daughter, now.— My lord, we must entreat the time alone.
passages.vernacular: 我而家有空,憂思嘅女兒。——大人,我哋得請您讓我哋獨處一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在有空,憂思的女兒。——大人,我們得請您讓我們獨處一會兒。

passages.title: Paris 帕里斯
passages.original: God shield I should disturb devotion!— Juliet, on Thursday early will I rouse ye, Till then, adieu; and keep this holy kiss.
passages.vernacular: 上帝保佑我唔好打擾虔誠!——茱麗葉,星期四一早我嚟喚醒你,到嗰時,再會,留下呢神聖嘅一吻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上帝保佑我不要打擾虔誠!——茱麗葉,星期四一早我來喚醒你,到那時,再會,留下這神聖的一吻。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O shut the door, and when thou hast done so, Come weep with me, past hope, past cure, past help!
passages.vernacular: 啊,把門關上,關上之後,嚟同我一起哭,希望已盡,無藥可救,無從幫助!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,把門關上,關上之後,來和我一起哭,希望已盡,無藥可救,無從幫助!

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: O Juliet, I already know thy grief; It strains me past the compass of my wits.
passages.vernacular: 啊茱麗葉,我已知道你嘅悲傷;佢使我緊繃到超出我智慧嘅範圍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊茱麗葉,我已知道你的悲傷;它使我緊繃到超出我智慧的範圍。

passages.original: I hear thou must, and nothing may prorogue it, On Thursday next be married to this County.
passages.vernacular: 我聽講你必須,而且乜嘢都唔能夠延遲,下星期四同呢位伯爵結婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽說你必須,而且什麼也不能延遲,下星期四與這位伯爵結婚。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Tell me not, Friar, that thou hear’st of this, Unless thou tell me how I may prevent it.
passages.vernacular: 神父,別告訴我你聽到呢事,除非你告訴我點樣阻止佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 神父,別告訴我你聽到這事,除非你告訴我怎樣阻止它。

passages.original: If in thy wisdom, thou canst give no help, Do thou but call my resolution wise, And with this knife I’ll help it presently.
passages.vernacular: 如果你憑智慧無法幫忙,就只要稱我嘅決心係明智嘅,我即刻用呢把刀幫佢實現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你憑智慧無法幫忙,就只要稱我的決心是明智的,我立刻用這把刀幫它實現。

passages.original: God join’d my heart and Romeo’s, thou our hands;
passages.vernacular: 上帝連結咗我嘅心同羅密歐嘅,你連結咗我哋嘅手;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上帝連結了我的心和羅密歐的,你連結了我們的手;

passages.original: And ere this hand, by thee to Romeo’s seal’d, Shall be the label to another deed, Or my true heart with treacherous revolt Turn to another, this shall slay them both.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢隻被你蓋印畀羅密歐嘅手,成為另一份契約嘅標籤之前,或者我真誠嘅心帶住背叛嘅反叛轉向另一個之前,呢把刀會殺死佢哋兩個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這隻被你蓋印給羅密歐的手,成為另一份契約的標籤之前,或者我真誠的心帶著背叛的反叛轉向另一個之前,這把刀會殺死它們兩個。

passages.original: Therefore, out of thy long-experienc’d time, Give me some present counsel, or behold ’Twixt my extremes and me this bloody knife Shall play the empire, arbitrating that Which the commission of thy years and art Could to no issue of true honour bring.
passages.vernacular: 所以,憑你悠久嘅經驗,畀我啲當下嘅指點,否則睇邊,喺我嘅極端同我之間,呢把血腥嘅刀會當裁判,裁決你嘅年歲同技藝嘅委任無法帶嚟真正榮譽結果嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,憑你悠久的經驗,給我一些當下的指點,否則看哪,在我的極端與我之間,這把血腥的刀會當裁判,裁決你的年歲與技藝的委任無法帶來真正榮譽結果的事。

passages.original: Be not so long to speak.
passages.vernacular: 別拖咁久才講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別拖那麼久才說。

passages.original: I long to die, If what thou speak’st speak not of remedy.
passages.vernacular: 我渴望死,如果你講嘅唔係補救嘅辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我渴望死,如果你說的不是補救的辦法。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Hold, daughter.
passages.vernacular: 住手,女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 住手,女兒。

passages.original: I do spy a kind of hope, Which craves as desperate an execution As that is desperate which we would prevent.
passages.vernacular: 我睇到一種希望,佢要求嘅執行,同我哋要防止嘅事一樣絕望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看到一種希望,它要求的執行,和我們要防止的事一樣絕望。

passages.original: If, rather than to marry County Paris Thou hast the strength of will to slay thyself, Then is it likely thou wilt undertake A thing like death to chide away this shame, That cop’st with death himself to scape from it.
passages.vernacular: 如果你有意志力寧願自殺都不嫁帕里斯伯爵,咁你好可能會去做一件像死亡一樣嘅事,嚟驅走呢恥辱,你既然敢於面對死亡本身以逃避佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你有意志力寧願自殺也不嫁帕里斯伯爵,那麼你很可能會去做一件像死亡一樣的事,來驅走這恥辱,你既然敢於面對死亡本身以逃避它。

passages.original: And if thou dar’st, I’ll give thee remedy.
passages.vernacular: 如果你敢,我畀你補救嘅辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你敢,我給你補救的辦法。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: O, bid me leap, rather than marry Paris, From off the battlements of yonder tower, Or walk in thievish ways, or bid me lurk Where serpents are.
passages.vernacular: 啊,叫我跳,同其嫁畀帕里斯,從嗰邊塔樓嘅城垛上跳下去,或喺盜賊出冇嘅路上走,或叫我躲喺有蛇嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,叫我跳,與其嫁給帕里斯,從那邊塔樓的城垛上跳下去,或在盜賊出沒的路上走,或叫我躲在有蛇的地方。

passages.original: Chain me with roaring bears; Or hide me nightly in a charnel-house, O’er-cover’d quite with dead men’s rattling bones, With reeky shanks and yellow chapless skulls.
passages.vernacular: 用咆哮嘅熊把我鎖起嚟;或每夜把我藏喺停屍房裡,被死人嘎嘎響嘅骨頭完全蓋住,有惡臭嘅脛骨同黃色無下巴嘅頭骨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用咆哮的熊把我鎖起來;或每夜把我藏在停屍房裡,被死人嘎嘎響的骨頭完全蓋住,有惡臭的脛骨和黃色無下巴的頭骨。

passages.original: Or bid me go into a new-made grave, And hide me with a dead man in his shroud;
passages.vernacular: 或者叫我走進新造嘅墳墓,同一個穿壽衣嘅死人一起藏起嚟;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者叫我走進新造的墳墓,與一個穿壽衣的死人一起藏起來;

passages.original: Things that, to hear them told, have made me tremble, And I will do it without fear or doubt, To live an unstain’d wife to my sweet love.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲事聽人講起都令我發抖,我都會毫無恐懼同猶豫地去做,為了對我甜蜜嘅愛人作一個無玷嘅妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些事聽人說起都令我發抖,我也會毫無恐懼和猶豫地去做,為了對我甜蜜的愛人作一個無玷的妻子。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Hold then.
passages.vernacular: 咁,聽住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,聽著。

passages.original: Go home, be merry, give consent To marry Paris.
passages.vernacular: 回家去,高興些,同意嫁畀帕里斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回家去,高興些,同意嫁給帕里斯。

passages.original: Wednesday is tomorrow; Tomorrow night look that thou lie alone, Let not thy Nurse lie with thee in thy chamber.
passages.vernacular: 聽日係星期三;聽日夜裡,務必獨自瞓,唔好畀奶媽喺你房間裡陪你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明天是星期三;明天夜裡,務必獨自睡,別讓奶媽在你房間裡陪你。

passages.original: Take thou this vial, being then in bed, And this distilled liquor drink thou off, When presently through all thy veins shall run A cold and drowsy humour;
passages.vernacular: 臨瞓時攞呢小瓶,把呢蒸餾嘅藥水飲光,一會兒就會有一種冰冷昏沉嘅體液流過你所有血管;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 臨睡時拿這小瓶,把這蒸餾的藥水喝光,一會兒就會有一種冰冷昏沉的體液流過你所有血管;

passages.original: for no pulse Shall keep his native progress, but surcease.
passages.vernacular: 脈搏都唔會保持佢嘅自然進程,而係停止。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 脈搏都不會保持它的自然進程,而是停止。

passages.original: No warmth, no breath shall testify thou livest, The roses in thy lips and cheeks shall fade To paly ashes;
passages.vernacular: 冇暖,冇氣息證明你活住,你嘴唇同臉頰上嘅玫瑰會褪成蒼白嘅灰;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有暖,沒有氣息證明你活著,你嘴唇和臉頰上的玫瑰會褪成蒼白的灰;

passages.original: thy eyes’ windows fall, Like death when he shuts up the day of life.
passages.vernacular: 你眼睛嘅窗子會閉上,像死亡關閉生命之日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你眼睛的窗子會閉上,像死亡關閉生命之日。

passages.original: Each part depriv’d of supple government, Shall stiff and stark and cold appear like death.
passages.vernacular: 每個部分失去柔軟嘅控制,會僵硬、直挺、冰冷,睇似死亡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個部分失去柔軟的控制,會僵硬、直挺、冰冷,看似死亡。

passages.original: And in this borrow’d likeness of shrunk death Thou shalt continue two and forty hours, And then awake as from a pleasant sleep.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢借嚟嘅萎縮死亡嘅樣子中,你將持續四十二小時,然後像從愉快嘅瞓眠中醒嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這借來的萎縮死亡的樣子中,你將持續四十二小時,然後像從愉快的睡眠中醒來。

passages.original: Now when the bridegroom in the morning comes To rouse thee from thy bed, there art thou dead.
passages.vernacular: 而家,當新郎早晨嚟把你從床上叫起,你就死喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,當新郎早晨來把你從床上叫起,你就死在那裡。

passages.original: Then as the manner of our country is, In thy best robes, uncover’d, on the bier, Thou shalt be borne to that same ancient vault Where all the kindred of the Capulets lie.
passages.vernacular: 然後按我哋國家嘅習俗,穿住你最好嘅衣袍,不蓋面,躺喺靈床上,你會被抬到嗰座古老嘅墓穴,凱普雷特家所有親屬長眠之處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後按我們國家的習俗,穿著你最好的衣袍,不蓋面,躺在靈床上,你會被抬到那座古老的墓穴,凱普雷特家所有親屬長眠之處。

passages.original: In the meantime, against thou shalt awake, Shall Romeo by my letters know our drift, And hither shall he come, and he and I Will watch thy waking, and that very night Shall Romeo bear thee hence to Mantua.
passages.vernacular: 喺此期間,為了你醒嚟嘅時候,羅密歐會通過我嘅信知道我哋嘅計劃,佢會嚟呢度,佢同我將守候你醒嚟,就喺嗰一夜羅密歐將帶你去曼圖亞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在此期間,為了你醒來的時候,羅密歐會通過我的信知道我們的計劃,他會來這裡,他和我將守候你醒來,就在那一夜羅密歐將帶你去曼圖亞。

passages.original: And this shall free thee from this present shame, If no inconstant toy nor womanish fear Abate thy valour in the acting it.
passages.vernacular: 呢將使你擺脫眼前嘅羞辱,只要冇反覆嘅念頭或女人嘅恐懼,削弱你執行時嘅勇氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這將使你擺脫眼前的羞辱,只要沒有反覆的念頭或女人的恐懼,削弱你執行時的勇氣。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Give me, give me!
passages.vernacular: 畀我,畀我!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我,給我!

passages.original: O tell not me of fear!
passages.vernacular: 啊,別對我講害怕!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,別對我說害怕!

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: Hold; get you gone, be strong and prosperous In this resolve.
passages.vernacular: 攞住;走吧,喺呢決心中堅強並順利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿著;走吧,在這決心中堅強並順利。

passages.original: I’ll send a friar with speed To Mantua, with my letters to thy lord.
passages.vernacular: 我會火速派一位修士去曼圖亞,帶我嘅信畀你嘅夫君。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會火速派一位修士去曼圖亞,帶我的信給你的夫君。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Love give me strength, and strength shall help afford.
passages.vernacular: 愛畀我力量,力量將提供幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛給我力量,力量將提供幫助。

passages.original: Farewell, dear father.
passages.vernacular: 再會,親愛嘅神父。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會,親愛的神父。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene II — Hall in Capulet’s House 第四幕第二場:凱普雷特家大廳

passages.original: Enter Capulet, Lady Capulet, Nurse and Servants.
passages.vernacular: [凱普雷特、凱普雷特夫人、奶媽同僕人哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱普雷特、凱普雷特夫人、奶媽與僕人們上。]

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: So many guests invite as here are writ.
passages.vernacular: 照呢上面寫嘅名單邀請咁多客人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 照這上面寫的名單邀請這麼多客人。

passages.original: [Exit first Servant.]
passages.vernacular: [第一僕人下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [第一僕人下。]

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Sirrah, go hire me twenty cunning cooks.
passages.vernacular: 小子,去替我雇二十個巧手嘅廚師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小子,去替我雇二十個巧手的廚師。

passages.title: Second Servant 第二僕人
passages.original: You shall have none ill, sir; for I’ll try if they can lick their fingers.
passages.vernacular: 您唔會雇到壞嘅,先生;因為我要試試佢哋會唔會舔手指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不會雇到壞的,先生;因為我要試試他們會不會舔手指。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: How canst thou try them so?
passages.vernacular: 你點試佢哋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼試他們?

passages.title: Second Servant 第二僕人
passages.original: Marry, sir, ’tis an ill cook that cannot lick his own fingers;
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,先生,唔會舔自己手指嘅係壞廚師;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,先生,不會舔自己手指的是壞廚師;

passages.original: therefore he that cannot lick his fingers goes not with me.
passages.vernacular: 所以唔會舔手指嘅,就不跟我走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以不會舔手指的,就不跟我走。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Go, begone.
passages.vernacular: 去,走吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,走吧。

passages.original: [Exit second Servant.]
passages.vernacular: [第二僕人下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [第二僕人下。]

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: We shall be much unfurnish’d for this time.
passages.vernacular: 呢次我哋會準備不足。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次我們會準備不足。

passages.original: What, is my daughter gone to Friar Lawrence?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,我女兒去勞倫斯神父嗰度咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,我女兒去勞倫斯神父那裡了嗎?

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: Ay, forsooth.
passages.vernacular: 係,真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,真的。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Well, he may chance to do some good on her.
passages.vernacular: 好,佢或者能對佢有點好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,他也許能對她有點好處。

passages.original: A peevish self-will’d harlotry it is.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個乖戾任性嘅小賤人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是個乖戾任性的小賤人。

passages.original: Enter Juliet.
passages.vernacular: [茱麗葉上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茱麗葉上。]

passages.title: Nurse 奶媽
passages.original: See where she comes from shrift with merry look.
passages.vernacular: 睇,佢懺悔回嚟喇,帶住快樂嘅神情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,她懺悔回來了,帶著快樂的神情。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: How now, my headstrong.
passages.vernacular: 點喇,我嘅倔強丫頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,我的倔強丫頭。

passages.original: Where have you been gadding?
passages.vernacular: 你到邊度閒逛去喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你到哪裡閒逛去了?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Where I have learnt me to repent the sin Of disobedient opposition To you and your behests;
passages.vernacular: 到我學會為對您同您嘅命令違抗反對嘅罪而悔改嘅地方;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到我學會為對您和您的命令違抗反對的罪而悔改的地方;

passages.original: and am enjoin’d By holy Lawrence to fall prostrate here, To beg your pardon.
passages.vernacular: 並被神聖嘅勞倫斯責令喺呢度俯伏,求您原諒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並被神聖的勞倫斯責令在這裡俯伏,求您原諒。

passages.original: Pardon, I beseech you.
passages.vernacular: 原諒,我懇求您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 原諒,我懇求您。

passages.original: Henceforward I am ever rul’d by you.
passages.vernacular: 從今以後我永遠聽您嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從今以後我永遠聽您的。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Send for the County, go tell him of this.
passages.vernacular: 派人去請伯爵,去告訴佢呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 派人去請伯爵,去告訴他這件事。

passages.original: I’ll have this knot knit up tomorrow morning.
passages.vernacular: 我要把呢個結聽日早晨就打好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把這個結明天早晨就打好。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: I met the youthful lord at Lawrence’ cell, And gave him what becomed love I might, Not stepping o’er the bounds of modesty.
passages.vernacular: 我喺勞倫斯嘅修室遇見嗰位年輕貴人,畀咗佢我所能畀嘅得體嘅愛,冇越過羞澀嘅界限。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在勞倫斯的修室遇見那位年輕貴人,給了他我所能給的得體的愛,沒有越過羞澀的界限。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Why, I am glad on’t.
passages.vernacular: 哎,我高興聽到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,我高興聽到。

passages.original: This is well. Stand up.
passages.vernacular: 呢個好好。起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這很好。起來。

passages.original: This is as’t should be.
passages.vernacular: 呢才係應該嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這才是應該的。

passages.original: Let me see the County. Ay, marry.
passages.vernacular: 讓我見伯爵。對,講真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我見伯爵。對,說真的。

passages.original: Go, I say, and fetch him hither.
passages.vernacular: 去,我講,把佢請到呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,我說,把他請到這裡。

passages.original: Now afore God, this reverend holy Friar, All our whole city is much bound to him.
passages.vernacular: 而家憑上帝,呢位可敬嘅神聖修士,我哋全城都深受佢嘅恩惠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在憑上帝,這位可敬的神聖修士,我們全城都深受他的恩惠。

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Nurse, will you go with me into my closet, To help me sort such needful ornaments As you think fit to furnish me tomorrow?
passages.vernacular: 奶媽,你願意跟我到小室,幫我挑出你認為聽日適合畀我備用嘅必要裝飾嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奶媽,你願意跟我到小室,幫我挑出你認為明天適合給我備用的必要裝飾嗎?

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: No, not till Thursday.
passages.vernacular: 不,星期四以前唔使。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,星期四以前不用。

passages.original: There is time enough.
passages.vernacular: 時間足夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 時間足夠。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Go, Nurse, go with her.
passages.vernacular: 去,奶媽,跟佢去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,奶媽,跟她去。

passages.original: We’ll to church tomorrow.
passages.vernacular: 我哋聽日去教堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們明天去教堂。

passages.original: [Exeunt Juliet and Nurse.]
passages.vernacular: [茱麗葉同奶媽下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茱麗葉與奶媽下。]

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: We shall be short in our provision, ’Tis now near night.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅準備會不足,而家快天黑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的準備會不足,現在快天黑了。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: Tush, I will stir about, And all things shall be well, I warrant thee, wife.
passages.vernacular: 嘖,我去張羅,一切都會好嘅,我向你保證,妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘖,我去張羅,一切都會好的,我向你保證,妻子。

passages.original: Go thou to Juliet, help to deck up her.
passages.vernacular: 你去茱麗葉嗰度,幫忙裝扮佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你去茱麗葉那裡,幫忙裝扮她。

passages.original: I’ll not to bed tonight, let me alone.
passages.vernacular: 今晚我不上床,別管我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晚我不上床,別管我。

passages.original: I’ll play the housewife for this once.—What, ho!— They are all forth:
passages.vernacular: 呢一次我嚟當家庭主婦。——喂!——佢哋都出去喇:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一次我來當家庭主婦。——喂!——他們都出去了:

passages.original: well, I will walk myself To County Paris, to prepare him up Against tomorrow.
passages.vernacular: 好,我自己走去帕里斯伯爵嗰度,讓佢為聽日準備好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,我自己走去帕里斯伯爵那裡,讓他為明天準備好。

passages.original: My heart is wondrous light Since this same wayward girl is so reclaim’d.
passages.vernacular: 自從呢個任性嘅女孩咁樣被挽回,我嘅心異常輕鬆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從這個任性的女孩這樣被挽回,我的心異常輕鬆。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene III — Juliet’s Chamber 第四幕第三場:茱麗葉的閨房

passages.original: Enter Juliet and Nurse.
passages.vernacular: [茱麗葉同奶媽上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [茱麗葉與奶媽上。]

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: Ay, those attires are best.
passages.vernacular: 對,嗰啲衣裳最好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,那些衣裳最好。

passages.original: But, gentle Nurse, I pray thee leave me to myself tonight;
passages.vernacular: 不過,好奶媽,求你今晚讓我一個人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,好奶媽,求你今晚讓我一個人;

passages.original: For I have need of many orisons To move the heavens to smile upon my state, Which, well thou know’st, is cross and full of sin.
passages.vernacular: 因為我需要許多禱告,嚟感動上天對我嘅處境微笑,你好清楚,我嘅處境乖舛而罪孽深重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我需要許多禱告,來感動上天對我的處境微笑,你很清楚,我的處境乖舛而罪孽深重。

passages.original: Enter Lady Capulet.
passages.vernacular: [凱普雷特夫人上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱普雷特夫人上。]

passages.title: Lady Capulet 凱普雷特夫人
passages.original: What, are you busy, ho?
passages.vernacular: 點,你哋忙嗎,喂?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,你們忙嗎,喂?

passages.original: Need you my help?
passages.vernacular: 你需要我幫忙嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你需要我幫忙嗎?

passages.title: Juliet 茱麗葉
passages.original: No, madam; we have cull’d such necessaries As are behoveful for our state tomorrow.
passages.vernacular: 唔使,夫人;我哋已挑好咗聽日所需嘅必要之物。
