passages.original: What manners is in this, To press before thy father to a grave?
passages.vernacular: 呢算乜嘢禮貌,搶喺你父親前面走向墳墓?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這算什麼禮貌,搶在你父親前面走向墳墓?

passages.title: Prince 親王
passages.original: Seal up the mouth of outrage for a while, Till we can clear these ambiguities, And know their spring, their head, their true descent, And then will I be general of your woes, And lead you even to death.
passages.vernacular: 暫時封住憤怒嘅口,直到我哋能澄清呢啲疑點,知道佢哋嘅根源、源頭、真正嘅出處,然後我會作你哋悲傷嘅統帥,引領你哋甚至到死亡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 暫時封住憤怒的口,直到我們能澄清這些疑點,知道它們的根源、源頭、真正的出處,然後我會作你們悲傷的統帥,引領你們甚至到死亡。

passages.original: Meantime forbear, And let mischance be slave to patience.
passages.vernacular: 同時要忍耐,讓不幸成為耐心嘅奴隸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時要忍耐,讓不幸成為耐心的奴隸。

passages.original: Bring forth the parties of suspicion.
passages.vernacular: 把嫌疑人帶上嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把嫌疑人帶上來。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: I am the greatest, able to do least, Yet most suspected, as the time and place Doth make against me, of this direful murder.
passages.vernacular: 我係最大嘅嫌疑人,能力最小,卻最被懷疑,因時間同地點都對我不利,涉及呢場可怕嘅謀殺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是最大的嫌疑人,能力最小,卻最被懷疑,因時間和地點都對我不利,涉及這場可怕的謀殺。

passages.original: And here I stand, both to impeach and purge Myself condemned and myself excus’d.
passages.vernacular: 我站喺呢度,既控告又澄清自己,自己被判有罪,又為自己辯解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我站在這裡,既控告又澄清自己,自己被判有罪,又為自己辯解。

passages.title: Prince 親王
passages.original: Then say at once what thou dost know in this.
passages.vernacular: 咁即刻講你喺呢件事上知道嘅一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼立刻說你在這件事上知道的一切。

passages.title: Friar Lawrence 勞倫斯神父
passages.original: I will be brief, for my short date of breath Is not so long as is a tedious tale.
passages.vernacular: 我會簡短,因為我氣息嘅短暫期限,不如一個冗長嘅故事長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會簡短,因為我氣息的短暫期限,不如一個冗長的故事長。

passages.original: Romeo, there dead, was husband to that Juliet, And she, there dead, that Romeo’s faithful wife.
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐,死喺嗰度嘅,係嗰位茱麗葉嘅丈夫,佢,死喺嗰度嘅,係羅密歐忠實嘅妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐,死在那裡的,是那位茱麗葉的丈夫,她,死在那裡的,是羅密歐忠實的妻子。

passages.original: I married them; and their stol’n marriage day Was Tybalt’s doomsday, whose untimely death Banish’d the new-made bridegroom from this city;
passages.vernacular: 我為佢哋證婚;佢哋偷偷結婚嘅日子,係提伯特嘅末日,佢嘅早死把新婚嘅新郎從呢城放逐;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為他們證婚;他們偷偷結婚的日子,是提伯特的末日,他的早死把新婚的新郎從這城放逐;

passages.original: For whom, and not for Tybalt, Juliet pin’d.
passages.vernacular: 為了佢,而唔係為了提伯特,茱麗葉憔悴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了他,而不是為了提伯特,茱麗葉憔悴。

passages.original: You, to remove that siege of grief from her, Betroth’d, and would have married her perforce To County Paris.
passages.vernacular: 你哋為了除去佢嗰圍城般嘅悲傷,把佢許配,打算強迫佢嫁畀帕里斯伯爵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們為了除去她那圍城般的悲傷,把她許配,打算強迫她嫁給帕里斯伯爵。

passages.original: Then comes she to me, And with wild looks, bid me devise some means To rid her from this second marriage, Or in my cell there would she kill herself.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢嚟找我,帶住狂亂嘅神情,叫我想辦法使佢擺脫呢第二次婚姻,否則佢就要喺我修室裡自殺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她來找我,帶著狂亂的神情,叫我想辦法使她擺脫這第二次婚姻,否則她就要在我修室裡自殺。

passages.original: Then gave I her, so tutored by my art, A sleeping potion, which so took effect As I intended, for it wrought on her The form of death.
passages.vernacular: 於是我憑我嘅技藝指點,畀咗佢一種瞓眠藥水,佢起咗我所預期嘅作用,使佢呈現死亡嘅形態。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是我憑我的技藝指點,給了她一種睡眠藥水,它起了我所預期的作用,使她呈現死亡的形態。

passages.original: Meantime I writ to Romeo That he should hither come as this dire night To help to take her from her borrow’d grave, Being the time the potion’s force should cease.
passages.vernacular: 同時我寫信畀羅密歐,叫佢喺呢個可怕嘅夜裡嚟呢度,幫助把佢從借嚟嘅墳墓裡救出,嗰時正是藥力將消嘅時刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時我寫信給羅密歐,叫他在這可怕的夜裡來這裡,幫助把她從借來的墳墓裡救出,那時正是藥力將消的時刻。

passages.original: But he which bore my letter, Friar John, Was stay’d by accident;
passages.vernacular: 但帶我信嘅人,約翰神父,被意外耽擱喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但帶我信的人,約翰神父,被意外耽擱了;

passages.original: and yesternight Return’d my letter back.
passages.vernacular: 昨夜把我嘅信退咗回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨夜把我的信退了回來。

passages.original: Then all alone At the prefixed hour of her waking Came I to take her from her kindred’s vault, Meaning to keep her closely at my cell Till I conveniently could send to Romeo.
passages.vernacular: 於是我獨自在佢預定醒嚟嘅時刻,嚟把佢從佢家族嘅墓穴裡帶出,打算把佢秘密留喺我嘅修室,直到我方便時可以送信畀羅密歐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是我獨自在她預定醒來的時刻,來把她從她家族的墓穴裡帶出,打算把她秘密留在我的修室,直到我方便時可以送信給羅密歐。

passages.original: But when I came, some minute ere the time Of her awaking, here untimely lay The noble Paris and true Romeo dead.
passages.vernacular: 但當我到來時,喺佢醒嚟前嘅一分鐘左右,高貴嘅帕里斯同真誠嘅羅密歐不合時宜地死喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但當我到來時,在她醒來前的一分鐘左右,高貴的帕里斯和真誠的羅密歐不合時宜地死在這裡。

passages.original: She wakes; and I entreated her come forth And bear this work of heaven with patience.
passages.vernacular: 佢醒嚟;我懇求佢出嚟,耐心承受呢上天嘅作為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她醒來;我懇求她出來,耐心承受這上天的作為。

passages.original: But then a noise did scare me from the tomb; And she, too desperate, would not go with me, But, as it seems, did violence on herself.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰時一陣聲響把我從墓穴嚇走;佢太絕望,唔肯隨我走,而係,睇來,對自己施咗暴力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那時一陣聲響把我從墓穴嚇走;她太絕望,不肯隨我走,而是,看來,對自己施了暴力。

passages.original: All this I know; and to the marriage Her Nurse is privy.
passages.vernacular: 呢一切我都知道;至於婚事,佢嘅奶媽知情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一切我都知道;至於婚事,她的奶媽知情。

passages.original: And if ought in this Miscarried by my fault, let my old life Be sacrific’d, some hour before his time, Unto the rigour of severest law.
passages.vernacular: 如果呢中間有乜嘢因我嘅過失而出錯,就讓我呢條老命,喺佢嘅時辰之前一小時,獻祭畀最嚴厲嘅法律。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果這中間有什麼因我的過失而出錯,就讓我這條老命,在他的時辰之前一小時,獻祭給最嚴厲的法律。

passages.title: Prince 親王
passages.original: We still have known thee for a holy man.
passages.vernacular: 我哋一向知道你係個神聖嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們一向知道你是個神聖的人。

passages.original: Where’s Romeo’s man?
passages.vernacular: 羅密歐嘅僕人喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅密歐的僕人在哪裡?

passages.original: What can he say to this?
passages.vernacular: 佢對此有乜嘢可講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對此有什麼可說?

passages.title: Balthasar 巴爾薩澤
passages.original: I brought my master news of Juliet’s death, And then in post he came from Mantua To this same place, to this same monument.
passages.vernacular: 我把茱麗葉嘅死訊帶畀我主人,然後佢飛馬從曼圖亞嚟到呢同一個地方,呢同一座墓穴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把茱麗葉的死訊帶給我主人,然後他飛馬從曼圖亞來到這同一個地方,這同一座墓穴。

passages.original: This letter he early bid me give his father, And threaten’d me with death, going in the vault, If I departed not, and left him there.
passages.vernacular: 呢封信佢叫我一早交畀佢父親,並喺進入墓穴時威脅講,如果我不離開、不把佢留喺嗰度,就要殺我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這封信他叫我一早交給他父親,並在進入墓穴時威脅說,如果我不離開、不把他留在那裡,就要殺我。

passages.title: Prince 親王
passages.original: Give me the letter, I will look on it.
passages.vernacular: 把信畀我,我嚟睇睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把信給我,我來看看。

passages.original: Where is the County’s Page that rais’d the watch?
passages.vernacular: 叫嚟守夜人嘅伯爵侍童喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫來守夜人的伯爵侍童在哪裡?

passages.original: Sirrah, what made your master in this place?
passages.vernacular: 小子,你主人喺呢地方做乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小子,你主人在這地方做什麼?

passages.title: Page 侍童
passages.original: He came with flowers to strew his lady’s grave, And bid me stand aloof, and so I did.
passages.vernacular: 佢攞住花嚟撒喺佢愛人嘅墳上,叫我站遠,我就咁樣做喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拿著花來撒在他愛人的墳上,叫我站遠,我就這樣做了。

passages.original: Anon comes one with light to ope the tomb, And by and by my master drew on him, And then I ran away to call the watch.
passages.vernacular: 不久有人攞住燈嚟開墓,接住我主人拔劍攻佢,然後我就跑去叫守夜人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久有人拿著燈來開墓,接著我主人拔劍攻他,然後我就跑去叫守夜人。

passages.title: Prince 親王
passages.original: This letter doth make good the Friar’s words, Their course of love, the tidings of her death.
passages.vernacular: 呢封信證實咗修士嘅話,佢哋嘅愛情經歷,佢死去嘅消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這封信證實了修士的話,他們的愛情經歷,她死去的消息。

passages.original: And here he writes that he did buy a poison Of a poor ’pothecary, and therewithal Came to this vault to die, and lie with Juliet.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺呢度寫道,佢向一位窮藥劑師買咗毒藥,隨即嚟到呢墓穴,要死並同茱麗葉同眠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在這裡寫道,他向一位窮藥劑師買了毒藥,隨即來到這墓穴,要死並與茱麗葉同眠。

passages.original: Where be these enemies?
passages.vernacular: 呢啲仇敵喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些仇敵在哪裡?

passages.original: Capulet, Montague, See what a scourge is laid upon your hate, That heaven finds means to kill your joys with love!
passages.vernacular: 凱普雷特,蒙太古,睇你哋嘅恨被加上咗點樣嘅鞭子,上天找到辦法用愛殺死你哋嘅歡樂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱普雷特,蒙太古,看你們的恨被加上了怎樣的鞭子,上天找到辦法用愛殺死你們的歡樂!

passages.original: And I, for winking at your discords too, Have lost a brace of kinsmen.
passages.vernacular: 而我,因為對你哋嘅不同睜一隻眼閉一隻眼,都失去咗一對親戚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我,因為對你們的不和睜一隻眼閉一隻眼,也失去了一對親戚。

passages.original: All are punish’d.
passages.vernacular: 大家都受到咗懲罰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家都受到了懲罰。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: O brother Montague, give me thy hand.
passages.vernacular: 啊蒙太古兄弟,把你嘅手畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊蒙太古兄弟,把你的手給我。

passages.original: This is my daughter’s jointure, for no more Can I demand.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我女兒嘅聘禮,我再唔能夠要求更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我女兒的聘禮,我再不能要求更多。

passages.title: Montague 蒙太古
passages.original: But I can give thee more, For I will raise her statue in pure gold, That whiles Verona by that name is known, There shall no figure at such rate be set As that of true and faithful Juliet.
passages.vernacular: 但我可以畀你更多,因為我要用純金為佢鑄一座像,只要維洛嗰仲以嗰個名字為人所知,就唔會有任何塑像被咁樣高價設立,像真誠忠實嘅茱麗葉嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我可以給你更多,因為我要用純金為她鑄一座像,只要維洛那還以那個名字為人所知,就不會有任何塑像被這樣高價設立,像真誠忠實的茱麗葉那樣。

passages.title: Capulet 凱普雷特
passages.original: As rich shall Romeo’s by his lady’s lie, Poor sacrifices of our enmity.
passages.vernacular: 同樣富麗地,羅密歐嘅像將立喺佢愛人旁邊,係我哋仇恨可憐嘅祭品。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同樣富麗地,羅密歐的像將立在他愛人旁邊,是我們仇恨可憐的祭品。

passages.title: Prince 親王
passages.original: A glooming peace this morning with it brings;
passages.vernacular: 今晨帶嚟一個陰沉嘅和平;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晨帶來一個陰沉的和平;

passages.original: The sun for sorrow will not show his head.
passages.vernacular: 太陽因悲傷唔肯露面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太陽因悲傷不肯露面。

passages.original: Go hence, to have more talk of these sad things.
passages.vernacular: 離開呢度,去更多談談呢啲悲傷嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 離開這裡,去更多談談這些悲傷的事。

passages.original: Some shall be pardon’d, and some punished, For never was a story of more woe Than this of Juliet and her Romeo.
passages.vernacular: 有些人將被赦免,有些人將受懲罰,因為再冇比茱麗葉同佢嘅羅密歐更悲哀嘅故事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人將被赦免,有些人將受懲罰,因為再沒有比茱麗葉和她的羅密歐更悲哀的故事了。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]
